items.stem: During a dynamic acceptance trial, an automated rail inspection trolley moves along a straight viaduct rail, taking eastward as positive. Using the velocity–time graph recorded from t = 0.0 s to t = 10.0 s, determine the total distance travelled.
items.workedSolution: Velocity crosses zero at t = 7 s. Forward area (0 to 7 s) = ½(2)(8) + (3)(8) + ½(2)(8) = 40.0 m. Reverse area magnitude (7 s to 10 s) = ½(1)(4) + (2)(4) = 10.0 m. Total distance = 40.0 + 10.0 = 50.0 m.

markScheme.criterion: Sums unsigned positive (40.0 m) and negative (10.0 m) velocity–time areas to obtain 50.0 m (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Integrates only up to the zero-velocity instant and omits the distance travelled after reversing direction.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts the area below the time axis from the positive area, giving net signed displacement rather than total distance.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies peak forward velocity by the entire duration without accounting for ramps or direction reversal.

items.stem: At t = 0.0 s, an inter-terminal airport monorail rests at a position 15.0 m ahead of a concourse datum post. The velocity–time graph shows its forward motion over 10.0 s, with uniform braking applied from t = 7.0 s until t = 10.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Trapezium area Δx = ½(10 + 5)(12) = 90.0 m. (b) Final distance from datum = 15 + 90.0 = 105 m. (c) Mean speed = 90.0 / 10 = 9.00 m s⁻¹. (d) Braking acceleration = (0 − 12) / (10 − 7) = -4.00 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Identifies distance travelled as the area under the v–t trapezium.
Obtains Δx = 90.0 m.
Adds 15 m offset to obtain 105 m.
Divides distance travelled from (a) by 10 s.
Obtains mean speed = 9.00 m s⁻¹.
Obtains braking acceleration = -4.00 m s⁻².

parts.prompt: Calculate the distance travelled during the 10.0 s journey.
workingSteps: Distance equals the trapezium area under the v–t curve.

parts.prompt: Hence state its final distance from the concourse datum post at t = 10.0 s.
Determine the mean speed over the 10.0 s run.
Calculate the acceleration between t = 7.0 s and t = 10.0 s.

items.stem: The displacement–time graph shows an ultrasonic rangefinder target cart moving on an air track from t = 0.0 s to t = 12.0 s. What is its velocity during the initial stage from t = 0.0 s to t = 4.0 s?
items.workedSolution: At t = 0.0 s, s₀ = 6 m; at t = 4 s, s₁ = 26 m. Velocity v = Δs / Δt = (26 − 6) / 4 = 5.00 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts initial position s₀ = 6 m to obtain v = (26 − 6) / 4 = 5.00 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: At t = 0.0 s, a mine hoist cage is already moving upward at 5.0 m s⁻¹. Its signed acceleration over the next 8.0 s (upward positive) is plotted. What maximum speed does it reach during the 8.0 s interval?
items.workedSolution: Speed increases while a > 0 (from t = 0.0 s until a = 0 at t = 4 s). Positive area Δv_max = (2)(6) + ½(2)(6) = 18.0 m s⁻¹. Maximum speed = u₀ + Δv_max = 5 + 18.0 = 23.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Integrates positive acceleration up to t = 4 s (18.0 m s⁻¹) and adds 5 m s⁻¹ to get 23.0 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: Along a horizontal guideway, an air-track glider of mass 0.5 kg moves in a fixed direction. Its momentum–time graph shows an impulse stage from t = 2.0 s to t = 6.0 s.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies resultant force as gradient Δp / Δt of the p–t graph.
Obtains F = 0.750 N.
Relates net work to ΔE_k = (p₂² − p₁²) / (2m).
Substitutes p₁ = 1.5 kg m s⁻¹, p₂ = 4.5 kg m s⁻¹, and m = 0.5 kg.
Obtains W = 18.0 J.

items.stem: Having initial forward momentum 6.0 kg m s⁻¹, a cold-gas attitude probe of mass 2.0 kg experiences a collinear cold-gas thruster burn over 0.8 s as shown on the force–time graph. What is its change in speed Δv?
items.workedSolution: Impulse J = area under F–t trapezium = ½(0.8 + 0.4)(40) = 24.0 N s. Speed increase Δv = J / m = 24.0 / 2 = 12.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Computes J = 24.0 N s and Δv = J / 2 = 12.0 m s⁻¹ (A).

options.distractorRationale: Evaluates the impulse ∫F dt in N s without dividing by the mass m to find Δv.

items.stem: Passing x = 0.0 m with speed 3.0 m s⁻¹, an instrumented crash-test carriage of mass 2.0 kg experiences the collinear resultant force plotted against displacement up to x = 10.0 m. What is its speed at x = 10.0 m?
items.workedSolution: Positive work (0 to 8 m) = ½(8 + 4)(12) = 72.0 J. Resistive work (8 m to 10 m) = −½(2)(4) = −4.00 J. Net work W = 68.0 J. From ½mv² = ½mu₀² + W, v = √(3² + 2 × 68.0 / 2) = 8.77 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Finds net work W = 68.0 J and v = √(3² + 2W/2) = 8.77 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: Using a shielded NaI scintillation counter, background-corrected count rates C from a medical technetium eluted phantom are measured over 40.0 s and linearized by plotting ln(C / s⁻¹) against time t.
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical intercept at t = 0 is ln(C₀ / s⁻¹) = 8.00. (b) Gradient = (3 − 8) / 40 = -0.125 s⁻¹ (which equals −λ).

markScheme.criterion: Reads vertical intercept = 8.00.
Uses large triangle (3 − 8) / 40.
Includes negative sign and unit s⁻¹.
Obtains gradient = -0.125 s⁻¹.

items.stem: Within its Hookean limit, a helical steel launcher spring produces the force–extension graph shown up to an extension of 0.4 m. How much elastic potential energy is stored at x = 0.4 m?
items.workedSolution: Elastic potential energy equals the triangular area under the F–x line: E_p = ½ F x = ½(32)(0.4) = 6.40 J.

markScheme.criterion: Computes triangular area ½(32)(0.4) = 6.40 J (B).

items.stem: In a tensile materials test, a high-density polyethylene filament obeys Hooke's law up to a strain of 0.2 before softening up to strain 0.4, as shown on the stress–strain graph. What is the Young's modulus of the material in the initial linear region?
items.workedSolution: Up to the limit of proportionality at ε = 0.2, stress reaches 120 MPa. Young's modulus E = σ / ε = 120 / 0.2 = 600 MPa.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates initial linear gradient E = 120 / 0.2 = 600 MPa (B).

items.stem: In a circuits practical, a student records the potential difference V across a tungsten filament indicator lamp as the current I is increased from 0.0 A to 1.2 A, obtaining the non-linear characteristic shown.
items.workedSolution: (a) At I = 1.2 A, V = 8.40 V. (b) Static resistance R = V / I = 8.4 / 1.2 = 7.00 Ω (the upper segment gradient 12.0 Ω is ΔV / ΔI, not R).

markScheme.criterion: Reads V = 8.40 V at I = 1.2 A.
Selects R = V / I rather than local segment gradient ΔV / ΔI.
Substitutes V = 8.4 V and I = 1.2 A.
Obtains R = 7.00 Ω.

items.stem: A variable load resistor is connected across a lithium-iron-phosphate storage cell, and the terminal potential difference V is plotted against current I up to 2.0 A. According to V = ε − Ir, what is the signed gradient of this graph?
items.workedSolution: At I = 0.0 A, V = ε = 6 V; at I = 2 A, V = 2.4 V. Gradient = (2.4 − 6) / 2 = -1.80 V A⁻¹ (equal to −r).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates (2.4 − 6) / 2 = -1.80 V A⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: To determine the resistivity ρ of a conductive carbon-polymer rod despite probe and lead resistance R₀, a student plots total measured resistance R against the ratio L / A from 0.0 m⁻¹ to 400.0 m⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical intercept R₀ = 4.00 Ω. (b) Resistivity ρ = (24 − 4) / 400 = 0.0500 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: States R₀ = 4.00 Ω.
Identifies ρ with the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A).
Subtracts R₀ = 4 Ω from 24 Ω before dividing by 400 m⁻¹.
Obtains ρ = 0.0500 Ω m.

items.stem: Using two light gates in a gravitational field g = 9.8 m s⁻², a student records speed v of a card-carrying glider on an inclined linear air track (inclination sin θ = 0.25) after passing an initial gate at s = 0.0 m with speed u₀ > 0, plotting v² against distance s up to 2.0 m. According to v² = u₀² + 2as, what is the gradient Δ(v²) / Δs of the line?
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 2 m² s⁻² and at s = 2 m, v² = 11.8 m² s⁻². Gradient = (11.8 − 2) / 2 = 2(9.8)(0.25) = 4.90 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 2 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.8 × 0.25) to get 4.90 m s⁻² (B).

options.distractorRationale: Inverts Δs / Δ(v²) instead of computing Δ(v²) / Δs.

options.label: C

items.stem: To test Coulomb's inverse-square law using two conducting pith spheres on a digital top-pan balance with an unzeroed tare offset F₀, the force reading F is plotted against inverse-square separation (r⁻²) up to 50.0 m⁻², following F = k|Q₁Q₂|r⁻² + F₀. What is the gradient k|Q₁Q₂| of the line?
items.workedSolution: At r⁻² = 0.0 m⁻², tare offset F₀ = 0.1 N; at r⁻² = 50 m⁻², F = 0.9 N. Gradient = (0.9 − 0.1) / 50 = 0.0160 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts tare offset F₀ = 0.1 N to get (0.9 − 0.1) / 50 = 0.0160 N m² (B).

items.stem: In a Hall-probe magnetic flux calibration, vertical error bars on the first (1.0 A) and last (5.0 A) data points are used to draw the steepest acceptable line of worst fit shown on the graph.
items.workedSolution: (a) At 5 A, y₂ = 19.0 mV. (b) Worst-fit gradient = (19 − 2) / (5 − 1) = 4.25 mV A⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Reads y₂ = 19.0 mV.
Reads y₁ = 2 mV at x₁ = 1 A and forms Δy / Δx.
Subtracts x₁ = 1 A in the denominator (5 − 1).
Obtains 4.25 mV A⁻¹.

items.stem: On a straight test section, a magnetic-levitation shuttle pod moves on a horizontal vacuum test guideway (to the right positive) as shown on the velocity–time graph. What is its net displacement from t = 0.0 s to t = 12.0 s?
items.workedSolution: Velocity reaches zero at t = 8 s. Positive area = 48.0 m and area below the axis has magnitude 14.0 m. Net displacement = 48.0 − 14.0 = 34.0 m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts reverse area (14.0 m) from forward area (48.0 m) to obtain 34.0 m (B).

options.distractorRationale: Adds the magnitude of the negative-velocity area instead of subtracting it, finding total distance rather than net displacement.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Finds the maximum forward displacement at the turning point and ignores the subsequent reverse motion.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies half the difference of terminal speeds by total time, ignoring the piecewise plateau durations.

items.stem: Beginning 20.0 m past a sorting-hall origin sensor, a linear-induction baggage carrier follows the velocity–time profile shown over 12.0 s. What is its mean speed during the 12.0 s journey?
items.workedSolution: Distance travelled Δx = ½(12 + 5)(10) = 85.0 m (independent of the 20 m starting offset). Mean speed = 85.0 / 12 = 7.08 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Divides trapezium distance (85.0 m) by 12 s to obtain 7.08 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: The displacement–time graph records the motion of a laser-tracked precision stage along a metrology rail from t = 0.0 s to t = 12.0 s, including a stationary dwell and a final return stage from t = 8.0 s to t = 12.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Maximum displacement at the plateau = 38.0 m. (b) Return-stage velocity = (14 − 38) / (12 − 8) = -6.00 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Reads plateau displacement = 38.0 m.
Uses gradient formula Δs / Δt = (14 − 38) / (12 − 8).
Retains negative sign for motion back toward the origin.
Obtains -6.00 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Initially travelling along the track at 6.0 m s⁻¹, a linear-motor brake-test bogie undergoes the signed acceleration–time profile shown for 10.0 s. What is its velocity at t = 10.0 s?
items.workedSolution: Positive a–t area (0 to 6 s) = 18.0 m s⁻¹; negative area magnitude (6 s to 10 s) = 9.00 m s⁻¹. Net Δv = 18.0 − 9.00 = 9.00 m s⁻¹. Final velocity = 6 + (9.00) = 15.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Combines net signed area (9.00 m s⁻¹) with u₀ = 6 m s⁻¹ to obtain 15.0 m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: The graph displays the linear momentum of a frictionless puck on an air table (mass 0.8 kg) against time. What resultant force acts on it between t = 2.0 s and t = 5.0 s?
items.workedSolution: By Newton's second law, F = Δp / Δt = (6.4 − 1.6) / (5 − 2) = 1.60 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F = Δp / Δt = (6.4 − 1.6) / (3) = 1.60 N (C).

options.distractorRationale: Computes the secant ratio p₂ / t₂ from the origin, ignoring both initial momentum p₁ and start time t₁.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies Δp by Δt instead of evaluating the rate of change of momentum Δp / Δt.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides Δp / Δt by mass m, obtaining acceleration rather than resultant force.

items.stem: Travelling in a straight line with initial momentum 10.0 kg m s⁻¹, a crash-barrier test sled of mass 2.5 kg is acted upon by a collinear hydraulic arrester pulse for 1.0 s, as shown on the force–time graph.
items.workedSolution: (a) Impulse J = ½(1 + 0.6)(50) = 40.0 N s. (b) Final momentum p_f = 10 + 40.0 = 50.0 kg m s⁻¹. (c) Speed increase Δv = 40.0 / 2.5 = 16.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Computes impulse from the trapezium area under the F–t curve.
Obtains J = 40.0 N s.
Adds 10 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 50.0 kg m s⁻¹.
Divides impulse from (a) by 2.5 kg.
Obtains Δv = 16.0 m s⁻¹.

workingSteps: Impulse equals the area under the force–time trapezium.

parts.prompt: Determine the final momentum at t = 1.0 s.
Calculate the increase in speed of the 2.5 kg object.

items.stem: Moving forward from x = 0.0 m with initial speed 2.0 m s⁻¹, a pneumatic factory transfer cart (mass 4.0 kg) is subjected to the resultant force–displacement profile shown up to x = 12.0 m. How much net work is done on it over the 12.0 m displacement?
items.workedSolution: Forward work (0 to 10 m) = 120 J; resistive work (10 m to 12 m) = −4.00 J. Net work = 120 − 4.00 = 116 J.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts resistive triangle (4.00 J) from positive trapezium (120 J) to get 116 J (B).

items.stem: Background-corrected count rates from a radon progeny filter sample are recorded with a solid-state silicon alpha spectrometer over 50.0 s. The linearized graph plots ln(C / s⁻¹) against time t according to ln C = ln C₀ − λt. What is the gradient of this best-fit line?
items.workedSolution: At t = 0.0 s, ln C₀ = 9; at t = 50 s, ln C = 4. Gradient = (4 − 9) / 50 = -0.100 s⁻¹.

items.stem: The stress–strain graph shows a bio-derived collagen fibre bundle stretched reversibly through two piecewise-linear stages up to strain 0.5 (kink at strain 0.2). What work is done per unit volume in stretching the specimen to strain 0.5?
items.workedSolution: Work per unit volume equals area under the σ–ε graph (1 MPa × 1 = 1 MJ m⁻³): u = ½(0.2)(160) + ½(160 + 250)(0.3) = 77.5 MJ m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Sums triangle and trapezium areas under σ–ε curve to obtain 77.5 MJ m⁻³ (D).

items.stem: The potential difference–current characteristic for a miniature incandescent beacon lamp is plotted up to I = 1.5 A. What is the electrical resistance of the component when the current through it is 1.5 A?
items.workedSolution: Electrical resistance at an operating point is defined by R = V / I (not the local slope ΔV / ΔI). At I = 1.5 A, V = 10.5 V, so R = 10.5 / 1.5 = 7.00 Ω.

markScheme.criterion: Uses static ratio R = V / I = 10.5 / 1.5 = 7.00 Ω (D).

items.stem: In an experiment to characterize a lead-acid laboratory accumulator, a variable resistor is adjusted while recording terminal potential difference V and current I from 0.0 A to 4.0 A. The resulting best-fit line is shown.
items.workedSolution: (a) Open-circuit intercept gives ε = 12.0 V. (b) Gradient = (6 − 12) / 4 = -1.50 V A⁻¹. (c) Mean terminal p.d. = ½(12 + 6) = 9.00 V.

markScheme.criterion: Reads ε = 12.0 V at I = 0.
Evaluates (6 − 12) / 4 including negative sign.
Obtains -1.50 V A⁻¹.
Uses ½(12 + 6) or area divided by 4 A.
Obtains 9.00 V.

items.stem: Using crocodile clips with constant contact resistance R₀, a student measures total resistance R of a concentrated saline conductivity column for different length-to-area ratios (L / A) up to 500.0 m⁻¹, so R = ρ(L / A) + R₀. From the plotted line, what is the resistivity ρ of the material?
items.workedSolution: Since R = ρ(L / A) + R₀, resistivity ρ equals the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A) = (30 − 5) / 500 = 0.0500 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept R₀ = 5 Ω to obtain ρ = (30 − 5) / 500 = 0.0500 Ω m (C).

items.stem: In a kinematics linearization lab (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²), a dual-photogate brass cylinder released past an upper light gate on a frictionless slope with sin θ = 0.3 passes s = 0.0 m at speed u₀ and continues to s = 2.0 m. Determine the gradient of the plotted v² versus s graph.
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 1.5 m² s⁻² and at s = 2 m, v² = 13.272 m² s⁻². Gradient = (13.272 − 1.5) / 2 = 2(9.81)(0.3) = 5.89 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 1.5 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.81 × 0.3) to get 5.89 m s⁻² (B).

items.stem: In an experiment verifying Coulomb's inverse-square law using charged graphite-coated spheres on a quartz-fibre force sensor, total force reading F is plotted against inverse-square separation r⁻² up to 100.0 m⁻², obeying F = k|Q₁Q₂|r⁻² + F₀.
items.workedSolution: (a) At r⁻² = 0, systematic tare offset F₀ = 0.200 N. (b) Gradient = (1.4 − 0.2) / 100 = 0.0120 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Reads intercept F₀ = 0.200 N.
Evaluates ΔF = 1.4 − 0.2 using intercept from (a).
Divides ΔF by 100 m⁻² and states correct unit N m².
Obtains 0.0120 N m².

parts.prompt: State the systematic tare offset F₀ of the balance as separation r approaches infinity.
workingSteps: As r → ∞, r⁻² → 0, where the vertical intercept gives F₀ = 0.200 N.

workingSteps: Read F = 1.4 N at r⁻² = 100 m⁻².

items.stem: To estimate gradient uncertainty in a piezoelectric load-cell calibration, a student draws the steepest acceptable line of worst fit between the extreme error-bar vertices at applied load 2.0 N and 10.0 N, as plotted. What is the gradient m_worst of this worst-fit line?
items.workedSolution: At x₁ = 2 N, y₁ = 6 mV; at x₂ = 10 N, y₂ = 34 mV. Worst-fit gradient m_worst = (34 − 6) / (10 − 2) = 3.50 mV N⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δy / Δx = (34 − 6) / (10 − 2) = 3.50 mV N⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: The graph displays how the velocity of a robotic warehouse retrieval carriage along a straight aisle rail varies with time over 12.0 s. Positive velocity corresponds to motion forward, and direction reversal occurs during the linear ramp between t = 6.0 s and t = 10.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Zero-velocity crossing is at t = 9 s. Positive area = 54.0 m and unsigned negative area = 7.50 m, giving total distance = 61.5 m. (b) Net displacement = 54.0 − 7.50 = 46.5 m; average velocity = 46.5 / 12 = 3.88 m s⁻¹. (c) Acceleration = (−3 − 9) / (10 − 6) = -3.00 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Finds zero-crossing t = 9 s and evaluates both unsigned areas (54.0 m and 7.50 m).
Obtains total distance = 61.5 m.
Subtracts areas for net displacement (46.5 m) and divides by 12 s.
Obtains average velocity = 3.88 m s⁻¹.
Obtains acceleration = -3.00 m s⁻² including negative sign.

parts.prompt: Calculate the total distance travelled between t = 0.0 s and t = 12.0 s.
workingSteps: Velocity crosses zero at t = 9 s; forward area = 54.0 m.
Unsigned reverse area = 7.50 m, so total distance = 54.0 + 7.50 = 61.5 m.

parts.prompt: Determine the net displacement and hence calculate the average velocity over the 12.0 s interval.
workingSteps: Average velocity = Δs / Δt = 46.5 / 12 = 3.88 m s⁻¹.

parts.prompt: Calculate the acceleration between t = 6.0 s and t = 10.0 s.

items.stem: Starting at x = 25.0 m from a lock-gate reference mark, a canal lock towing locomotive completes the 16.0 s journey shown on the velocity–time graph, braking uniformly from t = 10.0 s to t = 16.0 s. What is its acceleration during braking?
items.workedSolution: During braking from t = 10 s to t = 16 s, a = (0 − 15) / (16 − 10) = -2.50 m s⁻².

items.stem: Over a 10.0 s cycle on a straight chute, an automated pharmacy courier pod follows the piecewise displacement–time graph shown. What is its average velocity from t = 0.0 s to t = 10.0 s?
items.workedSolution: Initial displacement at t = 0.0 s is 10 m and final displacement at t = 10 s is 18 m. Average velocity = (18 − 10) / 10 = 0.800 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates net displacement (18 − 10) / 10 = 0.800 m s⁻¹ (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Sums outward and return path lengths to compute average speed rather than net average velocity.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Takes the unweighted arithmetic mean of the two non-zero stage velocities, ignoring stage durations and the dwell plateau.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses final coordinate s₂ / t₃ and forgets to subtract the non-zero starting coordinate s₀.

items.stem: At t = 0.0 s, a centrifuge carrier pod moves tangentially forward with an initial velocity of 4.0 m s⁻¹. The graph shows how its acceleration varies with time over 10.0 s (tangentially forward positive).
items.workedSolution: (a) Maximum speed occurs when acceleration crosses zero from positive to negative at t = 5.00 s. (b) Positive area = 28.0 m s⁻¹, giving v_max = 4 + 28.0 = 32.0 m s⁻¹. (c) Negative area magnitude = 16.0 m s⁻¹, so v_final = 32.0 − 16.0 = 16.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: States t = 5.00 s.
Evaluates positive area up to 5 s (28.0 m s⁻¹) and adds u₀ = 4 m s⁻¹.
Obtains v_max = 32.0 m s⁻¹.
Subtracts negative area (16.0 m s⁻¹) from v_max.
Obtains final velocity = 16.0 m s⁻¹.

workingSteps: Acceleration changes from positive to negative at t = 5.00 s.

parts.prompt: Calculate this maximum speed.
Calculate the velocity at t = 10.0 s.
workingSteps: Magnitude of negative a–t area (5 s to 10 s) = ½(2)(4) + (3)(4) = 16.0 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: The momentum–time graph is recorded for a magnetic rail cart (mass 1.2 kg) travelling along a straight guide. Calculate the net work done on the object from t = 3.0 s to t = 7.0 s.
items.workedSolution: Using E_k = p² / (2m), net work W = ΔE_k = (8.4² − 2.4²) / (2 × 1.2) = 27.0 J.

items.stem: During a 2.0 s solenoid kicker stroke, a robotic soccer puck (mass 4.0 kg, initial momentum 12.0 kg m s⁻¹) experiences the force–time profile shown. What is the time-averaged resultant force over the 2.0 s interval?
items.workedSolution: Total impulse J = ½(2 + 1)(32) = 48.0 N s. Mean force F_mean = J / Δt = 48.0 / 2 = 24.0 N.

markScheme.criterion: Divides impulse (48.0 N s) by 2 s to obtain 24.0 N (B).

items.stem: At x = 0.0 m, a magnetic-launch coaster bogie of mass 2.5 kg moves in the positive x-direction at 4.0 m s⁻¹. The graph shows the resultant force acting along its line of motion from x = 0.0 m to x = 10.0 m.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates positive (82.5 J) and negative (−5.00 J) areas.
Obtains net work W = 77.5 J.
Uses ½mv² = ½(2.5)(4²) + W.
Obtains v = 8.83 m s⁻¹.
Divides net work by 10 m to get 7.75 N.

items.stem: A 0.4 kg trolley rests against a linear valve return spring compressed to 0.8 m. Using the plotted force–compression line and neglecting friction, calculate the speed of the trolley upon separation.
items.workedSolution: Elastic energy stored E_p = ½(48)(0.8) = 19.2 J. Equating ½mv² = E_p gives v = √(2 × 19.2 / 0.4) = 9.80 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Sets ½(0.4)v² = 19.2 J to obtain v = 9.80 m s⁻¹ (A).

items.stem: A tensile testing machine stretches a polypropylene surgical suture up to a strain of 0.5, producing the stress–strain curve shown. The limit of proportionality occurs at strain 0.25.
items.workedSolution: (a) Young's modulus E = 150 / 0.25 = 600 MPa. (b) Energy per unit volume = ½(0.25)(150) + ½(150 + 220)(0.25) = 65.0 MJ m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates initial gradient σ / ε up to ε = 0.25.
Obtains E = 600 MPa.
Identifies work per unit volume as total area under the σ–ε graph.
Splits area into initial triangle plus upper trapezium.
Obtains 65.0 MJ m⁻³.

items.stem: Using the plotted V–I characteristic of a quartz-halogen calibration lamp, calculate its static resistance R at an operating current of 1.6 A.
items.workedSolution: Electrical resistance at an operating point is defined by R = V / I (not the local slope ΔV / ΔI). At I = 1.6 A, V = 9.6 V, so R = 9.6 / 1.6 = 6.00 Ω.

markScheme.criterion: Uses static ratio R = V / I = 9.6 / 1.6 = 6.00 Ω (A).

items.stem: Over load currents uniformly spanning 0.0 A to 2.5 A, a zinc-carbon dry cell exhibits the linear V–I plot shown. Calculate the average terminal potential difference across the plotted interval.
items.workedSolution: Terminal p.d. varies linearly from 9 V at I = 0.0 A to 3 V at I = 2.5 A, so V_mean = ½(9 + 3) = 6.00 V.

markScheme.criterion: Averages endpoint voltages ½(9 + 3) = 6.00 V (A).

options.distractorRationale: Halves the EMF as if terminal voltage dropped to zero at I_max.

options.label: C

items.stem: Measured resistance R is plotted against length-to-area ratio L / A up to 200.0 m⁻¹ for an aqueous copper-sulfate capillary cell, obeying R = ρ(L / A) + R₀ where R₀ is the constant lead resistance.
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical intercept R₀ = 3.00 Ω. (b) Resistivity ρ = (19 − 3) / 200 = 0.0800 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: States R₀ = 3.00 Ω.
Identifies ρ with the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A).
Subtracts R₀ = 3 Ω from 19 Ω before dividing by 200 m⁻¹.
Obtains ρ = 0.0800 Ω m.

parts.prompt: State the systematic lead and contact resistance R₀.
workingSteps: At L / A = 0.0 m⁻¹, the vertical intercept gives R₀ = 3.00 Ω.

parts.prompt: Determine the resistivity ρ of an aqueous copper-sulfate capillary cell from the graph.
workingSteps: From R = ρ(L / A) + R₀, ρ equals the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A).

items.stem: Photogate data for a levitated neodymium shuttle descending an inclined guide accelerating down an incline (sin θ = 0.4, g = 9.8 m s⁻²) from s = 0.0 m to s = 1.6 m are linearized by plotting v² against s. What gradient does the best-fit line have?
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 2.4 m² s⁻² and at s = 1.6 m, v² = 14.944 m² s⁻². Gradient = (14.944 − 2.4) / 1.6 = 2(9.8)(0.4) = 7.84 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 2.4 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.8 × 0.4) to get 7.84 m s⁻² (B).

items.stem: Readings F from nickel-plated hollow spheres suspended over an analytical balance are linearized against r⁻² from 0.0 m⁻² to 40.0 m⁻². Accounting for the systematic zero-offset F₀, determine the gradient ΔF / Δ(r⁻²).
items.workedSolution: At r⁻² = 0.0 m⁻², tare offset F₀ = 0.15 N; at r⁻² = 40 m⁻², F = 0.95 N. Gradient = (0.95 − 0.15) / 40 = 0.0200 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts tare offset F₀ = 0.15 N to get (0.95 − 0.15) / 40 = 0.0200 N m² (A).

items.stem: To bound gradient uncertainty in a thermocouple electromotive-force test, a student plots the shallowest line of worst fit through the error-bar extremes between 1.0 K and 5.0 K.
items.workedSolution: (a) At 5 K, y₂ = 17.0 mV. (b) Worst-fit gradient = (17 − 5) / (5 − 1) = 3.00 mV K⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Reads y₂ = 17.0 mV.
Reads y₁ = 5 mV at x₁ = 1 K and forms Δy / Δx.
Subtracts x₁ = 1 K in the denominator (5 − 1).
Obtains 3.00 mV K⁻¹.

items.stem: Telemetry from a cable-hauled alpine service car operating on a straight haulage section is plotted on the velocity–time axes shown (uphill positive). What total path distance is covered over the 10.0 s run?
items.workedSolution: Velocity crosses zero at t = 7 s. Forward area (0 to 7 s) = ½(2)(6) + (2)(6) + ½(3)(6) = 27.0 m. Reverse area magnitude (7 s to 10 s) = ½(1)(2) + (2)(2) = 5.00 m. Total distance = 27.0 + 5.00 = 32.0 m.

markScheme.criterion: Sums unsigned positive (27.0 m) and negative (5.00 m) velocity–time areas to obtain 32.0 m (A).

options.distractorRationale: Integrates only up to the zero-velocity instant and omits the distance travelled after reversing direction.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts the area below the time axis from the positive area, giving net signed displacement rather than total distance.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies peak forward velocity by the entire duration without accounting for ramps or direction reversal.

items.stem: Starting 12.0 m beyond the base-camp beacon at t = 0.0 s, a solar-powered desert research rover executes the 8.0 s velocity–time profile shown. How far from the base-camp beacon does it come to rest?
items.workedSolution: Displacement during the 8 s run equals the trapezium area: Δx = ½(8 + 4)(8) = 48.0 m. Final position from the base-camp beacon = x₀ + Δx = 12 + 48.0 = 60.0 m.

markScheme.criterion: Adds trapezium area (48.0 m) to initial offset (12 m) to get 60.0 m (A).

items.stem: Position measurements of a coastal tide-gauge float moving on a vertical stilling tube over a 16.0 s run are plotted on the displacement–time axes shown, with return travel occurring between t = 10.0 s and t = 16.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Maximum displacement at the plateau = 48.0 m. (b) Return-stage velocity = (24 − 48) / (16 − 10) = -4.00 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Reads plateau displacement = 48.0 m.
Uses gradient formula Δs / Δt = (24 − 48) / (16 − 10).
Retains negative sign for motion back toward the origin.
Obtains -4.00 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: An accelerometer mounted on a mine hoist cage records the 12.0 s profile shown, starting from an initial upward velocity of 8.0 m s⁻¹. Determine the greatest upward speed attained.
items.workedSolution: Speed increases while a > 0 (from t = 0.0 s until a = 0 at t = 6 s). Positive area Δv_max = (4)(5) + ½(2)(5) = 25.0 m s⁻¹. Maximum speed = u₀ + Δv_max = 8 + 25.0 = 33.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Integrates positive acceleration up to t = 6 s (25.0 m s⁻¹) and adds 8 m s⁻¹ to get 33.0 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: Data loggers record the linear momentum of a satellite attitude-test mass (mass 1.5 kg), which experiences a constant resultant force between t = 2.0 s and t = 6.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Resultant force F = Δp / Δt = (9 − 3) / (6 − 2) = 1.50 N. (b) Net work W = ΔE_k = (9² − 3²) / (2 × 1.5) = 24.0 J.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies resultant force as gradient Δp / Δt of the p–t graph.
Obtains F = 1.50 N.
Relates net work to ΔE_k = (p₂² − p₁²) / (2m).
Substitutes p₁ = 3 kg m s⁻¹, p₂ = 9 kg m s⁻¹, and m = 1.5 kg.
Obtains W = 24.0 J.

items.stem: A spring buffer contact acts for 1.6 s in the direction of motion of a rail-mounted docking target (mass 1.5 kg, initial momentum 4.5 kg m s⁻¹). Using the plotted force–time profile, determine Δv.
items.workedSolution: Impulse J = area under F–t trapezium = ½(1.6 + 0.8)(30) = 36.0 N s. Speed increase Δv = J / m = 36.0 / 1.5 = 24.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Computes J = 36.0 N s and Δv = J / 1.5 = 24.0 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: Evaluate the net work done by the resultant force on a cable-towed hydroplane model (mass 5.0 kg, initial speed 3.0 m s⁻¹) between x = 0.0 m and x = 16.0 m using the graph.
items.workedSolution: Forward work (0 to 14 m) = 200 J; resistive work (14 m to 16 m) = −5.00 J. Net work = 200 − 5.00 = 195 J.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts resistive triangle (5.00 J) from positive trapezium (200 J) to get 195 J (D).

items.stem: In a nuclear physics practical, a gallium radiopharmaceutical ampoule is monitored with an ionization well chamber. The semi-logarithmic plot of ln(C / s⁻¹) versus time t over 60.0 s is shown.
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical intercept at t = 0 is ln(C₀ / s⁻¹) = 8.40. (b) Gradient = (3.6 − 8.4) / 60 = -0.0800 s⁻¹ (which equals −λ).

markScheme.criterion: Reads vertical intercept = 8.40.
Uses large triangle (3.6 − 8.4) / 60.

items.stem: A tensile test on a helical steel launcher spring yields the linear force–extension plot up to 0.4 m. Calculate the elastic energy stored when extended by 0.4 m.
items.workedSolution: Elastic potential energy equals the triangular area under the F–x line: E_p = ½ F x = ½(60)(0.4) = 12.0 J.

markScheme.criterion: Computes triangular area ½(60)(0.4) = 12.0 J (A).

items.stem: Determine the strain energy stored per unit volume (in MJ m⁻³) when a high-density polyethylene filament is loaded from zero strain to 0.8 along the plotted stress–strain curve (proportional limit at 0.4).
items.workedSolution: Work per unit volume equals area under the σ–ε graph (1 MPa × 1 = 1 MJ m⁻³): u = ½(0.4)(200) + ½(200 + 280)(0.4) = 136 MJ m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Sums triangle and trapezium areas under σ–ε curve to obtain 136 MJ m⁻³ (A).

parts.prompt: State the potential difference across the component at I = 1.0 A.
workingSteps: From the graph at I = 1 A, V = 9.00 V.

parts.prompt: Calculate the resistance of the component at I = 1.0 A.
workingSteps: Resistance is defined as the ratio R = V / I at that operating point (not ΔV / ΔI).

items.stem: Refer to the terminal potential difference–current plot for a lithium-iron-phosphate storage cell over 0.0 A to 1.6 A. What value does the signed slope of the best-fit line take?
items.workedSolution: At I = 0.0 A, V = ε = 4.8 V; at I = 1.6 A, V = 1.6 V. Gradient = (1.6 − 4.8) / 1.6 = -2.00 V A⁻¹ (equal to −r).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Assumes the line meets V = 0 at I = I_max instead of reading the non-zero terminal voltage V(I_max).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates internal resistance r = |ΔV / ΔI| but omits the negative sign of the downward V–I gradient.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts ΔI / ΔV instead of computing ΔV / ΔI.

items.stem: Total circuit resistance R (including lead resistance R₀) is plotted against geometric ratio L / A up to 250.0 m⁻¹ for a potassium-chloride electrolyte tube. Calculate the electrical resistivity ρ.
items.workedSolution: Since R = ρ(L / A) + R₀, resistivity ρ equals the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A) = (26 − 6) / 250 = 0.0800 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept R₀ = 6 Ω to obtain ρ = (26 − 6) / 250 = 0.0800 Ω m (D).

items.stem: The linearized Coulomb plot shows balance force F versus inverse-square separation r⁻² up to 80.0 m⁻² for two conducting pith spheres on a digital top-pan balance. Calculate the gradient of the line in N m².
items.workedSolution: At r⁻² = 0.0 m⁻², tare offset F₀ = 0.2 N; at r⁻² = 80 m⁻², F = 1.8 N. Gradient = (1.8 − 0.2) / 80 = 0.0200 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts tare offset F₀ = 0.2 N to get (1.8 − 0.2) / 80 = 0.0200 N m² (A).

items.stem: The graph displays the steepest line of worst fit joining opposite vertical error-bar extremes from 2.0 A to 8.0 A in a Helmholtz-coil axial field check. Calculate its gradient.
items.workedSolution: At x₁ = 2 A, y₁ = 4 mT; at x₂ = 8 A, y₂ = 25 mT. Worst-fit gradient m_worst = (25 − 4) / (8 − 2) = 3.50 mT A⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δy / Δx = (25 − 4) / (8 − 2) = 3.50 mT A⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: A data logger records the signed velocity of a linear-motor camera dolly moving on a studio optical bench (northward positive) over a 16.0 s cycle, with constant braking and reversal applied between t = 8.0 s and t = 12.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Zero-velocity crossing is at t = 11 s. Positive area = 45.0 m and unsigned negative area = 9.00 m, giving total distance = 54.0 m. (b) Net displacement = 45.0 − 9.00 = 36.0 m; average velocity = 36.0 / 16 = 2.25 m s⁻¹. (c) Acceleration = (−2 − 6) / (12 − 8) = -2.00 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Finds zero-crossing t = 11 s and evaluates both unsigned areas (45.0 m and 9.00 m).
Obtains total distance = 54.0 m.
Subtracts areas for net displacement (36.0 m) and divides by 16 s.
Obtains average velocity = 2.25 m s⁻¹.
Obtains acceleration = -2.00 m s⁻² including negative sign.

parts.prompt: Calculate the total distance travelled between t = 0.0 s and t = 16.0 s.
workingSteps: Velocity crosses zero at t = 11 s; forward area = 45.0 m.
Unsigned reverse area = 9.00 m, so total distance = 45.0 + 9.00 = 54.0 m.

parts.prompt: Determine the net displacement and hence calculate the average velocity over the 16.0 s interval.
workingSteps: Average velocity = Δs / Δt = 36.0 / 16 = 2.25 m s⁻¹.

parts.prompt: Calculate the acceleration between t = 8.0 s and t = 12.0 s.

items.stem: Over a 20.0 s transfer starting at x = 30.0 m from the western end-stop, a shipyard gantry crane crab has the velocity–time graph shown. Calculate its average speed over the 20.0 s interval.
items.workedSolution: Distance travelled Δx = ½(20 + 10)(14) = 210 m (independent of the 30 m starting offset). Mean speed = 210 / 20 = 10.5 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Divides trapezium distance (210 m) by 20 s to obtain 10.5 m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: An inertial sensor logs the acceleration of an electromagnetic catapult shuttle over a 10.0 s interval (forward positive). At t = 0.0 s its velocity is 7.0 m s⁻¹ forward.
items.workedSolution: (a) Maximum speed occurs when acceleration crosses zero from positive to negative at t = 4.00 s. (b) Positive area = 30.0 m s⁻¹, giving v_max = 7 + 30.0 = 37.0 m s⁻¹. (c) Negative area magnitude = 15.0 m s⁻¹, so v_final = 37.0 − 15.0 = 22.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: States t = 4.00 s.
Evaluates positive area up to 4 s (30.0 m s⁻¹) and adds u₀ = 7 m s⁻¹.
Obtains v_max = 37.0 m s⁻¹.
Subtracts negative area (15.0 m s⁻¹) from v_max.
Obtains final velocity = 22.0 m s⁻¹.

parts.prompt: Calculate this maximum speed.
Calculate the velocity at t = 10.0 s.
workingSteps: Magnitude of negative a–t area (4 s to 10 s) = ½(2)(3) + (4)(3) = 15.0 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: A thruster acts from t = 4.0 s to t = 8.0 s on a superconducting levitation carrier of mass 2.0 kg, producing the momentum–time trace shown. What kinetic energy gain (net work) occurs over this interval?
items.workedSolution: Using E_k = p² / (2m), net work W = ΔE_k = (14² − 4²) / (2 × 2) = 45.0 J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies W = (p₂² − p₁²) / (2m) = (14² − 4²) / (4) = 45.0 J (A).

items.stem: Before a 4.0 s pulsed ion-beam firing, a Hall-effect thruster test rig of mass 5.0 kg has momentum 15.0 kg m s⁻¹. Using the force–time plot, find its momentum immediately after the pulse.
items.workedSolution: Impulse Δp = ½(4 + 2)(25) = 75.0 N s. Final momentum p_f = p₀ + Δp = 15 + 75.0 = 90.0 kg m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Adds impulse (75.0 N s) to p₀ = 15 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 90.0 kg m s⁻¹ (A).

options.distractorRationale: Subtracts initial momentum from impulse instead of adding collinear forward impulse.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses peak force times total duration for impulse rather than the trapezium area.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Finds the impulse Δp from the F–t area but forgets to add the initial momentum p₀.

items.stem: Force-transducer and encoder data for a linear dynamo test sled (mass 1.6 kg, speed 2.5 m s⁻¹ at x = 0.0 m) are plotted over a 8.0 m straight track.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates positive (54.0 J) and negative (−4.00 J) areas.
Obtains net work W = 50.0 J.
Uses ½mv² = ½(1.6)(2.5²) + W.
Obtains v = 8.29 m s⁻¹.
Divides net work by 8 m to get 6.25 N.

parts.prompt: Calculate the net work done on the 1.6 kg object between x = 0.0 m and x = 8.0 m.
workingSteps: Positive area (0 to 6 m) = ½(6 + 3)(12) = 54.0 J; negative area (6 m to 8 m) = −½(2)(4) = −4.00 J.

parts.prompt: Calculate its speed at x = 8.0 m.
State the mean resultant force over the 8.0 m displacement.

items.stem: In an energy-transfer investigation, an air-track bumper compression spring is compressed to 0.5 m as shown on the force–compression graph and used to project a 0.5 kg cart along a frictionless horizontal rail from rest.
items.workedSolution: (a) k = 80 / 0.5 = 160 N m⁻¹. (b) Elastic energy E_p = ½(80)(0.5) = 20.0 J. (c) Launch speed v = √(2(20.0)/0.5) = 8.94 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies k as the gradient ΔF / Δx.
Obtains k = 160 N m⁻¹.
Uses triangular area ½Fx.
Obtains E_p = 20.0 J.
Equates ½(0.5)v² to stored elastic energy from (b).
Obtains v = 8.94 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Refer to the tensile stress–strain plot for a bio-derived collagen fibre bundle, whose limit of proportionality lies at strain 0.3. Calculate its initial Young's modulus.
items.workedSolution: Up to the limit of proportionality at ε = 0.3, stress reaches 180 MPa. Young's modulus E = σ / ε = 180 / 0.3 = 600 MPa.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates initial linear gradient E = 180 / 0.3 = 600 MPa (A).

items.stem: A student measures the V–I curve shown for a halogen projection bulb. Determine the resistance of the device at I = 2.0 A.
items.workedSolution: Electrical resistance at an operating point is defined by R = V / I (not the local slope ΔV / ΔI). At I = 2 A, V = 11 V, so R = 11 / 2 = 5.50 Ω.

markScheme.criterion: Uses static ratio R = V / I = 11 / 2 = 5.50 Ω (B).

items.stem: A student connects an ammeter, high-impedance voltmeter, and rheostat to a portable photovoltaic module under constant irradiance, obtaining the linear V–I plot over 0.0 A to 5.0 A.
items.workedSolution: (a) Open-circuit intercept gives ε = 15.0 V. (b) Gradient = (6 − 15) / 5 = -1.80 V A⁻¹. (c) Mean terminal p.d. = ½(15 + 6) = 10.5 V.

markScheme.criterion: Reads ε = 15.0 V at I = 0.
Evaluates (6 − 15) / 5 including negative sign.
Obtains -1.80 V A⁻¹.
Uses ½(15 + 6) or area divided by 5 A.
Obtains 10.5 V.

items.stem: The linearized graph shows measured resistance R versus L / A for a concentrated saline conductivity column over 0.0 m⁻¹ to 400.0 m⁻¹. Accounting for the non-zero contact-resistance intercept, determine ρ.
items.workedSolution: Since R = ρ(L / A) + R₀, resistivity ρ equals the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A) = (40 − 8) / 400 = 0.0800 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept R₀ = 8 Ω to obtain ρ = (40 − 8) / 400 = 0.0800 Ω m (A).

items.stem: Taking g = 9.8 m s⁻², a dual-photogate brass cylinder released past an upper light gate descends a smooth plane inclined at sin θ = 0.35, passing s = 0.0 m already in motion. From the v² against s plot up to 2.0 m, find the slope Δ(v²) / Δs.
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 3 m² s⁻² and at s = 2 m, v² = 16.72 m² s⁻². Gradient = (16.72 − 3) / 2 = 2(9.8)(0.35) = 6.86 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 3 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.8 × 0.35) to get 6.86 m s⁻² (C).

options.label: D

items.stem: Electrostatic force measurements from isolated brass domes mounted above an electronic microbalance are linearized by plotting balance reading F against r⁻² over 0.0 m⁻² to 50.0 m⁻².
items.workedSolution: (a) At r⁻² = 0, systematic tare offset F₀ = 0.250 N. (b) Gradient = (1.25 − 0.25) / 50 = 0.0200 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Reads intercept F₀ = 0.250 N.
Evaluates ΔF = 1.25 − 0.25 using intercept from (a).
Divides ΔF by 50 m⁻² and states correct unit N m².
Obtains 0.0200 N m².

items.stem: During uncertainty analysis of a piezoelectric load-cell calibration, the steepest worst-fit line is constructed across the domain 0.5 N to 2.5 N. Determine the gradient of the plotted line.
items.workedSolution: At x₁ = 0.5 N, y₁ = 1.2 mV; at x₂ = 2.5 N, y₂ = 8.4 mV. Worst-fit gradient m_worst = (8.4 − 1.2) / (2.5 − 0.5) = 3.60 mV N⁻¹.

items.stem: Inspect the constant-gradient reversal stage from t = 7.0 s to t = 10.0 s for an underwater ROV thruster sled moving along a taut calibration tether. What signed acceleration acts over this stage?
items.workedSolution: Between t = 7 s and t = 10 s, velocity changes from +10 m s⁻¹ to −5 m s⁻¹. Acceleration a = Δv / Δt = (−5 − 10) / (10 − 7) = -5.00 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δv / Δt = (−5 − 10) / (3) = -5.00 m s⁻² (B).

items.stem: Telemetry for an underground mine haulage skip begins at t = 0.0 s when it is stationary 40.0 m beyond the shaft loading datum. Its velocity–time profile over the 15.0 s run is plotted, with braking starting at t = 9.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Trapezium area Δx = ½(15 + 6)(18) = 189 m. (b) Final distance from datum = 40 + 189 = 229 m. (c) Mean speed = 189 / 15 = 12.6 m s⁻¹. (d) Braking acceleration = (0 − 18) / (15 − 9) = -3.00 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Identifies distance travelled as the area under the v–t trapezium.
Obtains Δx = 189 m.
Adds 40 m offset to obtain 229 m.
Divides distance travelled from (a) by 15 s.
Obtains mean speed = 12.6 m s⁻¹.
Obtains braking acceleration = -3.00 m s⁻².

items.stem: Telemetry shows the downrange acceleration of a railgun armature test sled over 10.0 s. Given an initial downrange velocity of 9.0 m s⁻¹ at t = 0.0 s, calculate the velocity at t = 10.0 s.
items.workedSolution: Positive a–t area (0 to 5 s) = 24.0 m s⁻¹; negative area magnitude (5 s to 10 s) = 14.0 m s⁻¹. Net Δv = 24.0 − 14.0 = 10.0 m s⁻¹. Final velocity = 9 + (10.0) = 19.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Combines net signed area (10.0 m s⁻¹) with u₀ = 9 m s⁻¹ to obtain 19.0 m s⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: Along a horizontal guideway, a low-friction dynamics trolley of mass 0.4 kg moves in a fixed direction. Its momentum–time graph shows an impulse stage from t = 1.0 s to t = 5.0 s.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies resultant force as gradient Δp / Δt of the p–t graph.
Obtains F = 0.700 N.
Relates net work to ΔE_k = (p₂² − p₁²) / (2m).
Substitutes p₁ = 0.8 kg m s⁻¹, p₂ = 3.6 kg m s⁻¹, and m = 0.4 kg.
Obtains W = 15.4 J.

items.stem: Calculate the mean resultant force exerted during the 0.5 s controlled gas-jet pulse on a ballistic pendulum carriage (mass 0.8 kg, initial momentum 2.4 kg m s⁻¹) from the plotted F–t curve.
items.workedSolution: Total impulse J = ½(0.5 + 0.3)(32) = 12.8 N s. Mean force F_mean = J / Δt = 12.8 / 0.5 = 25.6 N.

markScheme.criterion: Divides impulse (12.8 N s) by 0.5 s to obtain 25.6 N (D).

items.stem: Moving forward from x = 0.0 m with initial speed 4.0 m s⁻¹, a warehouse pallet shuttle (mass 3.0 kg) is subjected to the resultant force–displacement profile shown up to x = 15.0 m. How much net work is done on it over the 15.0 m displacement?
items.workedSolution: Forward work (0 to 12 m) = 162 J; resistive work (12 m to 15 m) = −9.00 J. Net work = 162 − 9.00 = 153 J.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts resistive triangle (9.00 J) from positive trapezium (162 J) to get 153 J (B).

items.stem: After subtracting ambient background radiation, readings C from a thin-mica Geiger counter facing a protactinium generator organic layer are transformed to ln(C / s⁻¹) and plotted over 25.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical intercept at t = 0 is ln(C₀ / s⁻¹) = 7.50. (b) Gradient = (2.5 − 7.5) / 25 = -0.200 s⁻¹ (which equals −λ).

Includes negative sign and unit s⁻¹.

items.stem: Neglecting resistive losses, how fast does a 0.4 kg puck leave a linear valve return spring when released from rest at 1.0 m compression on the plotted curve?
items.workedSolution: Elastic energy stored E_p = ½(50)(1) = 25.0 J. Equating ½mv² = E_p gives v = √(2 × 25.0 / 0.4) = 11.2 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Sets ½(0.4)v² = 25.0 J to obtain v = 11.2 m s⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: The stress–strain graph shows an extruded fluoropolymer ribbon stretched reversibly through two piecewise-linear stages up to strain 0.4 (kink at strain 0.2). What work is done per unit volume in stretching the specimen to strain 0.4?
items.workedSolution: Work per unit volume equals area under the σ–ε graph (1 MPa × 1 = 1 MJ m⁻³): u = ½(0.2)(90) + ½(90 + 140)(0.2) = 32.0 MJ m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Sums triangle and trapezium areas under σ–ε curve to obtain 32.0 MJ m⁻³ (B).

items.stem: Using a variable DC supply, ammeter, and voltmeter, measurements on an NTC ceramic temperature-sensing disc up to 1.2 A produce the curved V–I trace below.
items.workedSolution: (a) At I = 1.2 A, V = 8.40 V. (b) Static resistance R = V / I = 8.4 / 1.2 = 7.00 Ω (the upper segment gradient 9.50 Ω is ΔV / ΔI, not R).

markScheme.criterion: Reads V = 8.40 V at I = 1.2 A.
Selects R = V / I rather than local segment gradient ΔV / ΔI.
Substitutes V = 8.4 V and I = 1.2 A.
Obtains R = 7.00 Ω.

items.stem: Evaluate the average terminal potential difference delivered by a zinc-carbon dry cell across the plotted current domain 0.0 A to 0.8 A.
items.workedSolution: Terminal p.d. varies linearly from 3.2 V at I = 0.0 A to 1.2 V at I = 0.8 A, so V_mean = ½(3.2 + 1.2) = 2.20 V.

markScheme.criterion: Averages endpoint voltages ½(3.2 + 1.2) = 2.20 V (D).

items.stem: In an electrical properties lab, resistance readings across a carbon-loaded antistatic composite bar are linearized against geometric factor L / A up to 500.0 m⁻¹, revealing a non-zero contact offset R₀.
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical intercept R₀ = 10.0 Ω. (b) Resistivity ρ = (45 − 10) / 500 = 0.0700 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: States R₀ = 10.0 Ω.
Identifies ρ with the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A).
Subtracts R₀ = 10 Ω from 45 Ω before dividing by 500 m⁻¹.
Obtains ρ = 0.0700 Ω m.

workingSteps: At L / A = 0.0 m⁻¹, the vertical intercept gives R₀ = 10.0 Ω.

items.stem: Speed-squared readings v² are graphed against displacement s (0.0 m to 1.0 m) for a levitated neodymium shuttle descending an inclined guide on a frictionless ramp of sin θ = 0.6 where g = 9.81 m s⁻². Calculate the gradient of the line.
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 2.2 m² s⁻² and at s = 1 m, v² = 13.972 m² s⁻². Gradient = (13.972 − 2.2) / 1 = 2(9.81)(0.6) = 11.8 m s⁻².

items.stem: In an electrostatics investigation with nickel-plated hollow spheres suspended over an analytical balance, F is plotted against r⁻² up to 100.0 m⁻². Extract the proportionality constant k|Q₁Q₂| given by the slope.
items.workedSolution: At r⁻² = 0.0 m⁻², tare offset F₀ = 0.1 N; at r⁻² = 100 m⁻², F = 0.8 N. Gradient = (0.8 − 0.1) / 100 = 0.00700 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts tare offset F₀ = 0.1 N to get (0.8 − 0.1) / 100 = 0.00700 N m² (C).

items.stem: During data analysis for an optical photodiode irradiance calibration, opposite ends of the uncertainty bars at 4.0 mW and 20.0 mW are joined to form the shallowest worst-fit line below.
items.workedSolution: (a) At 20 mW, y₂ = 52.0 μA. (b) Worst-fit gradient = (52 − 12) / (20 − 4) = 2.50 μA mW⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Reads y₂ = 52.0 μA.
Reads y₁ = 12 μA at x₁ = 4 mW and forms Δy / Δx.
Subtracts x₁ = 4 mW in the denominator (20 − 4).
Obtains 2.50 μA mW⁻¹.

items.stem: The velocity–time profile shows a cleanroom wafer transport shuttle reversing motion along a linear air bearing with to the right defined as positive. Calculate the total scalar distance travelled between t = 0.0 s and t = 12.0 s.
items.workedSolution: Velocity crosses zero at t = 8 s. Forward area (0 to 8 s) = ½(2)(12) + (3)(12) + ½(3)(12) = 66.0 m. Reverse area magnitude (8 s to 12 s) = ½(1)(4) + (3)(4) = 14.0 m. Total distance = 66.0 + 14.0 = 80.0 m.

markScheme.criterion: Sums unsigned positive (66.0 m) and negative (14.0 m) velocity–time areas to obtain 80.0 m (D).

items.stem: Sensors record a high-speed bottling-line transfer sled initially at x = 18.0 m relative to a optical home flag. Using the velocity–time plot up to t = 16.0 s, determine its final coordinate x.
items.workedSolution: Displacement during the 16 s run equals the trapezium area: Δx = ½(16 + 8)(16) = 192 m. Final position from the optical home flag = x₀ + Δx = 18 + 192 = 210 m.

markScheme.criterion: Adds trapezium area (192 m) to initial offset (18 m) to get 210 m (C).

items.stem: The displacement–time graph records the motion of a miniature autonomous submarine along a test tank from t = 0.0 s to t = 20.0 s, including a stationary dwell and a final return stage from t = 12.0 s to t = 20.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Maximum displacement at the plateau = 56.0 m. (b) Return-stage velocity = (24 − 56) / (20 − 12) = -4.00 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Reads plateau displacement = 56.0 m.
Uses gradient formula Δs / Δt = (24 − 56) / (20 − 12).
Retains negative sign for motion back toward the origin.
Obtains -4.00 m s⁻¹.

workingSteps: Velocity equals the gradient Δs / Δt of the s–t graph.

items.stem: Moving upward at 12.0 m s⁻¹ at t = 0.0 s, a mine hoist cage experiences the acceleration–time history plotted over 12.0 s. Find its peak speed.
items.workedSolution: Speed increases while a > 0 (from t = 0.0 s until a = 0 at t = 8 s). Positive area Δv_max = (4)(4) + ½(4)(4) = 24.0 m s⁻¹. Maximum speed = u₀ + Δv_max = 12 + 24.0 = 36.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Integrates positive acceleration up to t = 8 s (24.0 m s⁻¹) and adds 12 m s⁻¹ to get 36.0 m s⁻¹ (B).

options.distractorRationale: Integrates the positive acceleration area up to a = 0 correctly but omits the initial speed u₀.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats the entire positive acceleration region as a rectangle of height a_max, ignoring the linear ramp down to zero.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates the speed at the end of the interval (t = t_end) rather than at the instant acceleration changes sign.

items.stem: In a linear dynamics experiment, an ice-rink calibration sled of mass 2.5 kg moves in a straight line with momentum varying as shown. How much net work is done on it between t = 2.0 s and t = 7.0 s?
items.workedSolution: Using E_k = p² / (2m), net work W = ΔE_k = (15² − 5²) / (2 × 2.5) = 40.0 J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies W = (p₂² − p₁²) / (2m) = (15² − 5²) / (5) = 40.0 J (A).

items.stem: A force transducer logs a 2.5 s stator current pulse acting forward on a linear-motor launch shuttle (mass 3.0 kg), which had momentum 9.0 kg m s⁻¹ at t = 0.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Impulse J = ½(2.5 + 1.5)(36) = 72.0 N s. (b) Final momentum p_f = 9 + 72.0 = 81.0 kg m s⁻¹. (c) Speed increase Δv = 72.0 / 3 = 24.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Computes impulse from the trapezium area under the F–t curve.
Obtains J = 72.0 N s.
Adds 9 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 81.0 kg m s⁻¹.
Divides impulse from (a) by 3 kg.
Obtains Δv = 24.0 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Passing x = 0.0 m with speed 5.0 m s⁻¹, a wind-propelled land-yacht rig of mass 2.0 kg experiences the collinear resultant force plotted against displacement up to x = 16.0 m. What is its speed at x = 16.0 m?
items.workedSolution: Positive work (0 to 12 m) = ½(12 + 6)(10) = 90.0 J. Resistive work (12 m to 16 m) = −½(4)(2) = −4.00 J. Net work W = 86.0 J. From ½mv² = ½mu₀² + W, v = √(5² + 2 × 86.0 / 2) = 10.5 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Finds net work W = 86.0 J and v = √(5² + 2W/2) = 10.5 m s⁻¹ (A).

items.stem: A student calibrates a robotics compliant-joint spring up to 0.8 m compression (plotted below) before releasing it from rest against an unattached 0.6 kg puck on a horizontal air table.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies k as the gradient ΔF / Δx.
Obtains k = 90.0 N m⁻¹.
Uses triangular area ½Fx.
Obtains E_p = 28.8 J.
Equates ½(0.6)v² to stored elastic energy from (b).
Obtains v = 9.80 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: In a tensile materials test, a synthetic polyurethane tendon cord obeys Hooke's law up to a strain of 0.25 before softening up to strain 0.5, as shown on the stress–strain graph. What is the Young's modulus of the material in the initial linear region?
items.workedSolution: Up to the limit of proportionality at ε = 0.25, stress reaches 200 MPa. Young's modulus E = σ / ε = 200 / 0.25 = 800 MPa.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates initial linear gradient E = 200 / 0.25 = 800 MPa (C).

items.stem: Refer to the non-linear V–I characteristic of a carbon-filament heritage bulb. What value does its resistance take when carrying a steady current of 2.0 A?
items.workedSolution: Electrical resistance at an operating point is defined by R = V / I (not the local slope ΔV / ΔI). At I = 2 A, V = 10 V, so R = 10 / 2 = 5.00 Ω.

markScheme.criterion: Uses static ratio R = V / I = 10 / 2 = 5.00 Ω (A).

items.stem: Terminal voltage V across a vanadium redox flow single cell is logged as load current I varies from zero up to 2.0 A, producing the downward straight line below.
items.workedSolution: (a) Open-circuit intercept gives ε = 9.60 V. (b) Gradient = (4 − 9.6) / 2 = -2.80 V A⁻¹. (c) Mean terminal p.d. = ½(9.6 + 4) = 6.80 V.

markScheme.criterion: Reads ε = 9.60 V at I = 0.
Evaluates (4 − 9.6) / 2 including negative sign.
Obtains -2.80 V A⁻¹.
Uses ½(9.6 + 4) or area divided by 2 A.
Obtains 6.80 V.

items.stem: To find the resistivity ρ of a potassium-chloride electrolyte tube, total resistance R = ρ(L / A) + R₀ is plotted against L / A up to 200.0 m⁻¹. What value of ρ does the graph give?
items.workedSolution: Since R = ρ(L / A) + R₀, resistivity ρ equals the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A) = (28 − 4) / 200 = 0.120 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept R₀ = 4 Ω to obtain ρ = (28 − 4) / 200 = 0.120 Ω m (D).

items.stem: How steep (in m s⁻²) is the linear v² versus s graph recorded over 1.6 m for a steel ball bearing rolling in a V-channel with negligible rotational loss on a smooth slope (sin θ = 0.25, g = 9.8 m s⁻²)?
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 3.2 m² s⁻² and at s = 1.6 m, v² = 11.04 m² s⁻². Gradient = (11.04 − 3.2) / 1.6 = 2(9.8)(0.25) = 4.90 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 3.2 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.8 × 0.25) to get 4.90 m s⁻² (C).

items.stem: Because the force sensor has an unzeroed tare reading F₀, a student graphs total force F against r⁻² up to 25.0 m⁻² for conductive carbon spheres mounted in a dry-nitrogen force cell.
items.workedSolution: (a) At r⁻² = 0, systematic tare offset F₀ = 0.100 N. (b) Gradient = (0.85 − 0.1) / 25 = 0.0300 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Reads intercept F₀ = 0.100 N.
Evaluates ΔF = 0.85 − 0.1 using intercept from (a).
Divides ΔF by 25 m⁻² and states correct unit N m².
Obtains 0.0300 N m².

items.stem: Inspect the steepest error-bar line of worst fit plotted from 1.0 A to 6.0 A for a Helmholtz-coil axial field check. What value does its gradient take?
items.workedSolution: At x₁ = 1 A, y₁ = 3 mT; at x₂ = 6 A, y₂ = 22 mT. Worst-fit gradient m_worst = (22 − 3) / (6 − 1) = 3.80 mT A⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δy / Δx = (22 − 3) / (6 − 1) = 3.80 mT A⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: A data logger records the signed velocity of an autonomous harbour mooring buggy moving along a straight quay rail (southward positive) over a 20.0 s cycle, with constant braking and reversal applied between t = 10.0 s and t = 15.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Zero-velocity crossing is at t = 13 s. Positive area = 114 m and unsigned negative area = 48.0 m, giving total distance = 162 m. (b) Net displacement = 114 − 48.0 = 66.0 m; average velocity = 66.0 / 20 = 3.30 m s⁻¹. (c) Acceleration = (−8 − 12) / (15 − 10) = -4.00 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Finds zero-crossing t = 13 s and evaluates both unsigned areas (114 m and 48.0 m).
Obtains total distance = 162 m.
Subtracts areas for net displacement (66.0 m) and divides by 20 s.
Obtains average velocity = 3.30 m s⁻¹.
Obtains acceleration = -4.00 m s⁻² including negative sign.

workingSteps: Velocity crosses zero at t = 13 s; forward area = 114 m.
Unsigned reverse area = 48.0 m, so total distance = 114 + 48.0 = 162 m.

parts.prompt: Determine the net displacement and hence calculate the average velocity over the 20.0 s interval.
workingSteps: Average velocity = Δs / Δt = 66.0 / 20 = 3.30 m s⁻¹.

parts.prompt: Calculate the acceleration between t = 10.0 s and t = 15.0 s.

items.stem: Examine the 20.0 s velocity–time curve for a wind-tunnel moving-ground carriage (initial coordinate 35.0 m from the nozzle datum line). What mean speed is achieved during this movement?
items.workedSolution: Distance travelled Δx = ½(20 + 8)(20) = 280 m (independent of the 35 m starting offset). Mean speed = 280 / 20 = 14.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Divides trapezium distance (280 m) by 20 s to obtain 14.0 m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: From the final segment (8.0 s to 16.0 s) of the displacement–time graph for a motorized diffraction-slit carriage on an optical rail, calculate the velocity.
items.workedSolution: From t = 8 s to t = 16 s, displacement changes from 46 m to 22 m. Velocity v = (22 − 46) / (16 − 8) = -3.00 m s⁻¹.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates speed |Δs / Δt| correctly but omits the negative sign indicating motion back toward the origin.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Divides Δs by the final timestamp t₃ instead of the stage duration (t₃ − t₂).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Reads only the final displacement s₂ and fails to subtract the plateau displacement s₁.

items.stem: During a 12.0 s test run, a vertical-launch sounding sled enters the instrumented section moving upward at 10.0 m s⁻¹. Its subsequent signed acceleration–time trace is shown.
items.workedSolution: (a) Maximum speed occurs when acceleration crosses zero from positive to negative at t = 6.00 s. (b) Positive area = 24.0 m s⁻¹, giving v_max = 10 + 24.0 = 34.0 m s⁻¹. (c) Negative area magnitude = 15.0 m s⁻¹, so v_final = 34.0 − 15.0 = 19.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: States t = 6.00 s.
Evaluates positive area up to 6 s (24.0 m s⁻¹) and adds u₀ = 10 m s⁻¹.
Obtains v_max = 34.0 m s⁻¹.
Subtracts negative area (15.0 m s⁻¹) from v_max.
Obtains final velocity = 19.0 m s⁻¹.

parts.prompt: Calculate this maximum speed.
Calculate the velocity at t = 12.0 s.
workingSteps: Magnitude of negative a–t area (6 s to 12 s) = ½(2)(3) + (4)(3) = 15.0 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Motion sensors track the momentum of a linear air-bearing carriage of mass 1.6 kg. Determine the magnitude of the resultant force acting from t = 3.0 s to t = 8.0 s.
items.workedSolution: By Newton's second law, F = Δp / Δt = (11.2 − 3.2) / (8 − 3) = 1.60 N.

items.stem: Moving in a straight line with initial momentum 3.6 kg m s⁻¹, a microgravity cargo pod (mass 1.2 kg) undergoes the 1.0 s docking vernier firing shown. What is its final momentum at t = 1.0 s?
items.workedSolution: Impulse Δp = ½(1 + 0.4)(30) = 21.0 N s. Final momentum p_f = p₀ + Δp = 3.6 + 21.0 = 24.6 kg m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Adds impulse (21.0 N s) to p₀ = 3.6 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 24.6 kg m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: At x = 0.0 m, an automated mining skip of mass 4.0 kg moves in the positive x-direction at 3.5 m s⁻¹. The graph shows the resultant force acting along its line of motion from x = 0.0 m to x = 10.0 m.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates positive (144 J) and negative (−8.00 J) areas.
Obtains net work W = 136 J.
Uses ½mv² = ½(4)(3.5²) + W.
Obtains v = 8.96 m s⁻¹.
Divides net work by 10 m to get 13.6 N.

items.stem: Stress–strain data for a high-density polyethylene filament are plotted up to strain 0.8, showing an initial Hookean region from 0.0 to strain 0.4 followed by reduced stiffness.
items.workedSolution: (a) Young's modulus E = 140 / 0.4 = 350 MPa. (b) Energy per unit volume = ½(0.4)(140) + ½(140 + 200)(0.4) = 96.0 MJ m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates initial gradient σ / ε up to ε = 0.4.
Obtains E = 350 MPa.
Identifies work per unit volume as total area under the σ–ε graph.
Splits area into initial triangle plus upper trapezium.
Obtains 96.0 MJ m⁻³.

Calculate the work done per unit volume in stretching the specimen from zero strain to 0.8.

items.stem: In a DC bench test, a platinum-wire hot-wire anemometer element exhibits the V–I graph shown up to 2.0 A. Evaluate its electrical resistance R = V / I when I = 2.0 A.
items.workedSolution: Electrical resistance at an operating point is defined by R = V / I (not the local slope ΔV / ΔI). At I = 2 A, V = 16 V, so R = 16 / 2 = 8.00 Ω.

markScheme.criterion: Uses static ratio R = V / I = 16 / 2 = 8.00 Ω (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the local segment gradient ΔV / ΔI instead of the static ratio V / I defining electrical resistance.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the ratio to I / V (conductance in S) rather than V / I.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates the low-current resistance near the origin rather than at the specified operating current.

items.stem: By varying a rheostat connected to a lead-acid laboratory accumulator, terminal voltage V is graphed against current I up to 4.0 A. Find the signed slope ΔV / ΔI.
items.workedSolution: At I = 0.0 A, V = ε = 14 V; at I = 4 A, V = 4 V. Gradient = (4 − 14) / 4 = -2.50 V A⁻¹ (equal to −r).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates (4 − 14) / 4 = -2.50 V A⁻¹ (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Assumes the line meets V = 0 at I = I_max instead of reading the non-zero terminal voltage V(I_max).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Inverts ΔI / ΔV instead of computing ΔV / ΔI.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates internal resistance r = |ΔV / ΔI| but omits the negative sign of the downward V–I gradient.

items.stem: Two-terminal ohmmeter data R for a doped silicon bar of varying dimensions are graphed versus L / A from 0.0 m⁻¹ to 100.0 m⁻¹ as shown below.
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical intercept R₀ = 2.00 Ω. (b) Resistivity ρ = (18 − 2) / 100 = 0.160 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: States R₀ = 2.00 Ω.
Identifies ρ with the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A).
Subtracts R₀ = 2 Ω from 18 Ω before dividing by 100 m⁻¹.
Obtains ρ = 0.160 Ω m.

workingSteps: From R = ρ(L / A) + R₀, ρ equals the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A).

items.stem: Examine the straight-line plot of v² against track distance s up to 2.0 m for an optical-interruptor sled coasting down an inclined bench (ramp sin θ = 0.4, g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Evaluate its gradient.
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 4 m² s⁻² and at s = 2 m, v² = 19.696 m² s⁻². Gradient = (19.696 − 4) / 2 = 2(9.81)(0.4) = 7.85 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 4 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.81 × 0.4) to get 7.85 m s⁻² (C).

items.stem: Varying centre-to-centre separation up to r⁻² = 40.0 m⁻² for charged graphite-coated spheres on a quartz-fibre force sensor yields the linear F versus r⁻² trace shown. Evaluate the slope ΔF / Δ(r⁻²).
items.workedSolution: At r⁻² = 0.0 m⁻², tare offset F₀ = 0.2 N; at r⁻² = 40 m⁻², F = 1.2 N. Gradient = (1.2 − 0.2) / 40 = 0.0250 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts tare offset F₀ = 0.2 N to get (1.2 − 0.2) / 40 = 0.0250 N m² (A).

items.stem: The plotted line represents the shallowest acceptable worst-fit gradient spanning 2.0 m to 12.0 m in a simple-pendulum linearization study.
items.workedSolution: (a) At 12 m, y₂ = 36.0 s². (b) Worst-fit gradient = (36 − 8) / (12 − 2) = 2.80 s² m⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Reads y₂ = 36.0 s².
Reads y₁ = 8 s² at x₁ = 2 m and forms Δy / Δx.
Subtracts x₁ = 2 m in the denominator (12 − 2).

items.stem: Between t = 6.0 s and t = 10.0 s, a reverse thrust acts on a drop-tower counterbalance carriage inside a vertical guide shaft. Determine the acceleration indicated by the velocity–time plot.
items.workedSolution: Between t = 6 s and t = 10 s, velocity changes from +9 m s⁻¹ to −3 m s⁻¹. Acceleration a = Δv / Δt = (−3 − 9) / (10 − 6) = -3.00 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δv / Δt = (−3 − 9) / (4) = -3.00 m s⁻² (D).

options.distractorRationale: Computes the slope magnitude accurately but omits the negative sign of the acceleration.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses v_pos − |v_neg| instead of (−v_neg − v_pos) for Δv across the zero-velocity axis.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Divides the velocity change by t₃ rather than the elapsed stage duration (t₃ − t₂).

items.stem: Starting at x = 22.0 m from a concourse datum post, an inter-terminal airport monorail completes the 10.0 s journey shown on the velocity–time graph, braking uniformly from t = 8.0 s to t = 10.0 s. What is its acceleration during braking?
items.workedSolution: During braking from t = 8 s to t = 10 s, a = (0 − 15) / (10 − 8) = -7.50 m s⁻².

options.label: C

items.stem: Position measurements of an ultrasonic rangefinder target cart moving on an air track over a 15.0 s run are plotted on the displacement–time axes shown, with return travel occurring between t = 9.0 s and t = 15.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Maximum displacement at the plateau = 45.0 m. (b) Return-stage velocity = (15 − 45) / (15 − 9) = -5.00 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Reads plateau displacement = 45.0 m.
Uses gradient formula Δs / Δt = (15 − 45) / (15 − 9).
Retains negative sign for motion back toward the origin.
Obtains -5.00 m s⁻¹.

workingSteps: The plateau on the displacement–time graph reaches 45.0 m.

parts.prompt: Calculate the signed velocity between t = 9.0 s and t = 15.0 s.
workingSteps: Velocity equals the gradient Δs / Δt of the s–t graph.

items.stem: After passing t = 0.0 s with downrange speed 11.0 m s⁻¹, a railgun armature test sled experiences the 15.0 s acceleration curve plotted. Determine its final velocity at t = 15.0 s.
items.workedSolution: Positive a–t area (0 to 8 s) = 52.0 m s⁻¹; negative area magnitude (8 s to 15 s) = 24.0 m s⁻¹. Net Δv = 52.0 − 24.0 = 28.0 m s⁻¹. Final velocity = 11 + (28.0) = 39.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Combines net signed area (28.0 m s⁻¹) with u₀ = 11 m s⁻¹ to obtain 39.0 m s⁻¹ (C).

options.distractorRationale: Stops integrating when acceleration reaches zero and ignores the subsequent negative-acceleration stage.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes net velocity change Δv from the signed area but forgets to add the initial velocity u₀.

options.label: D

items.stem: Data loggers record the linear momentum of an air-track glider (mass 0.6 kg), which experiences a constant resultant force between t = 2.0 s and t = 5.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Resultant force F = Δp / Δt = (4.8 − 1.2) / (5 − 2) = 1.20 N. (b) Net work W = ΔE_k = (4.8² − 1.2²) / (2 × 0.6) = 18.0 J.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies resultant force as gradient Δp / Δt of the p–t graph.
Obtains F = 1.20 N.
Relates net work to ΔE_k = (p₂² − p₁²) / (2m).
Substitutes p₁ = 1.2 kg m s⁻¹, p₂ = 4.8 kg m s⁻¹, and m = 0.6 kg.
Obtains W = 18.0 J.

items.stem: During a 5.0 s cold-gas thruster burn, a cold-gas attitude probe (mass 6.0 kg, initial momentum 18.0 kg m s⁻¹) experiences the force–time profile shown. What is the time-averaged resultant force over the 5.0 s interval?
items.workedSolution: Total impulse J = ½(5 + 3)(30) = 120 N s. Mean force F_mean = J / Δt = 120 / 5 = 24.0 N.

markScheme.criterion: Divides impulse (120 N s) by 5 s to obtain 24.0 N (B).

items.stem: A 3.2 kg unit (an instrumented crash-test carriage) enters an instrumented zone at 2.0 m s⁻¹. From the resultant force–displacement graph over 14.0 m, calculate its exit speed at x = 14.0 m.
items.workedSolution: Positive work (0 to 11 m) = ½(11 + 6)(16) = 136 J. Resistive work (11 m to 14 m) = −½(3)(4) = −6.00 J. Net work W = 130 J. From ½mv² = ½mu₀² + W, v = √(2² + 2 × 130 / 3.2) = 9.23 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Finds net work W = 130 J and v = √(2² + 2W/3.2) = 9.23 m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: On a horizontal frictionless bench, a linear valve return spring is compressed by 0.4 m according to the force–compression graph shown and released from rest to propel a 0.22 kg block. What launch speed does the block acquire?
items.workedSolution: Elastic energy stored E_p = ½(44)(0.4) = 8.80 J. Equating ½mv² = E_p gives v = √(2 × 8.80 / 0.22) = 8.94 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Sets ½(0.22)v² = 8.80 J to obtain v = 8.94 m s⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: The tensile stress–strain curve for an extruded fluoropolymer ribbon is linear from 0.0 to strain 0.5 and reaches strain 1.0. Determine the Young's modulus in MPa.
items.workedSolution: Up to the limit of proportionality at ε = 0.5, stress reaches 250 MPa. Young's modulus E = σ / ε = 250 / 0.5 = 500 MPa.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates initial linear gradient E = 250 / 0.5 = 500 MPa (D).

items.stem: The terminal potential difference V of a zinc-carbon dry cell decreases linearly with load current I from 0.0 A to 1.0 A, as shown. What is the mean terminal potential difference across this current range?
items.workedSolution: Terminal p.d. varies linearly from 4.5 V at I = 0.0 A to 1.5 V at I = 1 A, so V_mean = ½(4.5 + 1.5) = 3.00 V.

markScheme.criterion: Averages endpoint voltages ½(4.5 + 1.5) = 3.00 V (B).

items.stem: Two-wire resistance readings R across a carbon-loaded antistatic composite bar include a fixed fixture offset R₀ when graphed against L / A from zero to 250.0 m⁻¹. Evaluate the resistivity ρ in Ω m.
items.workedSolution: Since R = ρ(L / A) + R₀, resistivity ρ equals the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A) = (35 − 5) / 250 = 0.120 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept R₀ = 5 Ω to obtain ρ = (35 − 5) / 250 = 0.120 Ω m (C).

markScheme.criterion: Reads intercept u₀² = 2.50 m² s⁻².
Forms gradient (17.2 − 2.5) / 2.5.
Subtracts non-zero intercept u₀² accurately.
Obtains 5.88 m s⁻².

items.stem: Subtracting the constant zero-offset intercept on the F versus r⁻² plot (0.0 m⁻² to 80.0 m⁻²) for nickel-plated hollow spheres suspended over an analytical balance, find the gradient in N m².
items.workedSolution: At r⁻² = 0.0 m⁻², tare offset F₀ = 0.4 N; at r⁻² = 80 m⁻², F = 2 N. Gradient = (2 − 0.4) / 80 = 0.0200 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts tare offset F₀ = 0.4 N to get (2 − 0.4) / 80 = 0.0200 N m² (B).

items.stem: Error-bar bounds at 0.4 mW and 2.0 mW define the steepest acceptable line in an optical photodiode irradiance calibration. Evaluate the slope of this worst-fit line.
items.workedSolution: At x₁ = 0.4 mW, y₁ = 1 μA; at x₂ = 2 mW, y₂ = 6.6 μA. Worst-fit gradient m_worst = (6.6 − 1) / (2 − 0.4) = 3.50 μA mW⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δy / Δx = (6.6 − 1) / (2 − 0.4) = 3.50 μA mW⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: In a laboratory motion trial, a seismic actuator test sled travels on a low-friction hydraulic guide with in the positive x-direction taken as positive. The velocity–time graph records its motion from t = 0.0 s to t = 20.0 s, including uniform reversal thrust from t = 10.0 s to t = 15.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Zero-velocity crossing is at t = 13.75 s. Positive area = 141 m and unsigned negative area = 28.1 m, giving total distance = 169 m. (b) Net displacement = 141 − 28.1 = 113 m; average velocity = 113 / 20 = 5.63 m s⁻¹. (c) Acceleration = (−5 − 15) / (15 − 10) = -4.00 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Finds zero-crossing t = 13.75 s and evaluates both unsigned areas (141 m and 28.1 m).
Obtains total distance = 169 m.
Subtracts areas for net displacement (113 m) and divides by 20 s.
Obtains average velocity = 5.63 m s⁻¹.
Obtains acceleration = -4.00 m s⁻² including negative sign.

parts.prompt: Calculate the total distance travelled between t = 0.0 s and t = 20.0 s.
workingSteps: Velocity crosses zero at t = 13.75 s; forward area = 141 m.
Unsigned reverse area = 28.1 m, so total distance = 141 + 28.1 = 169 m.

parts.prompt: Determine the net displacement and hence calculate the average velocity over the 20.0 s interval.
workingSteps: Average velocity = Δs / Δt = 113 / 20 = 5.63 m s⁻¹.

parts.prompt: Calculate the acceleration between t = 10.0 s and t = 15.0 s.

items.stem: At t = 0.0 s, a linear-induction baggage carrier is stationary at a position 28.0 m ahead of a sorting-hall origin sensor. It then moves forward along a straight guideway according to the velocity–time graph for 16.0 s. What is its final distance from the sorting-hall origin sensor at t = 16.0 s?
items.workedSolution: Displacement during the 16 s run equals the trapezium area: Δx = ½(16 + 7)(12) = 138 m. Final position from the sorting-hall origin sensor = x₀ + Δx = 28 + 138 = 166 m.

markScheme.criterion: Adds trapezium area (138 m) to initial offset (28 m) to get 166 m (B).

items.stem: The displacement–time graph shows a laser-tracked precision stage moving on a metrology rail from t = 0.0 s to t = 20.0 s. What is its velocity during the initial stage from t = 0.0 s to t = 5.0 s?
items.workedSolution: At t = 0.0 s, s₀ = 20 m; at t = 5 s, s₁ = 65 m. Velocity v = Δs / Δt = (65 − 20) / 5 = 9.00 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts initial position s₀ = 20 m to obtain v = (65 − 20) / 5 = 9.00 m s⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: Engineers monitor a drop-shaft recovery gondola for 12.0 s starting from an initial upward velocity of 14.0 m s⁻¹ at t = 0.0 s, obtaining the piecewise acceleration–time graph below.
items.workedSolution: (a) Maximum speed occurs when acceleration crosses zero from positive to negative at t = 6.00 s. (b) Positive area = 36.0 m s⁻¹, giving v_max = 14 + 36.0 = 50.0 m s⁻¹. (c) Negative area magnitude = 18.0 m s⁻¹, so v_final = 50.0 − 18.0 = 32.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: States t = 6.00 s.
Evaluates positive area up to 6 s (36.0 m s⁻¹) and adds u₀ = 14 m s⁻¹.
Obtains v_max = 50.0 m s⁻¹.
Subtracts negative area (18.0 m s⁻¹) from v_max.
Obtains final velocity = 32.0 m s⁻¹.

parts.prompt: Calculate this maximum speed.
Calculate the velocity at t = 12.0 s.
workingSteps: Magnitude of negative a–t area (6 s to 12 s) = ½(3)(4) + (3)(4) = 18.0 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: The graph displays the linear momentum of a frictionless puck on an air table (mass 3.0 kg) against time. What resultant force acts on it between t = 4.0 s and t = 10.0 s?
items.workedSolution: By Newton's second law, F = Δp / Δt = (18 − 6) / (10 − 4) = 2.00 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F = Δp / Δt = (18 − 6) / (6) = 2.00 N (C).

items.stem: Having initial forward momentum 8.0 kg m s⁻¹, a crash-barrier test sled of mass 2.0 kg experiences a collinear hydraulic arrester pulse over 2.0 s as shown on the force–time graph. What is its change in speed Δv?
items.workedSolution: Impulse J = area under F–t trapezium = ½(2 + 1)(25) = 37.5 N s. Speed increase Δv = J / m = 37.5 / 2 = 18.8 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Computes J = 37.5 N s and Δv = J / 2 = 18.8 m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: Force-transducer and encoder data for a pneumatic factory transfer cart (mass 5.0 kg, speed 4.0 m s⁻¹ at x = 0.0 m) are plotted over a 20.0 m straight track.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates positive (276 J) and negative (−12.0 J) areas.
Obtains net work W = 264 J.
Uses ½mv² = ½(5)(4²) + W.
Obtains v = 11.0 m s⁻¹.
Divides net work by 20 m to get 13.2 N.

items.stem: A nuclear physics experiment tracks a gallium radiopharmaceutical ampoule via an ionization well chamber and fits a straight line to ln(C / s⁻¹) against t from 0.0 s to 100.0 s. Evaluate the signed gradient of this line.
items.workedSolution: At t = 0.0 s, ln C₀ = 8; at t = 100 s, ln C = 2. Gradient = (2 − 8) / 100 = -0.0600 s⁻¹.

items.stem: During a mechanics practical, a beryllium-copper instrument spring follows the linear force–compression trace up to 1.0 m and subsequently accelerates a 0.5 kg block from rest across a frictionless bench.
items.workedSolution: (a) k = 90 / 1 = 90.0 N m⁻¹. (b) Elastic energy E_p = ½(90)(1) = 45.0 J. (c) Launch speed v = √(2(45.0)/0.5) = 13.4 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies k as the gradient ΔF / Δx.
Obtains k = 90.0 N m⁻¹.
Uses triangular area ½Fx.
Obtains E_p = 45.0 J.
Equates ½(0.5)v² to stored elastic energy from (b).
Obtains v = 13.4 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: The stress–strain graph shows a synthetic polyurethane tendon cord stretched reversibly through two piecewise-linear stages up to strain 0.6 (kink at strain 0.3). What work is done per unit volume in stretching the specimen to strain 0.6?
items.workedSolution: Work per unit volume equals area under the σ–ε graph (1 MPa × 1 = 1 MJ m⁻³): u = ½(0.3)(150) + ½(150 + 210)(0.3) = 76.5 MJ m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Sums triangle and trapezium areas under σ–ε curve to obtain 76.5 MJ m⁻³ (D).

items.stem: How many ohms of static resistance does a silicon-carbide varistor element present when driven at a direct current of 2.4 A according to the V–I curve?
items.workedSolution: Electrical resistance at an operating point is defined by R = V / I (not the local slope ΔV / ΔI). At I = 2.4 A, V = 14.4 V, so R = 14.4 / 2.4 = 6.00 Ω.

markScheme.criterion: Uses static ratio R = V / I = 14.4 / 2.4 = 6.00 Ω (B).
