items.stem: During an electrical power-source practical, a silver-oxide instrument battery is discharged through a stepped load up to 5.0 A, yielding the V–I graph shown.
items.workedSolution: (a) Open-circuit intercept gives ε = 24.0 V. (b) Gradient = (9 − 24) / 5 = -3.00 V A⁻¹. (c) Mean terminal p.d. = ½(24 + 9) = 16.5 V.

markScheme.criterion: Reads ε = 24.0 V at I = 0.
Evaluates (9 − 24) / 5 including negative sign.
Obtains -3.00 V A⁻¹.
Uses ½(24 + 9) or area divided by 5 A.
Obtains 16.5 V.

items.stem: In a materials conductivity test on a potassium-chloride electrolyte tube, measured resistance R varies linearly with L / A up to 400.0 m⁻¹ as shown. Extract the bulk resistivity ρ.
items.workedSolution: Since R = ρ(L / A) + R₀, resistivity ρ equals the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A) = (30 − 6) / 400 = 0.0600 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept R₀ = 6 Ω to obtain ρ = (30 − 6) / 400 = 0.0600 Ω m (B).

items.stem: An optical timer measures speed v of a steel ball bearing rolling in a V-channel with negligible rotational loss at positions up to s = 2.0 m along a frictionless incline (sin θ = 0.2, g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What is the slope of the resulting v²–s graph?
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 1.2 m² s⁻² and at s = 2 m, v² = 9.048 m² s⁻². Gradient = (9.048 − 1.2) / 2 = 2(9.81)(0.2) = 3.92 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 1.2 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.81 × 0.2) to get 3.92 m s⁻² (D).

items.stem: The straight-line plot below displays measured force F versus inverse-square separation r⁻² (0.0 m⁻² to 50.0 m⁻²) for charged copper electrodes on a laser-deflection cantilever.
items.workedSolution: (a) At r⁻² = 0, systematic tare offset F₀ = 0.300 N. (b) Gradient = (1.5 − 0.3) / 50 = 0.0240 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Reads intercept F₀ = 0.300 N.
Evaluates ΔF = 1.5 − 0.3 using intercept from (a).
Divides ΔF by 50 m⁻² and states correct unit N m².
Obtains 0.0240 N m².

items.stem: In a Helmholtz-coil axial field check, how large is the gradient of the steepest worst-fit line spanning 5.0 A to 25.0 A on the axes shown?
items.workedSolution: At x₁ = 5 A, y₁ = 15 mT; at x₂ = 25 A, y₂ = 71 mT. Worst-fit gradient m_worst = (71 − 15) / (25 − 5) = 2.80 mT A⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δy / Δx = (71 − 15) / (25 − 5) = 2.80 mT A⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: On a straight test section, an automated rail inspection trolley moves along a straight viaduct rail (eastward positive) as shown on the velocity–time graph. What is its net displacement from t = 0.0 s to t = 10.0 s?
items.workedSolution: Velocity reaches zero at t = 7 s. Positive area = 80.0 m and area below the axis has magnitude 20.0 m. Net displacement = 80.0 − 20.0 = 60.0 m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts reverse area (20.0 m) from forward area (80.0 m) to obtain 60.0 m (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Adds the magnitude of the negative-velocity area instead of subtracting it, finding total distance rather than net displacement.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies half the difference of terminal speeds by total time, ignoring the piecewise plateau durations.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Finds the maximum forward displacement at the turning point and ignores the subsequent reverse motion.

items.stem: At t = 0.0 s, a canal lock towing locomotive rests at a position 25.0 m ahead of a lock-gate reference mark. The velocity–time graph shows its forward motion over 10.0 s, with uniform braking applied from t = 7.0 s until t = 10.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Trapezium area Δx = ½(10 + 5)(16) = 120 m. (b) Final distance from datum = 25 + 120 = 145 m. (c) Mean speed = 120 / 10 = 12.0 m s⁻¹. (d) Braking acceleration = (0 − 16) / (10 − 7) = -5.33 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Identifies distance travelled as the area under the v–t trapezium.
Obtains Δx = 120 m.
Adds 25 m offset to obtain 145 m.
Divides distance travelled from (a) by 10 s.
Obtains mean speed = 12.0 m s⁻¹.
Obtains braking acceleration = -5.33 m s⁻².

parts.prompt: Calculate the distance travelled during the 10.0 s journey.
workingSteps: Distance equals the trapezium area under the v–t curve.

Determine the mean speed over the 10.0 s run.
Calculate the acceleration between t = 7.0 s and t = 10.0 s.

items.stem: A sensor records the displacement–time graph of an automated pharmacy courier pod along a straight chute. What is its signed velocity during the return stage between t = 7.0 s and t = 12.0 s?
items.workedSolution: From t = 7 s to t = 12 s, displacement changes from 34 m to 15 m. Velocity v = (15 − 34) / (12 − 7) = -3.80 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: How fast is a high-rise express lift travelling at its instant of greatest speed during the 16.0 s acceleration–time record shown, given an initial upward velocity of 9.0 m s⁻¹?
items.workedSolution: Speed increases while a > 0 (from t = 0.0 s until a = 0 at t = 10 s). Positive area Δv_max = (4)(5) + ½(6)(5) = 35.0 m s⁻¹. Maximum speed = u₀ + Δv_max = 9 + 35.0 = 44.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Integrates positive acceleration up to t = 10 s (35.0 m s⁻¹) and adds 9 m s⁻¹ to get 44.0 m s⁻¹ (A).

items.stem: Along a horizontal guideway, a magnetic rail cart of mass 1.0 kg moves in a fixed direction. Its momentum–time graph shows an impulse stage from t = 2.0 s to t = 6.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Resultant force F = Δp / Δt = (9 − 3) / (6 − 2) = 1.50 N. (b) Net work W = ΔE_k = (9² − 3²) / (2 × 1) = 36.0 J.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies resultant force as gradient Δp / Δt of the p–t graph.
Obtains F = 1.50 N.
Relates net work to ΔE_k = (p₂² − p₁²) / (2m).
Substitutes p₁ = 3 kg m s⁻¹, p₂ = 9 kg m s⁻¹, and m = 1 kg.
Obtains W = 36.0 J.

items.stem: Before a 0.8 s solenoid kicker stroke, a robotic soccer puck of mass 2.0 kg has momentum 6.0 kg m s⁻¹. Using the force–time plot, find its momentum immediately after the pulse.
items.workedSolution: Impulse Δp = ½(0.8 + 0.4)(50) = 30.0 N s. Final momentum p_f = p₀ + Δp = 6 + 30.0 = 36.0 kg m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Adds impulse (30.0 N s) to p₀ = 6 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 36.0 kg m s⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: The resultant force in the direction of motion of a magnetic-launch coaster bogie (mass 2.0 kg, initial speed 5.0 m s⁻¹) is plotted over 10.0 m. Determine its speed at x = 10.0 m.
items.workedSolution: Positive work (0 to 8 m) = ½(8 + 4)(12) = 72.0 J. Resistive work (8 m to 10 m) = −½(2)(4) = −4.00 J. Net work W = 68.0 J. From ½mv² = ½mu₀² + W, v = √(5² + 2 × 68.0 / 2) = 9.64 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Finds net work W = 68.0 J and v = √(5² + 2W/2) = 9.64 m s⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: Over 20.0 s, a Geiger–Müller tube after background subtraction records the decay of a short-lived barium isomer source; the resulting linearized trace of ln(C / s⁻¹) versus t is displayed.
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical intercept at t = 0 is ln(C₀ / s⁻¹) = 7.80. (b) Gradient = (3.4 − 7.8) / 20 = -0.220 s⁻¹ (which equals −λ).

markScheme.criterion: Reads vertical intercept = 7.80.
Uses large triangle (3.4 − 7.8) / 20.
Includes negative sign and unit s⁻¹.
Obtains gradient = -0.220 s⁻¹.

items.stem: Determine the spring constant k of a laboratory catapult tension spring from the linear force–extension graph recorded up to 0.4 m.
items.workedSolution: Spring constant k = gradient ΔF / Δx = 52 / 0.4 = 130 N m⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates gradient k = 52 / 0.4 = 130 N m⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: Refer to the tensile stress–strain plot for a braided aramid-polymer composite tape, whose limit of proportionality lies at strain 0.2. Calculate its initial Young's modulus.
items.workedSolution: Up to the limit of proportionality at ε = 0.2, stress reaches 150 MPa. Young's modulus E = σ / ε = 150 / 0.2 = 750 MPa.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates initial linear gradient E = 150 / 0.2 = 750 MPa (B).

items.stem: During a component-characterization lab, a carbon-filament heritage bulb is tested up to I = 2.5 A, yielding the non-linear V–I graph shown.
items.workedSolution: (a) At I = 2.5 A, V = 15.0 V. (b) Static resistance R = V / I = 15 / 2.5 = 6.00 Ω (the upper segment gradient 8.67 Ω is ΔV / ΔI, not R).

markScheme.criterion: Reads V = 15.0 V at I = 2.5 A.
Selects R = V / I rather than local segment gradient ΔV / ΔI.
Substitutes V = 15 V and I = 2.5 A.
Obtains R = 6.00 Ω.

items.stem: A variable load resistor is connected across a lead-acid laboratory accumulator, and the terminal potential difference V is plotted against current I up to 2.0 A. According to V = ε − Ir, what is the signed gradient of this graph?
items.workedSolution: At I = 0.0 A, V = ε = 7 V; at I = 2 A, V = 3.4 V. Gradient = (3.4 − 7) / 2 = -1.80 V A⁻¹ (equal to −r).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates (3.4 − 7) / 2 = -1.80 V A⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: Because clamping electrodes introduce a fixed series resistance R₀, a researcher plots R against L / A up to 80.0 m⁻¹ for an isotropic graphite heating element.
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical intercept R₀ = 3.00 Ω. (b) Resistivity ρ = (19 − 3) / 80 = 0.200 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: States R₀ = 3.00 Ω.
Identifies ρ with the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A).
Subtracts R₀ = 3 Ω from 19 Ω before dividing by 80 m⁻¹.
Obtains ρ = 0.200 Ω m.

parts.prompt: State the systematic lead and contact resistance R₀.
workingSteps: At L / A = 0.0 m⁻¹, the vertical intercept gives R₀ = 3.00 Ω.

parts.prompt: Determine the resistivity ρ of an isotropic graphite heating element from the graph.
workingSteps: From R = ρ(L / A) + R₀, ρ equals the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A).

items.stem: Using two light gates in a gravitational field g = 9.8 m s⁻², a student records speed v of an optical-interruptor sled coasting down an inclined bench (inclination sin θ = 0.15) after passing an initial gate at s = 0.0 m with speed u₀ > 0, plotting v² against distance s up to 4.0 m. According to v² = u₀² + 2as, what is the gradient Δ(v²) / Δs of the line?
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 1.6 m² s⁻² and at s = 4 m, v² = 13.36 m² s⁻². Gradient = (13.36 − 1.6) / 4 = 2(9.8)(0.15) = 2.94 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 1.6 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.8 × 0.15) to get 2.94 m s⁻² (B).

items.stem: How large is the slope ΔF / Δ(r⁻²) of the inverse-square linearization graph recorded up to 20.0 m⁻² using charged graphite-coated spheres on a quartz-fibre force sensor?
items.workedSolution: At r⁻² = 0.0 m⁻², tare offset F₀ = 0.1 N; at r⁻² = 20 m⁻², F = 0.7 N. Gradient = (0.7 − 0.1) / 20 = 0.0300 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts tare offset F₀ = 0.1 N to get (0.7 − 0.1) / 20 = 0.0300 N m² (D).

items.stem: Uncertainty propagation in a metal-rod thermal expansion experiment is carried out graphically using the shallowest line of worst fit drawn from 2.0 K to 16.0 K.
items.workedSolution: (a) At 16 K, y₂ = 40.0 mm. (b) Worst-fit gradient = (40 − 5) / (16 − 2) = 2.50 mm K⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Reads y₂ = 40.0 mm.
Reads y₁ = 5 mm at x₁ = 2 K and forms Δy / Δx.
Subtracts x₁ = 2 K in the denominator (16 − 2).
Obtains 2.50 mm K⁻¹.

items.stem: While operating on a horizontal vacuum test guideway (to the right positive), a magnetic-levitation shuttle pod brakes and reverses direction between t = 6.0 s and t = 9.0 s. From the velocity–time graph, what is its acceleration during this interval?
items.workedSolution: Between t = 6 s and t = 9 s, velocity changes from +16 m s⁻¹ to −8 m s⁻¹. Acceleration a = Δv / Δt = (−8 − 16) / (9 − 6) = -8.00 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δv / Δt = (−8 − 16) / (3) = -8.00 m s⁻² (D).

items.stem: In the velocity–time record for a solar-powered desert research rover (initially 30.0 m from the base-camp beacon), uniform braking begins at t = 8.0 s and ends at rest at t = 12.0 s. Find the signed braking acceleration.
items.workedSolution: During braking from t = 8 s to t = 12 s, a = (0 − 14) / (12 − 8) = -3.50 m s⁻².

items.stem: The displacement–time graph records the motion of a coastal tide-gauge float along a vertical stilling tube from t = 0.0 s to t = 12.0 s, including a stationary dwell and a final return stage from t = 8.0 s to t = 12.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Maximum displacement at the plateau = 46.0 m. (b) Return-stage velocity = (18 − 46) / (12 − 8) = -7.00 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Reads plateau displacement = 46.0 m.
Uses gradient formula Δs / Δt = (18 − 46) / (12 − 8).
Retains negative sign for motion back toward the origin.
Obtains -7.00 m s⁻¹.

parts.prompt: State the maximum displacement of the object from the reference origin.
workingSteps: The plateau on the displacement–time graph reaches 46.0 m.

parts.prompt: Calculate the signed velocity between t = 8.0 s and t = 12.0 s.
workingSteps: Velocity equals the gradient Δs / Δt of the s–t graph.

items.stem: Use the signed 20.0 s acceleration–time graph to find the terminal downrange velocity of a railgun armature test sled, which starts at 13.0 m s⁻¹ when t = 0.0 s.
items.workedSolution: Positive a–t area (0 to 10 s) = 48.0 m s⁻¹; negative area magnitude (10 s to 20 s) = 15.0 m s⁻¹. Net Δv = 48.0 − 15.0 = 33.0 m s⁻¹. Final velocity = 13 + (33.0) = 46.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Combines net signed area (33.0 m s⁻¹) with u₀ = 13 m s⁻¹ to obtain 46.0 m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: Motion sensors track the momentum of a satellite attitude-test mass of mass 1.6 kg. Determine the magnitude of the resultant force acting from t = 2.0 s to t = 5.0 s.
items.workedSolution: By Newton's second law, F = Δp / Δt = (12.8 − 3.2) / (5 − 2) = 3.20 N.

items.stem: Travelling in a straight line with initial momentum 10.0 kg m s⁻¹, a rail-mounted docking target of mass 2.5 kg is acted upon by a collinear spring buffer contact for 1.0 s, as shown on the force–time graph.
items.workedSolution: (a) Impulse J = ½(1 + 0.6)(60) = 48.0 N s. (b) Final momentum p_f = 10 + 48.0 = 58.0 kg m s⁻¹. (c) Speed increase Δv = 48.0 / 2.5 = 19.2 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Computes impulse from the trapezium area under the F–t curve.
Obtains J = 48.0 N s.
Adds 10 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 58.0 kg m s⁻¹.
Divides impulse from (a) by 2.5 kg.
Obtains Δv = 19.2 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Evaluate the net work done by the resultant force on a cable-towed hydroplane model (mass 4.0 kg, initial speed 4.0 m s⁻¹) between x = 0.0 m and x = 12.0 m using the graph.
items.workedSolution: Forward work (0 to 10 m) = 120 J; resistive work (10 m to 12 m) = −4.00 J. Net work = 120 − 4.00 = 116 J.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts resistive triangle (4.00 J) from positive trapezium (120 J) to get 116 J (D).

items.stem: Static loading of a seismometer suspension spring produces the force–compression line up to 0.5 m. Held at 0.5 m compression against a 0.25 kg carriage on a smooth level guideway, it is then released.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies k as the gradient ΔF / Δx.
Obtains k = 120 N m⁻¹.
Uses triangular area ½Fx.
Obtains E_p = 15.0 J.
Equates ½(0.25)v² to stored elastic energy from (b).
Obtains v = 11.0 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Determine the strain energy stored per unit volume (in MJ m⁻³) when a thermoplastic elastomer tether is loaded from zero strain to 0.5 along the plotted stress–strain curve (proportional limit at 0.2).
items.workedSolution: Work per unit volume equals area under the σ–ε graph (1 MPa × 1 = 1 MJ m⁻³): u = ½(0.2)(190) + ½(190 + 290)(0.3) = 91.0 MJ m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Sums triangle and trapezium areas under σ–ε curve to obtain 91.0 MJ m⁻³ (B).

items.stem: At the upper plotted current I = 4.0 A, find the resistance of a tungsten filament indicator lamp from its potential difference–current characteristic.
items.workedSolution: Electrical resistance at an operating point is defined by R = V / I (not the local slope ΔV / ΔI). At I = 4 A, V = 14 V, so R = 14 / 4 = 3.50 Ω.

markScheme.criterion: Uses static ratio R = V / I = 14 / 4 = 3.50 Ω (A).

items.stem: Calibrated meters measure terminal potential difference V versus current I up to 4.0 A for a hydrogen proton-exchange fuel cell, as plotted on the axes.
items.workedSolution: (a) Open-circuit intercept gives ε = 13.0 V. (b) Gradient = (7 − 13) / 4 = -1.50 V A⁻¹. (c) Mean terminal p.d. = ½(13 + 7) = 10.0 V.

markScheme.criterion: Reads ε = 13.0 V at I = 0.
Evaluates (7 − 13) / 4 including negative sign.
Obtains -1.50 V A⁻¹.
Uses ½(13 + 7) or area divided by 4 A.
Obtains 10.0 V.

items.stem: Inspect the linear plot of measured resistance R versus L / A (spanning 0.0 m⁻¹ to 160.0 m⁻¹) for a carbon-loaded antistatic composite bar. What is the material's resistivity ρ?
items.workedSolution: Since R = ρ(L / A) + R₀, resistivity ρ equals the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A) = (20 − 4) / 160 = 0.100 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept R₀ = 4 Ω to obtain ρ = (20 − 4) / 160 = 0.100 Ω m (A).

items.stem: In a kinematics linearization lab (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²), a wheeled telemetry trolley accelerating along a tilted track on a frictionless slope with sin θ = 0.45 passes s = 0.0 m at speed u₀ and continues to s = 1.2 m. Determine the gradient of the plotted v² versus s graph.
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 2.8 m² s⁻² and at s = 1.2 m, v² = 13.3948 m² s⁻². Gradient = (13.3948 − 2.8) / 1.2 = 2(9.81)(0.45) = 8.83 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 2.8 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.81 × 0.45) to get 8.83 m s⁻² (B).

items.stem: Repulsive force data between insulated aluminium spheres monitored by a strain-gauge beam are transformed to F against r⁻² up to 60.0 m⁻², revealing a constant tare intercept.
items.workedSolution: (a) At r⁻² = 0, systematic tare offset F₀ = 0.300 N. (b) Gradient = (1.5 − 0.3) / 60 = 0.0200 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Reads intercept F₀ = 0.300 N.
Evaluates ΔF = 1.5 − 0.3 using intercept from (a).
Divides ΔF by 60 m⁻² and states correct unit N m².
Obtains 0.0200 N m².

items.workedSolution: At x₁ = 1.5 mW, y₁ = 3 μA; at x₂ = 7.5 mW, y₂ = 24 μA. Worst-fit gradient m_worst = (24 − 3) / (7.5 − 1.5) = 3.50 μA mW⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δy / Δx = (24 − 3) / (7.5 − 1.5) = 3.50 μA mW⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: In a laboratory motion trial, a robotic warehouse retrieval carriage travels along a straight aisle rail with forward taken as positive. The velocity–time graph records its motion from t = 0.0 s to t = 12.0 s, including uniform reversal thrust from t = 6.0 s to t = 10.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Zero-velocity crossing is at t = 9 s. Positive area = 108 m and unsigned negative area = 15.0 m, giving total distance = 123 m. (b) Net displacement = 108 − 15.0 = 93.0 m; average velocity = 93.0 / 12 = 7.75 m s⁻¹. (c) Acceleration = (−6 − 18) / (10 − 6) = -6.00 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Finds zero-crossing t = 9 s and evaluates both unsigned areas (108 m and 15.0 m).
Obtains total distance = 123 m.
Subtracts areas for net displacement (93.0 m) and divides by 12 s.
Obtains average velocity = 7.75 m s⁻¹.
Obtains acceleration = -6.00 m s⁻² including negative sign.

workingSteps: Velocity crosses zero at t = 9 s; forward area = 108 m.
Unsigned reverse area = 15.0 m, so total distance = 108 + 15.0 = 123 m.

parts.prompt: Determine the net displacement and hence calculate the average velocity over the 12.0 s interval.
workingSteps: Average velocity = Δs / Δt = 93.0 / 12 = 7.75 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Starting 35.0 m beyond the western end-stop at t = 0.0 s, a shipyard gantry crane crab executes the 16.0 s velocity–time profile shown. How far from the western end-stop does it come to rest?
items.workedSolution: Displacement during the 16 s run equals the trapezium area: Δx = ½(16 + 6)(19) = 209 m. Final position from the western end-stop = x₀ + Δx = 35 + 209 = 244 m.

markScheme.criterion: Adds trapezium area (209 m) to initial offset (35 m) to get 244 m (C).

items.stem: Position data for a robotic welding torch carriage on a linear gantry are plotted against time. Determine the instantaneous velocity during the outward stage between t = 0.0 s and t = 4.0 s.
items.workedSolution: At t = 0.0 s, s₀ = 14 m; at t = 4 s, s₁ = 42 m. Velocity v = Δs / Δt = (42 − 14) / 4 = 7.00 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts initial position s₀ = 14 m to obtain v = (42 − 14) / 4 = 7.00 m s⁻¹ (A).

items.stem: Passing a timing marker at t = 0.0 s with speed 5.0 m s⁻¹ downrange, a railgun armature test sled undergoes positive then negative downrange acceleration over 6.0 s as plotted.
items.workedSolution: (a) Maximum speed occurs when acceleration crosses zero from positive to negative at t = 3.00 s. (b) Positive area = 24.0 m s⁻¹, giving v_max = 5 + 24.0 = 29.0 m s⁻¹. (c) Negative area magnitude = 15.0 m s⁻¹, so v_final = 29.0 − 15.0 = 14.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: States t = 3.00 s.
Evaluates positive area up to 3 s (24.0 m s⁻¹) and adds u₀ = 5 m s⁻¹.
Obtains v_max = 29.0 m s⁻¹.
Subtracts negative area (15.0 m s⁻¹) from v_max.
Obtains final velocity = 14.0 m s⁻¹.

workingSteps: Magnitude of negative a–t area (3 s to 6 s) = ½(1)(6) + (2)(6) = 15.0 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: In a linear dynamics experiment, a superconducting levitation carrier of mass 2.4 kg moves in a straight line with momentum varying as shown. How much net work is done on it between t = 3.0 s and t = 7.0 s?
items.workedSolution: Using E_k = p² / (2m), net work W = ΔE_k = (16.8² − 4.8²) / (2 × 2.4) = 54.0 J.

items.stem: A pulsed ion-beam firing acts for 2.0 s in the direction of motion of a Hall-effect thruster test rig (mass 4.0 kg, initial momentum 12.0 kg m s⁻¹). Using the plotted force–time profile, determine Δv.
items.workedSolution: Impulse J = area under F–t trapezium = ½(2 + 1)(42) = 63.0 N s. Speed increase Δv = J / m = 63.0 / 4 = 15.8 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Computes J = 63.0 N s and Δv = J / 4 = 15.8 m s⁻¹ (A).

items.stem: At x = 0.0 m, a linear dynamo test sled of mass 2.5 kg moves in the positive x-direction at 6.0 m s⁻¹. The graph shows the resultant force acting along its line of motion from x = 0.0 m to x = 10.0 m.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates positive (82.5 J) and negative (−5.00 J) areas.
Obtains net work W = 77.5 J.
Uses ½mv² = ½(2.5)(6²) + W.
Obtains v = 9.90 m s⁻¹.
Divides net work by 10 m to get 7.75 N.

items.stem: A tensile test on an optical-mount preload spring yields the linear force–extension plot up to 0.8 m. Calculate the elastic energy stored when extended by 0.8 m.
items.workedSolution: Elastic potential energy equals the triangular area under the F–x line: E_p = ½ F x = ½(68)(0.8) = 27.2 J.

markScheme.criterion: Computes triangular area ½(68)(0.8) = 27.2 J (D).

items.stem: In a materials laboratory, uniaxial tension applied to a braided aramid-polymer composite tape yields the bilinear stress–strain trace to strain 0.5, with proportional behaviour ending at 0.25.
items.workedSolution: (a) Young's modulus E = 180 / 0.25 = 720 MPa. (b) Energy per unit volume = ½(0.25)(180) + ½(180 + 260)(0.25) = 77.5 MJ m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates initial gradient σ / ε up to ε = 0.25.
Obtains E = 720 MPa.
Identifies work per unit volume as total area under the σ–ε graph.
Splits area into initial triangle plus upper trapezium.
Obtains 77.5 MJ m⁻³.

items.stem: Voltmeter and ammeter readings for an NTC ceramic temperature-sensing disc yield the non-ohmic curve shown. Calculate the resistance of the component at 1.0 A.
items.workedSolution: Electrical resistance at an operating point is defined by R = V / I (not the local slope ΔV / ΔI). At I = 1 A, V = 6.5 V, so R = 6.5 / 1 = 6.50 Ω.

markScheme.criterion: Uses static ratio R = V / I = 6.5 / 1 = 6.50 Ω (C).

items.stem: In an internal-resistance experiment on a rechargeable nickel-cadmium pack, a student plots terminal potential difference V versus current I from 0.0 A to 2.5 A. Determine the gradient ΔV / ΔI of the line.
items.workedSolution: At I = 0.0 A, V = ε = 10 V; at I = 2.5 A, V = 4 V. Gradient = (4 − 10) / 2.5 = -2.40 V A⁻¹ (equal to −r).

items.stem: The linear graph below displays total measured resistance R against L / A (0.0 m⁻¹ to 50.0 m⁻¹) during a resistivity test on a sintered silicon-carbide heating rod.
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical intercept R₀ = 2.00 Ω. (b) Resistivity ρ = (14 − 2) / 50 = 0.240 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: States R₀ = 2.00 Ω.
Identifies ρ with the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A).
Subtracts R₀ = 2 Ω from 14 Ω before dividing by 50 m⁻¹.
Obtains ρ = 0.240 Ω m.

parts.prompt: State the systematic lead and contact resistance R₀.
workingSteps: At L / A = 0.0 m⁻¹, the vertical intercept gives R₀ = 2.00 Ω.

workingSteps: From R = ρ(L / A) + R₀, ρ equals the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A).

items.stem: Photogate data for a low-friction dynamics cart descending a tilted aluminium runway accelerating down an incline (sin θ = 0.3, g = 9.8 m s⁻²) from s = 0.0 m to s = 1.5 m are linearized by plotting v² against s. What gradient does the best-fit line have?
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 3.5 m² s⁻² and at s = 1.5 m, v² = 12.32 m² s⁻². Gradient = (12.32 − 3.5) / 1.5 = 2(9.8)(0.3) = 5.88 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 3.5 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.8 × 0.3) to get 5.88 m s⁻² (D).

items.stem: Examine the straight-line graph of balance force F against r⁻² (spanning 0.0 m⁻² to 16.0 m⁻²) for silvered glass spheres positioned above a digital load pan. What value does its gradient take?
items.workedSolution: At r⁻² = 0.0 m⁻², tare offset F₀ = 0.12 N; at r⁻² = 16 m⁻², F = 0.76 N. Gradient = (0.76 − 0.12) / 16 = 0.0400 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts tare offset F₀ = 0.12 N to get (0.76 − 0.12) / 16 = 0.0400 N m² (B).

items.stem: Refer to the shallowest worst-fit construction across 3.0 N m to 15.0 N m obtained in a torsion-wire shear stiffness practical.
items.workedSolution: (a) At 15 N m, y₂ = 42.0 rad. (b) Worst-fit gradient = (42 − 9) / (15 − 3) = 2.75 rad N⁻¹ m⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Reads y₂ = 42.0 rad.
Reads y₁ = 9 rad at x₁ = 3 N m and forms Δy / Δx.
Subtracts x₁ = 3 N m in the denominator (15 − 3).
Obtains 2.75 rad N⁻¹ m⁻¹.

items.stem: A motion sensor tracks a cable-hauled alpine service car on a straight haulage section for 10.0 s, taking uphill velocity as positive. Find the net signed displacement at t = 10.0 s relative to its starting point.
items.workedSolution: Velocity reaches zero at t = 7 s. Positive area = 54.0 m and area below the axis has magnitude 10.0 m. Net displacement = 54.0 − 10.0 = 44.0 m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts reverse area (10.0 m) from forward area (54.0 m) to obtain 44.0 m (B).

options.distractorRationale: Adds the magnitude of the negative-velocity area instead of subtracting it, finding total distance rather than net displacement.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Finds the maximum forward displacement at the turning point and ignores the subsequent reverse motion.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies half the difference of terminal speeds by total time, ignoring the piecewise plateau durations.

items.stem: Over a 8.0 s transfer starting at x = 22.0 m from the shaft loading datum, an underground mine haulage skip has the velocity–time graph shown. Calculate its average speed over the 8.0 s interval.
items.workedSolution: Distance travelled Δx = ½(8 + 4)(12) = 72.0 m (independent of the 22 m starting offset). Mean speed = 72.0 / 8 = 9.00 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Divides trapezium distance (72.0 m) by 8 s to obtain 9.00 m s⁻¹ (A).

items.stem: Position measurements of a telescope secondary-mirror actuator moving on its axial mount over a 16.0 s run are plotted on the displacement–time axes shown, with return travel occurring between t = 10.0 s and t = 16.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Maximum displacement at the plateau = 56.0 m. (b) Return-stage velocity = (28 − 56) / (16 − 10) = -4.67 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Reads plateau displacement = 56.0 m.
Uses gradient formula Δs / Δt = (28 − 56) / (16 − 10).
Retains negative sign for motion back toward the origin.
Obtains -4.67 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: From the 8.0 s acceleration–time trace for a high-rise express lift (initial upward speed 9.0 m s⁻¹), calculate the maximum speed reached before braking reduces its velocity.
items.workedSolution: Speed increases while a > 0 (from t = 0.0 s until a = 0 at t = 4 s). Positive area Δv_max = (2)(6) + ½(2)(6) = 18.0 m s⁻¹. Maximum speed = u₀ + Δv_max = 9 + 18.0 = 27.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Integrates positive acceleration up to t = 4 s (18.0 m s⁻¹) and adds 9 m s⁻¹ to get 27.0 m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: Data loggers record the linear momentum of a low-friction dynamics trolley (mass 3.0 kg), which experiences a constant resultant force between t = 2.0 s and t = 6.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Resultant force F = Δp / Δt = (18 − 6) / (6 − 2) = 3.00 N. (b) Net work W = ΔE_k = (18² − 6²) / (2 × 3) = 48.0 J.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies resultant force as gradient Δp / Δt of the p–t graph.
Obtains F = 3.00 N.
Relates net work to ΔE_k = (p₂² − p₁²) / (2m).
Substitutes p₁ = 6 kg m s⁻¹, p₂ = 18 kg m s⁻¹, and m = 3 kg.
Obtains W = 48.0 J.

items.stem: Moving in a straight line with initial momentum 4.5 kg m s⁻¹, a ballistic pendulum carriage (mass 1.5 kg) undergoes the 1.6 s controlled gas-jet pulse shown. What is its final momentum at t = 1.6 s?
items.workedSolution: Impulse Δp = ½(1.6 + 0.8)(40) = 48.0 N s. Final momentum p_f = p₀ + Δp = 4.5 + 48.0 = 52.5 kg m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Adds impulse (48.0 N s) to p₀ = 4.5 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 52.5 kg m s⁻¹ (C).

options.label: D

items.stem: Moving forward from x = 0.0 m with initial speed 5.0 m s⁻¹, a warehouse pallet shuttle (mass 5.0 kg) is subjected to the resultant force–displacement profile shown up to x = 16.0 m. How much net work is done on it over the 16.0 m displacement?
items.workedSolution: Forward work (0 to 14 m) = 200 J; resistive work (14 m to 16 m) = −5.00 J. Net work = 200 − 5.00 = 195 J.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts resistive triangle (5.00 J) from positive trapezium (200 J) to get 195 J (B).

items.stem: To verify first-order decay kinetics for a medical technetium eluted phantom, corrected count rates from a shielded NaI scintillation counter are graphed as ln(C / s⁻¹) versus time for 40.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical intercept at t = 0 is ln(C₀ / s⁻¹) = 8.60. (b) Gradient = (3.6 − 8.6) / 40 = -0.125 s⁻¹ (which equals −λ).

markScheme.criterion: Reads vertical intercept = 8.60.
Uses large triangle (3.6 − 8.6) / 40.
Includes negative sign and unit s⁻¹.
Obtains gradient = -0.125 s⁻¹.

items.stem: How many newtons per metre (k) are required to extend a laboratory catapult tension spring according to the Hookean graph spanning 0.0 m to 0.4 m?
items.workedSolution: Spring constant k = gradient ΔF / Δx = 80 / 0.4 = 200 N m⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates gradient k = 80 / 0.4 = 200 N m⁻¹ (A).

items.stem: The stress–strain graph shows a braided aramid-polymer composite tape stretched reversibly through two piecewise-linear stages up to strain 0.8 (kink at strain 0.4). What work is done per unit volume in stretching the specimen to strain 0.8?
items.workedSolution: Work per unit volume equals area under the σ–ε graph (1 MPa × 1 = 1 MJ m⁻³): u = ½(0.4)(230) + ½(230 + 320)(0.4) = 156 MJ m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Sums triangle and trapezium areas under σ–ε curve to obtain 156 MJ m⁻³ (B).

items.stem: An electronics technician logs potential difference V against current I from zero to 1.2 A across a vacuum-tube heater filament.
items.workedSolution: (a) At I = 1.2 A, V = 12.6 V. (b) Static resistance R = V / I = 12.6 / 1.2 = 10.5 Ω (the upper segment gradient 18.0 Ω is ΔV / ΔI, not R).

markScheme.criterion: Reads V = 12.6 V at I = 1.2 A.
Selects R = V / I rather than local segment gradient ΔV / ΔI.
Substitutes V = 12.6 V and I = 1.2 A.
Obtains R = 10.5 Ω.

workingSteps: Resistance is defined as the ratio R = V / I at that operating point (not ΔV / ΔI).

items.stem: Refer to the terminal potential difference–current plot for a lead-acid laboratory accumulator over 0.0 A to 1.6 A. What value does the signed slope of the best-fit line take?
items.workedSolution: At I = 0.0 A, V = ε = 5.8 V; at I = 1.6 A, V = 2.6 V. Gradient = (2.6 − 5.8) / 1.6 = -2.00 V A⁻¹ (equal to −r).

options.distractorRationale: Inverts ΔI / ΔV instead of computing ΔV / ΔI.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Assumes the line meets V = 0 at I = I_max instead of reading the non-zero terminal voltage V(I_max).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates internal resistance r = |ΔV / ΔI| but omits the negative sign of the downward V–I gradient.

items.stem: Eliminating the constant probe-lead offset from the R versus L / A graph (plotted to 400.0 m⁻¹), find the resistivity ρ of a doped silicon bar.
items.workedSolution: Since R = ρ(L / A) + R₀, resistivity ρ equals the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A) = (30 − 6) / 400 = 0.0600 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept R₀ = 6 Ω to obtain ρ = (30 − 6) / 400 = 0.0600 Ω m (D).

items.stem: Photogates spaced up to 2.0 m along a smooth slope (sin θ = 0.25, g = 9.81 m s⁻²) record a levitated neodymium shuttle descending an inclined guide, producing the linear v² versus s graph below.
items.workedSolution: (a) At s = 0.0 m, u₀² = 3.00 m² s⁻². (b) Gradient = (12.81 − 3) / 2 = 4.91 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Reads intercept u₀² = 3.00 m² s⁻².
Forms gradient (12.81 − 3) / 2.
Subtracts non-zero intercept u₀² accurately.
Obtains 4.91 m s⁻².

items.stem: To test Coulomb's inverse-square law using charged graphite-coated spheres on a quartz-fibre force sensor with an unzeroed tare offset F₀, the force reading F is plotted against inverse-square separation (r⁻²) up to 50.0 m⁻², following F = k|Q₁Q₂|r⁻² + F₀. What is the gradient k|Q₁Q₂| of the line?
items.workedSolution: At r⁻² = 0.0 m⁻², tare offset F₀ = 0.1 N; at r⁻² = 50 m⁻², F = 1.3 N. Gradient = (1.3 − 0.1) / 50 = 0.0240 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts tare offset F₀ = 0.1 N to get (1.3 − 0.1) / 50 = 0.0240 N m² (B).

items.stem: The graph displays how the velocity of a linear-motor camera dolly on a studio optical bench varies with time over 16.0 s. Positive velocity corresponds to motion northward, and direction reversal occurs during the linear ramp between t = 8.0 s and t = 12.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Zero-velocity crossing is at t = 11 s. Positive area = 90.0 m and unsigned negative area = 18.0 m, giving total distance = 108 m. (b) Net displacement = 90.0 − 18.0 = 72.0 m; average velocity = 72.0 / 16 = 4.50 m s⁻¹. (c) Acceleration = (−4 − 12) / (12 − 8) = -4.00 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Finds zero-crossing t = 11 s and evaluates both unsigned areas (90.0 m and 18.0 m).
Obtains total distance = 108 m.
Subtracts areas for net displacement (72.0 m) and divides by 16 s.
Obtains average velocity = 4.50 m s⁻¹.
Obtains acceleration = -4.00 m s⁻² including negative sign.

parts.prompt: Calculate the total distance travelled between t = 0.0 s and t = 16.0 s.
workingSteps: Velocity crosses zero at t = 11 s; forward area = 90.0 m.
Unsigned reverse area = 18.0 m, so total distance = 90.0 + 18.0 = 108 m.

parts.prompt: Determine the net displacement and hence calculate the average velocity over the 16.0 s interval.
workingSteps: Average velocity = Δs / Δt = 72.0 / 16 = 4.50 m s⁻¹.

parts.prompt: Calculate the acceleration between t = 8.0 s and t = 12.0 s.

items.stem: Starting at x = 40.0 m from a optical home flag, a high-speed bottling-line transfer sled completes the 20.0 s journey shown on the velocity–time graph, braking uniformly from t = 15.0 s to t = 20.0 s. What is its acceleration during braking?
items.workedSolution: During braking from t = 15 s to t = 20 s, a = (0 − 18) / (20 − 15) = -3.60 m s⁻².

items.stem: Over a 15.0 s cycle on a test tank, a miniature autonomous submarine follows the piecewise displacement–time graph shown. What is its average velocity from t = 0.0 s to t = 15.0 s?
items.workedSolution: Initial displacement at t = 0.0 s is 19 m and final displacement at t = 15 s is 25 m. Average velocity = (25 − 19) / 15 = 0.400 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates net displacement (25 − 19) / 15 = 0.400 m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: The signed upward acceleration of a high-rise express lift is plotted from t = 0.0 s to t = 10.0 s; at the start of the recording, its velocity is 10.0 m s⁻¹ upward.
items.workedSolution: (a) Maximum speed occurs when acceleration crosses zero from positive to negative at t = 6.00 s. (b) Positive area = 18.0 m s⁻¹, giving v_max = 10 + 18.0 = 28.0 m s⁻¹. (c) Negative area magnitude = 9.00 m s⁻¹, so v_final = 28.0 − 9.00 = 19.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: States t = 6.00 s.
Evaluates positive area up to 6 s (18.0 m s⁻¹) and adds u₀ = 10 m s⁻¹.
Obtains v_max = 28.0 m s⁻¹.
Subtracts negative area (9.00 m s⁻¹) from v_max.
Obtains final velocity = 19.0 m s⁻¹.

workingSteps: Magnitude of negative a–t area (6 s to 10 s) = ½(2)(3) + (2)(3) = 9.00 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: The momentum–time graph is recorded for an ice-rink calibration sled (mass 4.0 kg) travelling along a straight guide. Calculate the net work done on the object from t = 4.0 s to t = 8.0 s.
items.workedSolution: Using E_k = p² / (2m), net work W = ΔE_k = (28² − 8²) / (2 × 4) = 90.0 J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies W = (p₂² − p₁²) / (2m) = (28² − 8²) / (8) = 90.0 J (C).

items.stem: During a 4.0 s stator current pulse, a linear-motor launch shuttle (mass 5.0 kg, initial momentum 15.0 kg m s⁻¹) experiences the force–time profile shown. What is the time-averaged resultant force over the 4.0 s interval?
items.workedSolution: Total impulse J = ½(4 + 2)(35) = 105 N s. Mean force F_mean = J / Δt = 105 / 4 = 26.3 N.

markScheme.criterion: Divides impulse (105 N s) by 4 s to obtain 26.3 N (C).

Obtains v = 10.0 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: The tensile stress–strain curve for a thermoplastic elastomer tether is linear from 0.0 to strain 0.3 and reaches strain 0.6. Determine the Young's modulus in MPa.
items.workedSolution: Up to the limit of proportionality at ε = 0.3, stress reaches 210 MPa. Young's modulus E = σ / ε = 210 / 0.3 = 700 MPa.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates initial linear gradient E = 210 / 0.3 = 700 MPa (D).

items.stem: When an automotive dashboard filament bulb carries 1.5 A, what electrical resistance is indicated by the potential difference–current plot?
items.workedSolution: Electrical resistance at an operating point is defined by R = V / I (not the local slope ΔV / ΔI). At I = 1.5 A, V = 15.75 V, so R = 15.75 / 1.5 = 10.5 Ω.

markScheme.criterion: Uses static ratio R = V / I = 15.75 / 1.5 = 10.5 Ω (C).

items.stem: To determine the EMF and internal resistance of a lead-acid laboratory accumulator, V is graphed against I over the current interval 0.0 A to 5.0 A.
items.workedSolution: (a) Open-circuit intercept gives ε = 16.0 V. (b) Gradient = (7 − 16) / 5 = -1.80 V A⁻¹. (c) Mean terminal p.d. = ½(16 + 7) = 11.5 V.

markScheme.criterion: Reads ε = 16.0 V at I = 0.
Evaluates (7 − 16) / 5 including negative sign.
Obtains -1.80 V A⁻¹.
Uses ½(16 + 7) or area divided by 5 A.
Obtains 11.5 V.

parts.prompt: State the electromotive force ε of the source.
Determine the signed gradient of the V–I graph between 0.0 A and 5.0 A.
Calculate the mean terminal potential difference across the 0.0 A to 5.0 A interval.

items.stem: Using crocodile clips with constant contact resistance R₀, a student measures total resistance R of a carbon-loaded antistatic composite bar for different length-to-area ratios (L / A) up to 500.0 m⁻¹, so R = ρ(L / A) + R₀. From the plotted line, what is the resistivity ρ of the material?
items.workedSolution: Since R = ρ(L / A) + R₀, resistivity ρ equals the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A) = (36 − 7) / 500 = 0.0580 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept R₀ = 7 Ω to obtain ρ = (36 − 7) / 500 = 0.0580 Ω m (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes the secant ratio R_max / (L/A)_max from the origin and fails to subtract the non-zero contact-resistance intercept R₀.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Adds the zero-offset intercept R₀ to R_max instead of subtracting it when finding ΔR.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Δ(L/A) / ΔR (electrical conductivity σ) instead of ΔR / Δ(L/A).

items.stem: Taking g = 9.8 m s⁻², a wheeled telemetry trolley accelerating along a tilted track descends a smooth plane inclined at sin θ = 0.3, passing s = 0.0 m already in motion. From the v² against s plot up to 2.0 m, find the slope Δ(v²) / Δs.
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 2.5 m² s⁻² and at s = 2 m, v² = 14.26 m² s⁻². Gradient = (14.26 − 2.5) / 2 = 2(9.8)(0.3) = 5.88 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 2.5 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.8 × 0.3) to get 5.88 m s⁻² (D).

items.stem: During an electrostatics practical with charged graphite-coated spheres on a quartz-fibre force sensor, readings of F are plotted versus r⁻² across 0.0 m⁻² to 100.0 m⁻² as shown.
items.workedSolution: (a) At r⁻² = 0, systematic tare offset F₀ = 0.200 N. (b) Gradient = (1.8 − 0.2) / 100 = 0.0160 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Reads intercept F₀ = 0.200 N.
Evaluates ΔF = 1.8 − 0.2 using intercept from (a).
Divides ΔF by 100 m⁻² and states correct unit N m².
Obtains 0.0160 N m².

parts.prompt: State the systematic tare offset F₀ of the balance as separation r approaches infinity.
workingSteps: As r → ∞, r⁻² → 0, where the vertical intercept gives F₀ = 0.200 N.

parts.prompt: Calculate the gradient k|Q₁Q₂| of the linearized plot over 0.0 m⁻² to 100.0 m⁻².
workingSteps: Read F = 1.8 N at r⁻² = 100 m⁻².

items.stem: To estimate gradient uncertainty in an optical photodiode irradiance calibration, a student draws the steepest acceptable line of worst fit between the extreme error-bar vertices at incident power 2.0 mW and 10.0 mW, as plotted. What is the gradient m_worst of this worst-fit line?
items.workedSolution: At x₁ = 2 mW, y₁ = 6 μA; at x₂ = 10 mW, y₂ = 38 μA. Worst-fit gradient m_worst = (38 − 6) / (10 − 2) = 4.00 μA mW⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δy / Δx = (38 − 6) / (10 − 2) = 4.00 μA mW⁻¹ (A).

items.stem: Telemetry from an underwater ROV thruster sled operating along a taut calibration tether is plotted on the velocity–time axes shown (away from the dock positive). What total path distance is covered over the 15.0 s run?
items.workedSolution: Velocity crosses zero at t = 9 s. Forward area (0 to 9 s) = ½(3)(20) + (4)(20) + ½(2)(20) = 130 m. Reverse area magnitude (9 s to 15 s) = ½(1)(10) + (5)(10) = 55.0 m. Total distance = 130 + 55.0 = 185 m.

markScheme.criterion: Sums unsigned positive (130 m) and negative (55.0 m) velocity–time areas to obtain 185 m (B).

items.stem: Telemetry for a wind-tunnel moving-ground carriage begins at t = 0.0 s when it is stationary 50.0 m beyond the nozzle datum line. Its velocity–time profile over the 15.0 s run is plotted, with braking starting at t = 9.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Trapezium area Δx = ½(15 + 6)(22) = 231 m. (b) Final distance from datum = 50 + 231 = 281 m. (c) Mean speed = 231 / 15 = 15.4 m s⁻¹. (d) Braking acceleration = (0 − 22) / (15 − 9) = -3.67 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Identifies distance travelled as the area under the v–t trapezium.
Obtains Δx = 231 m.
Adds 50 m offset to obtain 281 m.
Divides distance travelled from (a) by 15 s.
Obtains mean speed = 15.4 m s⁻¹.
Obtains braking acceleration = -3.67 m s⁻².

items.stem: Inspect the first segment (0.0 s to 3.0 s) of the displacement–time plot for a motorized diffraction-slit carriage on an optical rail. What constant velocity does it have in this interval?
items.workedSolution: At t = 0.0 s, s₀ = 9 m; at t = 3 s, s₁ = 37 m. Velocity v = Δs / Δt = (37 − 9) / 3 = 9.33 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts initial position s₀ = 9 m to obtain v = (37 − 9) / 3 = 9.33 m s⁻¹ (A).

items.stem: Over an interval of 10.0 s, a maglev propulsion test pod (initial velocity 8.0 m s⁻¹ eastward) follows the plotted acceleration profile. What velocity does it have when t = 10.0 s?
items.workedSolution: Positive a–t area (0 to 5 s) = 28.0 m s⁻¹; negative area magnitude (5 s to 10 s) = 16.0 m s⁻¹. Net Δv = 28.0 − 16.0 = 12.0 m s⁻¹. Final velocity = 8 + (12.0) = 20.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Combines net signed area (12.0 m s⁻¹) with u₀ = 8 m s⁻¹ to obtain 20.0 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: Along a horizontal guideway, a linear air-bearing carriage of mass 0.8 kg moves in a fixed direction. Its momentum–time graph shows an impulse stage from t = 1.0 s to t = 5.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Resultant force F = Δp / Δt = (7.2 − 1.6) / (5 − 1) = 1.40 N. (b) Net work W = ΔE_k = (7.2² − 1.6²) / (2 × 0.8) = 30.8 J.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies resultant force as gradient Δp / Δt of the p–t graph.
Obtains F = 1.40 N.
Relates net work to ΔE_k = (p₂² − p₁²) / (2m).
Substitutes p₁ = 1.6 kg m s⁻¹, p₂ = 7.2 kg m s⁻¹, and m = 0.8 kg.
Obtains W = 30.8 J.

items.stem: Refer to the force–time profile of a docking vernier firing on a microgravity cargo pod of mass 0.8 kg (initial momentum 2.4 kg m s⁻¹). By how much does its speed increase over the 0.5 s pulse?
items.workedSolution: Impulse J = area under F–t trapezium = ½(0.5 + 0.3)(42) = 16.8 N s. Speed increase Δv = J / m = 16.8 / 0.8 = 21.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Computes J = 16.8 N s and Δv = J / 0.8 = 21.0 m s⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: Evaluate the net work done by the resultant force on an automated mining skip (mass 3.0 kg, initial speed 6.0 m s⁻¹) between x = 0.0 m and x = 15.0 m using the graph.
items.workedSolution: Forward work (0 to 12 m) = 162 J; resistive work (12 m to 15 m) = −9.00 J. Net work = 162 − 9.00 = 153 J.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts resistive triangle (9.00 J) from positive trapezium (162 J) to get 153 J (A).

markScheme.criterion: Reads vertical intercept = 8.20.
Uses large triangle (3.4 − 8.2) / 80.
Includes negative sign and unit s⁻¹.
Obtains gradient = -0.0600 s⁻¹.

items.stem: Refer to the Hooke's-law force–extension line for an optical-mount preload spring. What work is done in stretching it from x = 0.0 m to x = 1.0 m?
items.workedSolution: Elastic potential energy equals the triangular area under the F–x line: E_p = ½ F x = ½(70)(1) = 35.0 J.

options.distractorRationale: Multiplies peak force by maximum extension (F_max × x_max) and omits the triangular factor of ½.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Squares the spring constant k instead of the extension x when applying E_p = ½kx².

items.stem: Determine the strain energy stored per unit volume (in MJ m⁻³) when a drawn nylon monofilament is loaded from zero strain to 0.4 along the plotted stress–strain curve (proportional limit at 0.2).
items.workedSolution: Work per unit volume equals area under the σ–ε graph (1 MPa × 1 = 1 MJ m⁻³): u = ½(0.2)(120) + ½(120 + 180)(0.2) = 42.0 MJ m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Sums triangle and trapezium areas under σ–ε curve to obtain 42.0 MJ m⁻³ (A).

options.distractorRationale: Integrates only up to the limit of proportionality at ε₁ and omits the trapezium from ε₁ to ε_max.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies peak stress by maximum strain without integrating the piecewise area.

options.distractorRationale: Approximates the entire bilinear curve as a single triangle from (0, 0) to (ε_max, σ_max).

items.stem: Examine the experimental V–I characteristic obtained for a platinum-wire hot-wire anemometer element as current is swept slowly up to 1.6 A.
items.workedSolution: (a) At I = 1.6 A, V = 14.4 V. (b) Static resistance R = V / I = 14.4 / 1.6 = 9.00 Ω (the upper segment gradient 4.50 Ω is ΔV / ΔI, not R).

markScheme.criterion: Reads V = 14.4 V at I = 1.6 A.
Selects R = V / I rather than local segment gradient ΔV / ΔI.
Substitutes V = 14.4 V and I = 1.6 A.
Obtains R = 9.00 Ω.

items.workedSolution: At I = 0.0 A, V = ε = 4.2 V; at I = 0.8 A, V = 2.2 V. Gradient = (2.2 − 4.2) / 0.8 = -2.50 V A⁻¹ (equal to −r).

items.stem: Varying specimen geometry up to L / A = 200.0 m⁻¹, a student obtains the straight-line R versus L / A plot shown for an aqueous copper-sulfate capillary cell.
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical intercept R₀ = 5.00 Ω. (b) Resistivity ρ = (25 − 5) / 200 = 0.100 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: States R₀ = 5.00 Ω.
Identifies ρ with the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A).
Subtracts R₀ = 5 Ω from 25 Ω before dividing by 200 m⁻¹.
Obtains ρ = 0.100 Ω m.

items.stem: Speed-squared readings v² are graphed against displacement s (0.0 m to 1.6 m) for a low-friction dynamics cart descending a tilted aluminium runway on a frictionless ramp of sin θ = 0.4 where g = 9.81 m s⁻². Calculate the gradient of the line.
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 3.4 m² s⁻² and at s = 1.6 m, v² = 15.9568 m² s⁻². Gradient = (15.9568 − 3.4) / 1.6 = 2(9.81)(0.4) = 7.85 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 3.4 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.81 × 0.4) to get 7.85 m s⁻² (A).

items.stem: Readings F from silvered glass spheres positioned above a digital load pan are linearized against r⁻² from 0.0 m⁻² to 40.0 m⁻². Accounting for the systematic zero-offset F₀, determine the gradient ΔF / Δ(r⁻²).
items.workedSolution: At r⁻² = 0.0 m⁻², tare offset F₀ = 0.15 N; at r⁻² = 40 m⁻², F = 1.35 N. Gradient = (1.35 − 0.15) / 40 = 0.0300 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts tare offset F₀ = 0.15 N to get (1.35 − 0.15) / 40 = 0.0300 N m² (A).

items.stem: A laboratory report for a thermocouple electromotive-force test includes the shallowest error-bar line of worst fit graphed between 1.0 K and 5.0 K.
items.workedSolution: (a) At 5 K, y₂ = 21.0 mV. (b) Worst-fit gradient = (21 − 5) / (5 − 1) = 4.00 mV K⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Reads y₂ = 21.0 mV.
Reads y₁ = 5 mV at x₁ = 1 K and forms Δy / Δx.
Subtracts x₁ = 1 K in the denominator (5 − 1).
Obtains 4.00 mV K⁻¹.

items.workedSolution: Velocity reaches zero at t = 8 s. Positive area = 132 m and area below the axis has magnitude 28.0 m. Net displacement = 132 − 28.0 = 104 m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts reverse area (28.0 m) from forward area (132 m) to obtain 104 m (A).

items.stem: Examine the 16.0 s velocity–time curve for an inter-terminal airport monorail (initial coordinate 28.0 m from the concourse datum post). What mean speed is achieved during this movement?
items.workedSolution: Distance travelled Δx = ½(16 + 8)(20) = 240 m (independent of the 28 m starting offset). Mean speed = 240 / 16 = 15.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Divides trapezium distance (240 m) by 16 s to obtain 15.0 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: The displacement–time graph records the motion of an ultrasonic rangefinder target cart along an air track from t = 0.0 s to t = 20.0 s, including a stationary dwell and a final return stage from t = 12.0 s to t = 20.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Maximum displacement at the plateau = 64.0 m. (b) Return-stage velocity = (28 − 64) / (20 − 12) = -4.50 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Reads plateau displacement = 64.0 m.
Uses gradient formula Δs / Δt = (28 − 64) / (20 − 12).
Retains negative sign for motion back toward the origin.
Obtains -4.50 m s⁻¹.

workingSteps: Velocity equals the gradient Δs / Δt of the s–t graph.

items.stem: A data logger captures 12.0 s of signed upward acceleration for a high-rise express lift, which passes t = 0.0 s at 12.0 m s⁻¹. Evaluate the peak speed achieved.
items.workedSolution: Speed increases while a > 0 (from t = 0.0 s until a = 0 at t = 6 s). Positive area Δv_max = (4)(5) + ½(2)(5) = 25.0 m s⁻¹. Maximum speed = u₀ + Δv_max = 12 + 25.0 = 37.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Integrates positive acceleration up to t = 6 s (25.0 m s⁻¹) and adds 12 m s⁻¹ to get 37.0 m s⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: A thruster acts from t = 2.0 s to t = 7.0 s on an air-track glider of mass 5.0 kg, producing the momentum–time trace shown. What kinetic energy gain (net work) occurs over this interval?
items.workedSolution: Using E_k = p² / (2m), net work W = ΔE_k = (30² − 10²) / (2 × 5) = 80.0 J.

items.stem: A force transducer logs a 2.5 s cold-gas thruster burn acting forward on a cold-gas attitude probe (mass 3.0 kg), which had momentum 9.0 kg m s⁻¹ at t = 0.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Impulse J = ½(2.5 + 1.5)(46) = 92.0 N s. (b) Final momentum p_f = 9 + 92.0 = 101 kg m s⁻¹. (c) Speed increase Δv = 92.0 / 3 = 30.7 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Computes impulse from the trapezium area under the F–t curve.
Obtains J = 92.0 N s.
Adds 9 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 101 kg m s⁻¹.
Divides impulse from (a) by 3 kg.
Obtains Δv = 30.7 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: The resultant force in the direction of motion of an instrumented crash-test carriage (mass 2.0 kg, initial speed 7.0 m s⁻¹) is plotted over 16.0 m. Determine its speed at x = 16.0 m.
items.workedSolution: Positive work (0 to 12 m) = ½(12 + 6)(10) = 90.0 J. Resistive work (12 m to 16 m) = −½(4)(2) = −4.00 J. Net work W = 86.0 J. From ½mv² = ½mu₀² + W, v = √(7² + 2 × 86.0 / 2) = 11.6 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Finds net work W = 86.0 J and v = √(7² + 2W/2) = 11.6 m s⁻¹ (B).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Δt / Δ(ln C) to obtain −1/λ (negative mean lifetime) instead of the gradient −λ.

items.stem: Calibration measurements up to 0.8 m for an optical-mount preload spring are graphed below; at full compression it propels a stationary 0.6 kg slider along a level frictionless rail.
items.workedSolution: (a) k = 92 / 0.8 = 115 N m⁻¹. (b) Elastic energy E_p = ½(92)(0.8) = 36.8 J. (c) Launch speed v = √(2(36.8)/0.6) = 11.1 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies k as the gradient ΔF / Δx.
Obtains k = 115 N m⁻¹.
Uses triangular area ½Fx.
Obtains E_p = 36.8 J.
Equates ½(0.6)v² to stored elastic energy from (b).
Obtains v = 11.1 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Refer to the tensile stress–strain plot for a polypropylene surgical suture, whose limit of proportionality lies at strain 0.25. Calculate its initial Young's modulus.
items.workedSolution: Up to the limit of proportionality at ε = 0.25, stress reaches 230 MPa. Young's modulus E = σ / ε = 230 / 0.25 = 920 MPa.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates initial linear gradient E = 230 / 0.25 = 920 MPa (C).

items.stem: The potential difference–current characteristic for a vacuum-tube heater filament is plotted up to I = 1.0 A. What is the electrical resistance of the component when the current through it is 1.0 A?
items.workedSolution: Electrical resistance at an operating point is defined by R = V / I (not the local slope ΔV / ΔI). At I = 1 A, V = 13.5 V, so R = 13.5 / 1 = 13.5 Ω.

markScheme.criterion: Uses static ratio R = V / I = 13.5 / 1 = 13.5 Ω (A).

items.stem: The straight-line plot below shows how the terminal potential difference of a rechargeable nickel-cadmium pack falls as load current increases from 0.0 A to 2.0 A.
items.workedSolution: (a) Open-circuit intercept gives ε = 10.6 V. (b) Gradient = (5 − 10.6) / 2 = -2.80 V A⁻¹. (c) Mean terminal p.d. = ½(10.6 + 5) = 7.80 V.

markScheme.criterion: Reads ε = 10.6 V at I = 0.
Evaluates (5 − 10.6) / 2 including negative sign.
Obtains -2.80 V A⁻¹.
Uses ½(10.6 + 5) or area divided by 2 A.
Obtains 7.80 V.

items.stem: Total circuit resistance R (including lead resistance R₀) is plotted against geometric ratio L / A up to 250.0 m⁻¹ for a doped silicon bar. Calculate the electrical resistivity ρ.
items.workedSolution: Since R = ρ(L / A) + R₀, resistivity ρ equals the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A) = (32 − 8) / 250 = 0.0960 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept R₀ = 8 Ω to obtain ρ = (32 − 8) / 250 = 0.0960 Ω m (C).

items.stem: How steep (in m s⁻²) is the linear v² versus s graph recorded over 2.5 m for an air-bearing carriage coasting down a Precision granite incline on a smooth slope (sin θ = 0.2, g = 9.8 m s⁻²)?
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 2.8 m² s⁻² and at s = 2.5 m, v² = 12.6 m² s⁻². Gradient = (12.6 − 2.8) / 2.5 = 2(9.8)(0.2) = 3.92 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 2.8 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.8 × 0.2) to get 3.92 m s⁻² (C).

items.stem: Refer to the linearized Coulomb graph of balance reading F against r⁻² (up to 80.0 m⁻²) recorded using silvered glass spheres positioned above a digital load pan.
items.workedSolution: (a) At r⁻² = 0, systematic tare offset F₀ = 0.200 N. (b) Gradient = (2.2 − 0.2) / 80 = 0.0250 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Reads intercept F₀ = 0.200 N.
Evaluates ΔF = 2.2 − 0.2 using intercept from (a).
Divides ΔF by 80 m⁻² and states correct unit N m².
Obtains 0.0250 N m².

items.stem: The graph displays the steepest line of worst fit joining opposite vertical error-bar extremes from 2.0 m to 8.0 m in a simple-pendulum linearization study. Calculate its gradient.
items.workedSolution: At x₁ = 2 m, y₁ = 4 s²; at x₂ = 8 m, y₂ = 29 s². Worst-fit gradient m_worst = (29 − 4) / (8 − 2) = 4.17 s² m⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δy / Δx = (29 − 4) / (8 − 2) = 4.17 s² m⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: The graph displays how the velocity of an autonomous harbour mooring buggy along a straight quay rail varies with time over 20.0 s. Positive velocity corresponds to motion southward, and direction reversal occurs during the linear ramp between t = 10.0 s and t = 15.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Zero-velocity crossing is at t = 13 s. Positive area = 228 m and unsigned negative area = 96.0 m, giving total distance = 324 m. (b) Net displacement = 228 − 96.0 = 132 m; average velocity = 132 / 20 = 6.60 m s⁻¹. (c) Acceleration = (−16 − 24) / (15 − 10) = -8.00 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Finds zero-crossing t = 13 s and evaluates both unsigned areas (228 m and 96.0 m).
Obtains total distance = 324 m.
Subtracts areas for net displacement (132 m) and divides by 20 s.
Obtains average velocity = 6.60 m s⁻¹.
Obtains acceleration = -8.00 m s⁻² including negative sign.

items.stem: In the velocity–time record for a linear-induction baggage carrier (initially 45.0 m from the sorting-hall origin sensor), uniform braking begins at t = 14.0 s and ends at rest at t = 20.0 s. Find the signed braking acceleration.
items.workedSolution: During braking from t = 14 s to t = 20 s, a = (0 − 24) / (20 − 14) = -4.00 m s⁻².

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Δt / Δv instead of computing Δv / Δt.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Divides the velocity drop by the full journey duration t₃ instead of the braking duration (t₃ − t₂).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Finds the magnitude of deceleration but omits the negative sign required for signed acceleration.

items.stem: Using the complete 16.0 s displacement–time trace for a laser-tracked precision stage on a metrology rail, calculate the average velocity over the entire 16.0 s interval.
items.workedSolution: Initial displacement at t = 0.0 s is 18 m and final displacement at t = 16 s is 26 m. Average velocity = (26 − 18) / 16 = 0.500 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates net displacement (26 − 18) / 16 = 0.500 m s⁻¹ (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Sums outward and return path lengths to compute average speed rather than net average velocity.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Takes the unweighted arithmetic mean of the two non-zero stage velocities, ignoring stage durations and the dwell plateau.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses final coordinate s₂ / t₃ and forgets to subtract the non-zero starting coordinate s₀.

items.stem: A 10.0 s accelerometer log is shown for an electromagnetic catapult shuttle, which is already travelling forward at 11.0 m s⁻¹ when t = 0.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Maximum speed occurs when acceleration crosses zero from positive to negative at t = 4.00 s. (b) Positive area = 30.0 m s⁻¹, giving v_max = 11 + 30.0 = 41.0 m s⁻¹. (c) Negative area magnitude = 15.0 m s⁻¹, so v_final = 41.0 − 15.0 = 26.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: States t = 4.00 s.
Evaluates positive area up to 4 s (30.0 m s⁻¹) and adds u₀ = 11 m s⁻¹.
Obtains v_max = 41.0 m s⁻¹.
Subtracts negative area (15.0 m s⁻¹) from v_max.
Obtains final velocity = 26.0 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: The graph displays the linear momentum of a frictionless puck on an air table (mass 3.2 kg) against time. What resultant force acts on it between t = 3.0 s and t = 8.0 s?
items.workedSolution: By Newton's second law, F = Δp / Δt = (22.4 − 6.4) / (8 − 3) = 3.20 N.

items.stem: Calculate the mean resultant force exerted during the 1.0 s hydraulic arrester pulse on a crash-barrier test sled (mass 1.2 kg, initial momentum 3.6 kg m s⁻¹) from the plotted F–t curve.
items.workedSolution: Total impulse J = ½(1 + 0.4)(40) = 28.0 N s. Mean force F_mean = J / Δt = 28.0 / 1 = 28.0 N.

markScheme.criterion: Divides impulse (28.0 N s) by 1 s to obtain 28.0 N (B).

items.stem: At x = 0.0 m, a pneumatic factory transfer cart of mass 4.0 kg moves in the positive x-direction at 5.5 m s⁻¹. The graph shows the resultant force acting along its line of motion from x = 0.0 m to x = 10.0 m.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates positive (144 J) and negative (−8.00 J) areas.
Obtains net work W = 136 J.
Uses ½mv² = ½(4)(5.5²) + W.
Obtains v = 9.91 m s⁻¹.
Divides net work by 10 m to get 13.6 N.

items.stem: On a horizontal frictionless bench, a pinball plunger coil spring is compressed by 0.5 m according to the force–compression graph shown and released from rest to propel a 0.15 kg block. What launch speed does the block acquire?
items.workedSolution: Elastic energy stored E_p = ½(50)(0.5) = 12.5 J. Equating ½mv² = E_p gives v = √(2 × 12.5 / 0.15) = 12.9 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Sets ½(0.15)v² = 12.5 J to obtain v = 12.9 m s⁻¹ (A).

items.stem: Extensometer and load-cell readings for a regenerated silk-fibroin strand are converted to tensile stress and strain up to 0.8 (proportional limit 0.4) as graphed.
items.workedSolution: (a) Young's modulus E = 170 / 0.4 = 425 MPa. (b) Energy per unit volume = ½(0.4)(170) + ½(170 + 240)(0.4) = 116 MJ m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates initial gradient σ / ε up to ε = 0.4.
Obtains E = 425 MPa.
Identifies work per unit volume as total area under the σ–ε graph.
Splits area into initial triangle plus upper trapezium.
Obtains 116 MJ m⁻³.

parts.prompt: Determine the Young's modulus of the specimen over the proportional region (0.0 to 0.4).
Calculate the work done per unit volume in stretching the specimen from zero strain to 0.8.
workingSteps: Area from 0 to 0.4 = ½(0.4)(170) = 34.0 MJ m⁻³.
Area from 0.4 to 0.8 = ½(170 + 240)(0.4) = 82.0 MJ m⁻³; total = 116 MJ m⁻³.

items.stem: Using the plotted V–I characteristic of a miniature krypton torch lamp, calculate its static resistance R at an operating current of 2.0 A.
items.workedSolution: Electrical resistance at an operating point is defined by R = V / I (not the local slope ΔV / ΔI). At I = 2 A, V = 16.5 V, so R = 16.5 / 2 = 8.25 Ω.

markScheme.criterion: Uses static ratio R = V / I = 16.5 / 2 = 8.25 Ω (C).

items.stem: The terminal potential difference V of a thermoelectric Seebeck generator decreases linearly with load current I from 0.0 A to 4.0 A, as shown. What is the mean terminal potential difference across this current range?
items.workedSolution: Terminal p.d. varies linearly from 15 V at I = 0.0 A to 5 V at I = 4 A, so V_mean = ½(15 + 5) = 10.0 V.

markScheme.criterion: Averages endpoint voltages ½(15 + 5) = 10.0 V (A).

items.stem: To determine the resistivity ρ of a concentrated saline conductivity column despite probe and lead resistance R₀, a student plots total measured resistance R against the ratio L / A from 0.0 m⁻¹ to 400.0 m⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical intercept R₀ = 10.0 Ω. (b) Resistivity ρ = (46 − 10) / 400 = 0.0900 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: States R₀ = 10.0 Ω.
Identifies ρ with the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A).
Subtracts R₀ = 10 Ω from 46 Ω before dividing by 400 m⁻¹.
Obtains ρ = 0.0900 Ω m.

workingSteps: From R = ρ(L / A) + R₀, ρ equals the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A).

items.stem: Examine the straight-line plot of v² against track distance s up to 2.0 m for a low-drag calibration capsule descending a straight guide rail (ramp sin θ = 0.35, g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Evaluate its gradient.
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 4 m² s⁻² and at s = 2 m, v² = 17.734 m² s⁻². Gradient = (17.734 − 4) / 2 = 2(9.81)(0.35) = 6.87 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 4 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.81 × 0.35) to get 6.87 m s⁻² (C).

items.stem: The linearized Coulomb plot shows balance force F versus inverse-square separation r⁻² up to 50.0 m⁻² for gold-leaf coated polymer spheres on a capacitive force transducer. Calculate the gradient of the line in N m².
items.workedSolution: At r⁻² = 0.0 m⁻², tare offset F₀ = 0.25 N; at r⁻² = 50 m⁻², F = 1.65 N. Gradient = (1.65 − 0.25) / 50 = 0.0280 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts tare offset F₀ = 0.25 N to get (1.65 − 0.25) / 50 = 0.0280 N m² (A).

items.stem: In a piezoelectric load-cell calibration, vertical error bars on the first (0.5 N) and last (2.5 N) data points are used to draw the steepest acceptable line of worst fit shown on the graph.
items.workedSolution: (a) At 2.5 N, y₂ = 12.4 mV. (b) Worst-fit gradient = (12.4 − 1.2) / (2.5 − 0.5) = 5.60 mV N⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Reads y₂ = 12.4 mV.
Reads y₁ = 1.2 mV at x₁ = 0.5 N and forms Δy / Δx.
Subtracts x₁ = 0.5 N in the denominator (2.5 − 0.5).
Obtains 5.60 mV N⁻¹.

items.stem: The velocity–time profile shows a drop-tower counterbalance carriage reversing motion inside a vertical guide shaft with upward defined as positive. Calculate the total scalar distance travelled between t = 0.0 s and t = 14.0 s.
items.workedSolution: Velocity crosses zero at t = 9 s. Forward area (0 to 9 s) = ½(2)(18) + (4)(18) + ½(3)(18) = 117 m. Reverse area magnitude (9 s to 14 s) = ½(1)(6) + (4)(6) = 27.0 m. Total distance = 117 + 27.0 = 144 m.

markScheme.criterion: Sums unsigned positive (117 m) and negative (27.0 m) velocity–time areas to obtain 144 m (D).

items.stem: At t = 0.0 s, a canal lock towing locomotive is stationary at a position 32.0 m ahead of a lock-gate reference mark. It then moves forward along a straight guideway according to the velocity–time graph for 10.0 s. What is its final distance from the lock-gate reference mark at t = 10.0 s?
items.workedSolution: Displacement during the 10 s run equals the trapezium area: Δx = ½(10 + 6)(19) = 152 m. Final position from the lock-gate reference mark = x₀ + Δx = 32 + 152 = 184 m.

markScheme.criterion: Adds trapezium area (152 m) to initial offset (32 m) to get 184 m (A).

options.distractorRationale: Treats the entire journey as constant-speed motion at peak velocity before adding x₀.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the trapezium displacement correctly but forgets to add the initial position offset x₀.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts the initial forward position x₀ from the integrated displacement instead of adding it.

items.stem: Position measurements of an automated pharmacy courier pod moving on a straight chute over a 15.0 s run are plotted on the displacement–time axes shown, with return travel occurring between t = 9.0 s and t = 15.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Maximum displacement at the plateau = 53.0 m. (b) Return-stage velocity = (19 − 53) / (15 − 9) = -5.67 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Reads plateau displacement = 53.0 m.
Uses gradient formula Δs / Δt = (19 − 53) / (15 − 9).
Retains negative sign for motion back toward the origin.
Obtains -5.67 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Calculate the eastward velocity at t = 10.0 s for a maglev propulsion test pod, given u = 13.0 m s⁻¹ at t = 0.0 s and the acceleration–time trace shown.
items.workedSolution: Positive a–t area (0 to 5 s) = 24.0 m s⁻¹; negative area magnitude (5 s to 10 s) = 14.0 m s⁻¹. Net Δv = 24.0 − 14.0 = 10.0 m s⁻¹. Final velocity = 13 + (10.0) = 23.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Combines net signed area (10.0 m s⁻¹) with u₀ = 13 m s⁻¹ to obtain 23.0 m s⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: Data loggers record the linear momentum of a magnetic rail cart (mass 1.2 kg), which experiences a constant resultant force between t = 2.0 s and t = 5.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Resultant force F = Δp / Δt = (9.6 − 2.4) / (5 − 2) = 2.40 N. (b) Net work W = ΔE_k = (9.6² − 2.4²) / (2 × 1.2) = 36.0 J.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies resultant force as gradient Δp / Δt of the p–t graph.
Obtains F = 2.40 N.
Relates net work to ΔE_k = (p₂² − p₁²) / (2m).
Substitutes p₁ = 2.4 kg m s⁻¹, p₂ = 9.6 kg m s⁻¹, and m = 1.2 kg.
Obtains W = 36.0 J.

items.stem: Having initial forward momentum 18.0 kg m s⁻¹, a robotic soccer puck of mass 6.0 kg experiences a collinear solenoid kicker stroke over 5.0 s as shown on the force–time graph. What is its change in speed Δv?
items.workedSolution: Impulse J = area under F–t trapezium = ½(5 + 3)(40) = 160 N s. Speed increase Δv = J / m = 160 / 6 = 26.7 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Computes J = 160 N s and Δv = J / 6 = 26.7 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: Passing x = 0.0 m with speed 4.0 m s⁻¹, a magnetic-launch coaster bogie of mass 3.2 kg experiences the collinear resultant force plotted against displacement up to x = 14.0 m. What is its speed at x = 14.0 m?
items.workedSolution: Positive work (0 to 11 m) = ½(11 + 6)(16) = 136 J. Resistive work (11 m to 14 m) = −½(3)(4) = −6.00 J. Net work W = 130 J. From ½mv² = ½mu₀² + W, v = √(4² + 2 × 130 / 3.2) = 9.86 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Finds net work W = 130 J and v = √(4² + 2W/3.2) = 9.86 m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: Using a thin-mica Geiger counter, background-corrected count rates C from a protactinium generator organic layer are measured over 25.0 s and linearized by plotting ln(C / s⁻¹) against time t.
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical intercept at t = 0 is ln(C₀ / s⁻¹) = 8.10. (b) Gradient = (3.1 − 8.1) / 25 = -0.200 s⁻¹ (which equals −λ).

markScheme.criterion: Reads vertical intercept = 8.10.
Uses large triangle (3.1 − 8.1) / 25.
Includes negative sign and unit s⁻¹.
Obtains gradient = -0.200 s⁻¹.

items.stem: Within its Hookean limit, an optical-mount preload spring produces the force–extension graph shown up to an extension of 0.4 m. How much elastic potential energy is stored at x = 0.4 m?
items.workedSolution: Elastic potential energy equals the triangular area under the F–x line: E_p = ½ F x = ½(64)(0.4) = 12.8 J.

markScheme.criterion: Computes triangular area ½(64)(0.4) = 12.8 J (C).

items.stem: In a tensile materials test, a drawn nylon monofilament obeys Hooke's law up to a strain of 0.5 before softening up to strain 1.0, as shown on the stress–strain graph. What is the Young's modulus of the material in the initial linear region?
items.workedSolution: Up to the limit of proportionality at ε = 0.5, stress reaches 280 MPa. Young's modulus E = σ / ε = 280 / 0.5 = 560 MPa.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates initial linear gradient E = 280 / 0.5 = 560 MPa (A).

items.stem: In a circuits practical, a student records the potential difference V across a miniature krypton torch lamp as the current I is increased from 0.0 A to 1.2 A, obtaining the non-linear characteristic shown.
items.workedSolution: (a) At I = 1.2 A, V = 12.6 V. (b) Static resistance R = V / I = 12.6 / 1.2 = 10.5 Ω (the upper segment gradient 14.3 Ω is ΔV / ΔI, not R).

markScheme.criterion: Reads V = 12.6 V at I = 1.2 A.
Selects R = V / I rather than local segment gradient ΔV / ΔI.
Substitutes V = 12.6 V and I = 1.2 A.
Obtains R = 10.5 Ω.

items.stem: Examine the linear V–I characteristic recorded for a rechargeable nickel-cadmium pack between zero current and 1.0 A. What is its signed gradient?
items.workedSolution: At I = 0.0 A, V = ε = 5.5 V; at I = 1 A, V = 2.5 V. Gradient = (2.5 − 5.5) / 1 = -3.00 V A⁻¹ (equal to −r).

items.stem: The linearized graph shows measured resistance R versus L / A for a polypyrrole conductive polymer film over 0.0 m⁻¹ to 500.0 m⁻¹. Accounting for the non-zero contact-resistance intercept, determine ρ.
items.workedSolution: Since R = ρ(L / A) + R₀, resistivity ρ equals the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A) = (51 − 12) / 500 = 0.0780 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept R₀ = 12 Ω to obtain ρ = (51 − 12) / 500 = 0.0780 Ω m (D).

items.stem: Passing s = 0.0 m already moving at speed u₀, a low-friction dynamics cart descending a tilted aluminium runway accelerates down a frictionless incline of sin θ = 0.6 (g = 9.8 m s⁻²); its v²–s trace over 1.0 m is shown.

markScheme.criterion: Reads intercept u₀² = 3.20 m² s⁻².
Forms gradient (14.96 − 3.2) / 1.
Subtracts non-zero intercept u₀² accurately.
Obtains 11.8 m s⁻².

items.stem: In an electrostatics investigation with silvered glass spheres positioned above a digital load pan, F is plotted against r⁻² up to 100.0 m⁻². Extract the proportionality constant k|Q₁Q₂| given by the slope.
items.workedSolution: At r⁻² = 0.0 m⁻², tare offset F₀ = 0.1 N; at r⁻² = 100 m⁻², F = 1.2 N. Gradient = (1.2 − 0.1) / 100 = 0.0110 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts tare offset F₀ = 0.1 N to get (1.2 − 0.1) / 100 = 0.0110 N m² (A).

items.stem: During uncertainty analysis of a capillary Poiseuille flow experiment, the shallowest worst-fit line is constructed across the domain 4.0 kPa to 20.0 kPa. Determine the gradient of the plotted line.
items.workedSolution: At x₁ = 4 kPa, y₁ = 12 mL s⁻¹; at x₂ = 20 kPa, y₂ = 56 mL s⁻¹. Worst-fit gradient m_worst = (56 − 12) / (20 − 4) = 2.75 mL s⁻¹ kPa⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δy / Δx = (56 − 12) / (20 − 4) = 2.75 mL s⁻¹ kPa⁻¹ (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Δx / Δy instead of evaluating Δy / Δx.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts y₁ in the numerator but divides by x₂ instead of the horizontal span (x₂ − x₁).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Adds the endpoint ordinates (y₂ + y₁) instead of computing their difference (y₂ − y₁).

items.stem: A data logger records the signed velocity of a seismic actuator test sled moving on a low-friction hydraulic guide (in the positive x-direction positive) over a 20.0 s cycle, with constant braking and reversal applied between t = 10.0 s and t = 15.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Zero-velocity crossing is at t = 13.75 s. Positive area = 281 m and unsigned negative area = 56.3 m, giving total distance = 338 m. (b) Net displacement = 281 − 56.3 = 225 m; average velocity = 225 / 20 = 11.3 m s⁻¹. (c) Acceleration = (−10 − 30) / (15 − 10) = -8.00 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Finds zero-crossing t = 13.75 s and evaluates both unsigned areas (281 m and 56.3 m).
Obtains total distance = 338 m.
Subtracts areas for net displacement (225 m) and divides by 20 s.
Obtains average velocity = 11.3 m s⁻¹.
Obtains acceleration = -8.00 m s⁻² including negative sign.

workingSteps: Velocity crosses zero at t = 13.75 s; forward area = 281 m.
Unsigned reverse area = 56.3 m, so total distance = 281 + 56.3 = 338 m.

parts.prompt: Determine the net displacement and hence calculate the average velocity over the 20.0 s interval.
workingSteps: Average velocity = Δs / Δt = 225 / 20 = 11.3 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Beginning 38.0 m past a base-camp beacon, a solar-powered desert research rover follows the velocity–time profile shown over 16.0 s. What is its mean speed during the 16.0 s journey?
items.workedSolution: Distance travelled Δx = ½(16 + 7)(16) = 184 m (independent of the 38 m starting offset). Mean speed = 184 / 16 = 11.5 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Divides trapezium distance (184 m) by 16 s to obtain 11.5 m s⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: A sensor records the displacement–time graph of a coastal tide-gauge float along a vertical stilling tube. What is its signed velocity during the return stage between t = 10.0 s and t = 20.0 s?
items.workedSolution: From t = 10 s to t = 20 s, displacement changes from 73 m to 39 m. Velocity v = (39 − 73) / (20 − 10) = -3.40 m s⁻¹.

options.distractorRationale: Evaluates speed |Δs / Δt| correctly but omits the negative sign indicating motion back toward the origin.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Divides Δs by the final timestamp t₃ instead of the stage duration (t₃ − t₂).

items.stem: Starting with forward velocity 16.0 m s⁻¹ at t = 0.0 s, an aerotow winch launch carriage follows the 12.0 s acceleration–time profile displayed on the axes.
items.workedSolution: (a) Maximum speed occurs when acceleration crosses zero from positive to negative at t = 8.00 s. (b) Positive area = 24.0 m s⁻¹, giving v_max = 16 + 24.0 = 40.0 m s⁻¹. (c) Negative area magnitude = 15.0 m s⁻¹, so v_final = 40.0 − 15.0 = 25.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: States t = 8.00 s.
Evaluates positive area up to 8 s (24.0 m s⁻¹) and adds u₀ = 16 m s⁻¹.
Obtains v_max = 40.0 m s⁻¹.
Subtracts negative area (15.0 m s⁻¹) from v_max.
Obtains final velocity = 25.0 m s⁻¹.

parts.prompt: Calculate this maximum speed.
Calculate the velocity at t = 12.0 s.

items.stem: Motion sensors track the momentum of a satellite attitude-test mass of mass 6.0 kg. Determine the magnitude of the resultant force acting from t = 4.0 s to t = 10.0 s.
items.workedSolution: By Newton's second law, F = Δp / Δt = (36 − 12) / (10 − 4) = 4.00 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F = Δp / Δt = (36 − 12) / (6) = 4.00 N (B).

options.distractorRationale: Divides Δp / Δt by mass m, obtaining acceleration rather than resultant force.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies Δp by Δt instead of evaluating the rate of change of momentum Δp / Δt.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes the secant ratio p₂ / t₂ from the origin, ignoring both initial momentum p₁ and start time t₁.

items.stem: Moving in a straight line with initial momentum 8.0 kg m s⁻¹, a rail-mounted docking target (mass 2.0 kg) undergoes the 2.0 s spring buffer contact shown. What is its final momentum at t = 2.0 s?
items.workedSolution: Impulse Δp = ½(2 + 1)(35) = 52.5 N s. Final momentum p_f = p₀ + Δp = 8 + 52.5 = 60.5 kg m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Adds impulse (52.5 N s) to p₀ = 8 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 60.5 kg m s⁻¹ (A).

options.distractorRationale: Assumes ln C drops to zero at t = t_max instead of subtracting the non-zero final ordinate ln C(t_max).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes λ = |Δ(ln C) / Δt| correctly in magnitude but omits the negative sign of the downward semi-log slope.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Δt / Δ(ln C) to obtain −1/λ (negative mean lifetime) instead of the gradient −λ.

items.stem: The force–compression graph for a robotics compliant-joint spring is recorded up to a maximum compression of 1.0 m. The compressed spring is then released from rest on a smooth horizontal track to launch a 0.5 kg glider.
items.workedSolution: (a) k = 110 / 1 = 110 N m⁻¹. (b) Elastic energy E_p = ½(110)(1) = 55.0 J. (c) Launch speed v = √(2(55.0)/0.5) = 14.8 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies k as the gradient ΔF / Δx.
Obtains k = 110 N m⁻¹.
Uses triangular area ½Fx.
Obtains E_p = 55.0 J.
Equates ½(0.5)v² to stored elastic energy from (b).
Obtains v = 14.8 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Determine the strain energy stored per unit volume (in MJ m⁻³) when a polypropylene surgical suture is loaded from zero strain to 0.6 along the plotted stress–strain curve (proportional limit at 0.3).
items.workedSolution: Work per unit volume equals area under the σ–ε graph (1 MPa × 1 = 1 MJ m⁻³): u = ½(0.3)(180) + ½(180 + 250)(0.3) = 91.5 MJ m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Sums triangle and trapezium areas under σ–ε curve to obtain 91.5 MJ m⁻³ (B).

items.stem: A student measures the V–I curve shown for a miniature incandescent beacon lamp. Determine the resistance of the device at I = 2.0 A.
items.workedSolution: Electrical resistance at an operating point is defined by R = V / I (not the local slope ΔV / ΔI). At I = 2 A, V = 15 V, so R = 15 / 2 = 7.50 Ω.

markScheme.criterion: Uses static ratio R = V / I = 15 / 2 = 7.50 Ω (D).
