items.stem: In an experiment to characterize a vanadium redox flow single cell, a variable resistor is adjusted while recording terminal potential difference V and current I from 0.0 A to 5.0 A. The resulting best-fit line is shown.
items.workedSolution: (a) Open-circuit intercept gives ε = 25.0 V. (b) Gradient = (10 − 25) / 5 = -3.00 V A⁻¹. (c) Mean terminal p.d. = ½(25 + 10) = 17.5 V.

markScheme.criterion: Reads ε = 25.0 V at I = 0.
Evaluates (10 − 25) / 5 including negative sign.
Obtains -3.00 V A⁻¹.
Uses ½(25 + 10) or area divided by 5 A.
Obtains 17.5 V.

items.stem: To find the resistivity ρ of a doped silicon bar, total resistance R = ρ(L / A) + R₀ is plotted against L / A up to 200.0 m⁻¹. What value of ρ does the graph give?
items.workedSolution: Since R = ρ(L / A) + R₀, resistivity ρ equals the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A) = (34 − 6) / 200 = 0.140 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept R₀ = 6 Ω to obtain ρ = (34 − 6) / 200 = 0.140 Ω m (A).

items.stem: An optical timer measures speed v of an air-bearing carriage coasting down a Precision granite incline at positions up to s = 1.6 m along a frictionless incline (sin θ = 0.25, g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What is the slope of the resulting v²–s graph?
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 4.2 m² s⁻² and at s = 1.6 m, v² = 12.048 m² s⁻². Gradient = (12.048 − 4.2) / 1.6 = 2(9.81)(0.25) = 4.91 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 4.2 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.81 × 0.25) to get 4.91 m s⁻² (B).

items.stem: In an experiment verifying Coulomb's inverse-square law using conductive carbon spheres mounted in a dry-nitrogen force cell, total force reading F is plotted against inverse-square separation r⁻² up to 25.0 m⁻², obeying F = k|Q₁Q₂|r⁻² + F₀.
items.workedSolution: (a) At r⁻² = 0, systematic tare offset F₀ = 0.100 N. (b) Gradient = (1.25 − 0.1) / 25 = 0.0460 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Reads intercept F₀ = 0.100 N.
Evaluates ΔF = 1.25 − 0.1 using intercept from (a).
Divides ΔF by 25 m⁻² and states correct unit N m².
Obtains 0.0460 N m².

items.stem: Inspect the steepest error-bar line of worst fit plotted from 1.0 m to 6.0 m for a simple-pendulum linearization study. What value does its gradient take?
items.workedSolution: At x₁ = 1 m, y₁ = 3 s²; at x₂ = 6 m, y₂ = 26 s². Worst-fit gradient m_worst = (26 − 3) / (6 − 1) = 4.60 s² m⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δy / Δx = (26 − 3) / (6 − 1) = 4.60 s² m⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: While operating along a straight viaduct rail (eastward positive), an automated rail inspection trolley brakes and reverses direction between t = 5.0 s and t = 8.0 s. From the velocity–time graph, what is its acceleration during this interval?
items.workedSolution: Between t = 5 s and t = 8 s, velocity changes from +16 m s⁻¹ to −8 m s⁻¹. Acceleration a = Δv / Δt = (−8 − 16) / (8 − 5) = -8.00 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δv / Δt = (−8 − 16) / (3) = -8.00 m s⁻² (A).

options.distractorRationale: Divides the velocity change by t₃ rather than the elapsed stage duration (t₃ − t₂).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes the slope magnitude accurately but omits the negative sign of the acceleration.

items.stem: Given that a centrifuge carrier pod has velocity 14.0 m s⁻¹ tangentially forward when t = 0.0 s, use the 12.0 s acceleration–time plot to find its maximum speed.
items.workedSolution: Speed increases while a > 0 (from t = 0.0 s until a = 0 at t = 6 s). Positive area Δv_max = (2)(6) + ½(4)(6) = 24.0 m s⁻¹. Maximum speed = u₀ + Δv_max = 14 + 24.0 = 38.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Integrates positive acceleration up to t = 6 s (24.0 m s⁻¹) and adds 14 m s⁻¹ to get 38.0 m s⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: During a 0.8 s pulsed ion-beam firing, a Hall-effect thruster test rig (mass 2.0 kg, initial momentum 6.0 kg m s⁻¹) experiences the force–time profile shown. What is the time-averaged resultant force over the 0.8 s interval?
items.workedSolution: Total impulse J = ½(0.8 + 0.4)(50) = 30.0 N s. Mean force F_mean = J / Δt = 30.0 / 0.8 = 37.5 N.

markScheme.criterion: Divides impulse (30.0 N s) by 0.8 s to obtain 37.5 N (C).

items.stem: A 2.0 kg unit (a linear dynamo test sled) enters an instrumented zone at 5.0 m s⁻¹. From the resultant force–displacement graph over 10.0 m, calculate its exit speed at x = 10.0 m.
items.workedSolution: Positive work (0 to 8 m) = ½(8 + 4)(12) = 72.0 J. Resistive work (8 m to 10 m) = −½(2)(4) = −4.00 J. Net work W = 68.0 J. From ½mv² = ½mu₀² + W, v = √(5² + 2 × 68.0 / 2) = 9.64 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Finds net work W = 68.0 J and v = √(5² + 2W/2) = 9.64 m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: The tensile stress–strain curve for a regenerated silk-fibroin strand is linear from 0.0 to strain 0.2 and reaches strain 0.4. Determine the Young's modulus in MPa.
items.workedSolution: Up to the limit of proportionality at ε = 0.2, stress reaches 150 MPa. Young's modulus E = σ / ε = 150 / 0.2 = 750 MPa.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates initial linear gradient E = 150 / 0.2 = 750 MPa (C).

items.stem: As current drawn from a thermoelectric Seebeck generator rises steadily from zero to 2.0 A, V follows the straight line on the graph. Determine the mean terminal voltage over this range.
items.workedSolution: Terminal p.d. varies linearly from 7 V at I = 0.0 A to 3.4 V at I = 2 A, so V_mean = ½(7 + 3.4) = 5.20 V.

markScheme.criterion: Averages endpoint voltages ½(7 + 3.4) = 5.20 V (B).

items.stem: Using two light gates in a gravitational field g = 9.8 m s⁻², a student records speed v of a low-drag calibration capsule descending a straight guide rail (inclination sin θ = 0.4) after passing an initial gate at s = 0.0 m with speed u₀ > 0, plotting v² against distance s up to 2.0 m. According to v² = u₀² + 2as, what is the gradient Δ(v²) / Δs of the line?
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 5 m² s⁻² and at s = 2 m, v² = 20.68 m² s⁻². Gradient = (20.68 − 5) / 2 = 2(9.8)(0.4) = 7.84 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 5 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.8 × 0.4) to get 7.84 m s⁻² (C).

items.stem: Varying centre-to-centre separation up to r⁻² = 40.0 m⁻² for gold-leaf coated polymer spheres on a capacitive force transducer yields the linear F versus r⁻² trace shown. Evaluate the slope ΔF / Δ(r⁻²).
items.workedSolution: At r⁻² = 0.0 m⁻², tare offset F₀ = 0.2 N; at r⁻² = 40 m⁻², F = 1.6 N. Gradient = (1.6 − 0.2) / 40 = 0.0350 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts tare offset F₀ = 0.2 N to get (1.6 − 0.2) / 40 = 0.0350 N m² (C).

items.stem: Engineers log the signed velocity of a magnetic-levitation shuttle pod on a horizontal vacuum test guideway over 12.0 s. How much total distance does it cover before the recording ends at t = 12.0 s?
items.workedSolution: Velocity crosses zero at t = 8 s. Forward area (0 to 8 s) = ½(2)(16) + (4)(16) + ½(2)(16) = 96.0 m. Reverse area magnitude (8 s to 12 s) = ½(1)(8) + (3)(8) = 28.0 m. Total distance = 96.0 + 28.0 = 124 m.

markScheme.criterion: Sums unsigned positive (96.0 m) and negative (28.0 m) velocity–time areas to obtain 124 m (D).

items.stem: Starting 30.0 m beyond the shaft loading datum at t = 0.0 s, an underground mine haulage skip executes the 12.0 s velocity–time profile shown. How far from the shaft loading datum does it come to rest?
items.workedSolution: Displacement during the 12 s run equals the trapezium area: Δx = ½(12 + 5)(14) = 119 m. Final position from the shaft loading datum = x₀ + Δx = 30 + 119 = 149 m.

markScheme.criterion: Adds trapezium area (119 m) to initial offset (30 m) to get 149 m (D).

items.stem: Sensors aboard a maglev propulsion test pod record the 15.0 s acceleration history shown from an initial eastward speed of 15.0 m s⁻¹. Find its velocity at the end of the 15.0 s window.
items.workedSolution: Positive a–t area (0 to 8 s) = 52.0 m s⁻¹; negative area magnitude (8 s to 15 s) = 24.0 m s⁻¹. Net Δv = 52.0 − 24.0 = 28.0 m s⁻¹. Final velocity = 15 + (28.0) = 43.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Combines net signed area (28.0 m s⁻¹) with u₀ = 15 m s⁻¹ to obtain 43.0 m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: The graph displays the linear momentum of a low-friction dynamics trolley (mass 1.6 kg) against time. What resultant force acts on it between t = 2.0 s and t = 5.0 s?
items.workedSolution: By Newton's second law, F = Δp / Δt = (12.8 − 3.2) / (5 − 2) = 3.20 N.

items.stem: Moving forward from x = 0.0 m with initial speed 4.0 m s⁻¹, a warehouse pallet shuttle (mass 4.0 kg) is subjected to the resultant force–displacement profile shown up to x = 12.0 m. How much net work is done on it over the 12.0 m displacement?
items.workedSolution: Forward work (0 to 10 m) = 120 J; resistive work (10 m to 12 m) = −4.00 J. Net work = 120 − 4.00 = 116 J.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts resistive triangle (4.00 J) from positive trapezium (120 J) to get 116 J (A).

items.stem: The stress–strain graph shows a cross-linked elastomer strip stretched reversibly through two piecewise-linear stages up to strain 0.5 (kink at strain 0.2). What work is done per unit volume in stretching the specimen to strain 0.5?
items.workedSolution: Work per unit volume equals area under the σ–ε graph (1 MPa × 1 = 1 MJ m⁻³): u = ½(0.2)(190) + ½(190 + 290)(0.3) = 91.0 MJ m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Sums triangle and trapezium areas under σ–ε curve to obtain 91.0 MJ m⁻³ (D).

options.distractorRationale: Multiplies peak stress by maximum strain without integrating the piecewise area.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Integrates only up to the limit of proportionality at ε₁ and omits the trapezium from ε₁ to ε_max.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Approximates the entire bilinear curve as a single triangle from (0, 0) to (ε_max, σ_max).

items.stem: Two-wire resistance readings R across a polypyrrole conductive polymer film include a fixed fixture offset R₀ when graphed against L / A from zero to 250.0 m⁻¹. Evaluate the resistivity ρ in Ω m.
items.workedSolution: Since R = ρ(L / A) + R₀, resistivity ρ equals the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A) = (41 − 7) / 250 = 0.136 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept R₀ = 7 Ω to obtain ρ = (41 − 7) / 250 = 0.136 Ω m (A).

items.stem: In a kinematics linearization lab (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²), a magnetic-cushion puck sliding down a tilted glass rail on a frictionless slope with sin θ = 0.3 passes s = 0.0 m at speed u₀ and continues to s = 2.5 m. Determine the gradient of the plotted v² versus s graph.
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 3.5 m² s⁻² and at s = 2.5 m, v² = 18.215 m² s⁻². Gradient = (18.215 − 3.5) / 2.5 = 2(9.81)(0.3) = 5.89 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 3.5 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.81 × 0.3) to get 5.89 m s⁻² (B).

items.stem: Over a 16.0 s transfer starting at x = 35.0 m from the optical home flag, a high-speed bottling-line transfer sled has the velocity–time graph shown. Calculate its average speed over the 16.0 s interval.
items.workedSolution: Distance travelled Δx = ½(16 + 6)(19) = 209 m (independent of the 35 m starting offset). Mean speed = 209 / 16 = 13.1 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Divides trapezium distance (209 m) by 16 s to obtain 13.1 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: A thruster acts from t = 3.0 s to t = 7.0 s on an ice-rink calibration sled of mass 2.4 kg, producing the momentum–time trace shown. What kinetic energy gain (net work) occurs over this interval?
items.workedSolution: Using E_k = p² / (2m), net work W = ΔE_k = (16.8² − 4.8²) / (2 × 2.4) = 54.0 J.

items.stem: Before a 2.0 s stator current pulse, a linear-motor launch shuttle of mass 4.0 kg has momentum 12.0 kg m s⁻¹. Using the force–time plot, find its momentum immediately after the pulse.
items.workedSolution: Impulse Δp = ½(2 + 1)(42) = 63.0 N s. Final momentum p_f = p₀ + Δp = 12 + 63.0 = 75.0 kg m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Adds impulse (63.0 N s) to p₀ = 12 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 75.0 kg m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: In an internal-resistance experiment on a portable photovoltaic module under constant irradiance, a student plots terminal potential difference V versus current I from 0.0 A to 2.5 A. Determine the gradient ΔV / ΔI of the line.
items.workedSolution: At I = 0.0 A, V = ε = 10 V; at I = 2.5 A, V = 4 V. Gradient = (4 − 10) / 2.5 = -2.40 V A⁻¹ (equal to −r).

items.stem: Photogate data for a PTFE-shod test block sliding down a polished low-friction chute accelerating down an incline (sin θ = 0.2, g = 9.8 m s⁻²) from s = 0.0 m to s = 2.0 m are linearized by plotting v² against s. What gradient does the best-fit line have?
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 2.2 m² s⁻² and at s = 2 m, v² = 10.04 m² s⁻². Gradient = (10.04 − 2.2) / 2 = 2(9.8)(0.2) = 3.92 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 2.2 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.8 × 0.2) to get 3.92 m s⁻² (C).

items.stem: Subtracting the constant zero-offset intercept on the F versus r⁻² plot (0.0 m⁻² to 50.0 m⁻²) for isolated brass domes mounted above an electronic microbalance, find the gradient in N m².
items.workedSolution: At r⁻² = 0.0 m⁻², tare offset F₀ = 0.3 N; at r⁻² = 50 m⁻², F = 1.9 N. Gradient = (1.9 − 0.3) / 50 = 0.0320 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts tare offset F₀ = 0.3 N to get (1.9 − 0.3) / 50 = 0.0320 N m² (B).

items.stem: Inspect the constant-gradient reversal stage from t = 4.0 s to t = 8.0 s for a cable-hauled alpine service car moving on a straight haulage section. What signed acceleration acts over this stage?
items.workedSolution: Between t = 4 s and t = 8 s, velocity changes from +12 m s⁻¹ to −4 m s⁻¹. Acceleration a = Δv / Δt = (−4 − 12) / (8 − 4) = -4.00 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δv / Δt = (−4 − 12) / (4) = -4.00 m s⁻² (B).

items.stem: In the velocity–time record for a wind-tunnel moving-ground carriage (initially 22.0 m from the nozzle datum line), uniform braking begins at t = 6.0 s and ends at rest at t = 8.0 s. Find the signed braking acceleration.
items.workedSolution: During braking from t = 6 s to t = 8 s, a = (0 − 12) / (8 − 6) = -6.00 m s⁻².

items.stem: At t = 0.0 s, a centrifuge carrier pod is already moving tangentially forward at 13.0 m s⁻¹. Its signed acceleration over the next 16.0 s (tangentially forward positive) is plotted. What maximum speed does it reach during the 16.0 s interval?
items.workedSolution: Speed increases while a > 0 (from t = 0.0 s until a = 0 at t = 10 s). Positive area Δv_max = (4)(5) + ½(6)(5) = 35.0 m s⁻¹. Maximum speed = u₀ + Δv_max = 13 + 35.0 = 48.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Integrates positive acceleration up to t = 10 s (35.0 m s⁻¹) and adds 13 m s⁻¹ to get 48.0 m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: Calculate the mean resultant force exerted during the 1.6 s docking vernier firing on a microgravity cargo pod (mass 1.5 kg, initial momentum 4.5 kg m s⁻¹) from the plotted F–t curve.
items.workedSolution: Total impulse J = ½(1.6 + 0.8)(40) = 48.0 N s. Mean force F_mean = J / Δt = 48.0 / 1.6 = 30.0 N.

items.stem: Evaluate the net work done by the resultant force on an automated mining skip (mass 5.0 kg, initial speed 5.0 m s⁻¹) between x = 0.0 m and x = 16.0 m using the graph.
items.workedSolution: Forward work (0 to 14 m) = 200 J; resistive work (14 m to 16 m) = −5.00 J. Net work = 200 − 5.00 = 195 J.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts resistive triangle (5.00 J) from positive trapezium (200 J) to get 195 J (C).

items.stem: Determine the strain energy stored per unit volume (in MJ m⁻³) when a regenerated silk-fibroin strand is loaded from zero strain to 0.8 along the plotted stress–strain curve (proportional limit at 0.4).
items.workedSolution: Work per unit volume equals area under the σ–ε graph (1 MPa × 1 = 1 MJ m⁻³): u = ½(0.4)(230) + ½(230 + 320)(0.4) = 156 MJ m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Sums triangle and trapezium areas under σ–ε curve to obtain 156 MJ m⁻³ (B).

items.stem: Inspect the linear discharge characteristic V versus I (0.0 A to 1.6 A) for a thermoelectric Seebeck generator. What is the mean value of V across this interval?
items.workedSolution: Terminal p.d. varies linearly from 5.8 V at I = 0.0 A to 2.6 V at I = 1.6 A, so V_mean = ½(5.8 + 2.6) = 4.20 V.

markScheme.criterion: Averages endpoint voltages ½(5.8 + 2.6) = 4.20 V (B).

items.stem: In a materials conductivity test on a germanium crystal prism, measured resistance R varies linearly with L / A up to 80.0 m⁻¹ as shown. Extract the bulk resistivity ρ.
items.workedSolution: Since R = ρ(L / A) + R₀, resistivity ρ equals the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A) = (25 − 5) / 80 = 0.250 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept R₀ = 5 Ω to obtain ρ = (25 − 5) / 80 = 0.250 Ω m (D).

items.stem: How large is the slope ΔF / Δ(r⁻²) of the inverse-square linearization graph recorded up to 20.0 m⁻² using gold-leaf coated polymer spheres on a capacitive force transducer?
items.workedSolution: At r⁻² = 0.0 m⁻², tare offset F₀ = 0.1 N; at r⁻² = 20 m⁻², F = 1.1 N. Gradient = (1.1 − 0.1) / 20 = 0.0500 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts tare offset F₀ = 0.1 N to get (1.1 − 0.1) / 20 = 0.0500 N m² (C).

items.stem: Sensors record an inter-terminal airport monorail initially at x = 40.0 m relative to a concourse datum post. Using the velocity–time plot up to t = 20.0 s, determine its final coordinate x.
items.workedSolution: Displacement during the 20 s run equals the trapezium area: Δx = ½(20 + 10)(18) = 270 m. Final position from the concourse datum post = x₀ + Δx = 40 + 270 = 310 m.

markScheme.criterion: Adds trapezium area (270 m) to initial offset (40 m) to get 310 m (D).

items.stem: In a linear dynamics experiment, an air-track glider of mass 4.0 kg moves in a straight line with momentum varying as shown. How much net work is done on it between t = 4.0 s and t = 8.0 s?
items.workedSolution: Using E_k = p² / (2m), net work W = ΔE_k = (28² − 8²) / (2 × 4) = 90.0 J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies W = (p₂² − p₁²) / (2m) = (28² − 8²) / (8) = 90.0 J (A).

items.stem: Refer to the force–time profile of a cold-gas thruster burn on a cold-gas attitude probe of mass 5.0 kg (initial momentum 15.0 kg m s⁻¹). By how much does its speed increase over the 4.0 s pulse?
items.workedSolution: Impulse J = area under F–t trapezium = ½(4 + 2)(35) = 105 N s. Speed increase Δv = J / m = 105 / 5 = 21.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Computes J = 105 N s and Δv = J / 5 = 21.0 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: In a tensile materials test, a cross-linked elastomer strip obeys Hooke's law up to a strain of 0.3 before softening up to strain 0.6, as shown on the stress–strain graph. What is the Young's modulus of the material in the initial linear region?
items.workedSolution: Up to the limit of proportionality at ε = 0.3, stress reaches 210 MPa. Young's modulus E = σ / ε = 210 / 0.3 = 700 MPa.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates initial linear gradient E = 210 / 0.3 = 700 MPa (D).

items.stem: Inspect the linear plot of measured resistance R versus L / A (spanning 0.0 m⁻¹ to 160.0 m⁻¹) for a polypyrrole conductive polymer film. What is the material's resistivity ρ?
items.workedSolution: Since R = ρ(L / A) + R₀, resistivity ρ equals the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A) = (26 − 6) / 160 = 0.125 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept R₀ = 6 Ω to obtain ρ = (26 − 6) / 160 = 0.125 Ω m (A).

items.stem: Taking g = 9.8 m s⁻², a magnetic-cushion puck sliding down a tilted glass rail descends a smooth plane inclined at sin θ = 0.45, passing s = 0.0 m already in motion. From the v² against s plot up to 1.2 m, find the slope Δ(v²) / Δs.
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 3.8 m² s⁻² and at s = 1.2 m, v² = 14.384 m² s⁻². Gradient = (14.384 − 3.8) / 1.2 = 2(9.8)(0.45) = 8.82 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 3.8 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.8 × 0.45) to get 8.82 m s⁻² (D).

items.stem: Refer to the signed velocity–time graph for an underwater ROV thruster sled travelling along a taut calibration tether. Determine the resultant displacement after 15.0 s.
items.workedSolution: Velocity reaches zero at t = 9 s. Positive area = 130 m and area below the axis has magnitude 55.0 m. Net displacement = 130 − 55.0 = 75.0 m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts reverse area (55.0 m) from forward area (130 m) to obtain 75.0 m (C).

items.stem: Initially travelling forward at 9.0 m s⁻¹, an electromagnetic catapult shuttle undergoes the signed acceleration–time profile shown for 6.0 s. What is its velocity at t = 6.0 s?
items.workedSolution: Positive a–t area (0 to 3 s) = 24.0 m s⁻¹; negative area magnitude (3 s to 6 s) = 15.0 m s⁻¹. Net Δv = 24.0 − 15.0 = 9.00 m s⁻¹. Final velocity = 9 + (9.00) = 18.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Combines net signed area (9.00 m s⁻¹) with u₀ = 9 m s⁻¹ to obtain 18.0 m s⁻¹ (A).

items.stem: Moving in a straight line with initial momentum 2.4 kg m s⁻¹, a crash-barrier test sled (mass 0.8 kg) undergoes the 0.5 s hydraulic arrester pulse shown. What is its final momentum at t = 0.5 s?
items.workedSolution: Impulse Δp = ½(0.5 + 0.3)(42) = 16.8 N s. Final momentum p_f = p₀ + Δp = 2.4 + 16.8 = 19.2 kg m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Adds impulse (16.8 N s) to p₀ = 2.4 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 19.2 kg m s⁻¹ (A).

items.stem: Moving forward from x = 0.0 m with initial speed 6.0 m s⁻¹, a pneumatic factory transfer cart (mass 3.0 kg) is subjected to the resultant force–displacement profile shown up to x = 15.0 m. How much net work is done on it over the 15.0 m displacement?
items.workedSolution: Forward work (0 to 12 m) = 162 J; resistive work (12 m to 15 m) = −9.00 J. Net work = 162 − 9.00 = 153 J.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts resistive triangle (9.00 J) from positive trapezium (162 J) to get 153 J (B).

items.stem: The stress–strain graph shows a vulcanized neoprene damper rod stretched reversibly through two piecewise-linear stages up to strain 0.4 (kink at strain 0.2). What work is done per unit volume in stretching the specimen to strain 0.4?
items.workedSolution: Work per unit volume equals area under the σ–ε graph (1 MPa × 1 = 1 MJ m⁻³): u = ½(0.2)(120) + ½(120 + 180)(0.2) = 42.0 MJ m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Sums triangle and trapezium areas under σ–ε curve to obtain 42.0 MJ m⁻³ (B).

items.stem: Load tests on a portable photovoltaic module under constant irradiance up to I = 0.8 A produce the straight-line V–I trace shown. Calculate the signed gradient of the graph in V A⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: At I = 0.0 A, V = ε = 4.2 V; at I = 0.8 A, V = 2.2 V. Gradient = (2.2 − 4.2) / 0.8 = -2.50 V A⁻¹ (equal to −r).

items.stem: Speed-squared readings v² are graphed against displacement s (0.0 m to 1.5 m) for a PTFE-shod test block sliding down a polished low-friction chute on a frictionless ramp of sin θ = 0.3 where g = 9.81 m s⁻². Calculate the gradient of the line.
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 4.5 m² s⁻² and at s = 1.5 m, v² = 13.329 m² s⁻². Gradient = (13.329 − 4.5) / 1.5 = 2(9.81)(0.3) = 5.89 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 4.5 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.81 × 0.3) to get 5.89 m s⁻² (B).

items.stem: Examine the straight-line graph of balance force F against r⁻² (spanning 0.0 m⁻² to 16.0 m⁻²) for isolated brass domes mounted above an electronic microbalance. What value does its gradient take?
items.workedSolution: At r⁻² = 0.0 m⁻², tare offset F₀ = 0.12 N; at r⁻² = 16 m⁻², F = 1.16 N. Gradient = (1.16 − 0.12) / 16 = 0.0650 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts tare offset F₀ = 0.12 N to get (1.16 − 0.12) / 16 = 0.0650 N m² (C).

items.stem: Between t = 5.0 s and t = 9.0 s, a reverse thrust acts on a cleanroom wafer transport shuttle along a linear air bearing. Determine the acceleration indicated by the velocity–time plot.
items.workedSolution: Between t = 5 s and t = 9 s, velocity changes from +24 m s⁻¹ to −8 m s⁻¹. Acceleration a = Δv / Δt = (−8 − 24) / (9 − 5) = -8.00 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δv / Δt = (−8 − 24) / (4) = -8.00 m s⁻² (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Divides the velocity change by t₃ rather than the elapsed stage duration (t₃ − t₂).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses v_pos − |v_neg| instead of (−v_neg − v_pos) for Δv across the zero-velocity axis.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes the slope magnitude accurately but omits the negative sign of the acceleration.

items.stem: Starting at x = 28.0 m from a lock-gate reference mark, a canal lock towing locomotive completes the 16.0 s journey shown on the velocity–time graph, braking uniformly from t = 12.0 s to t = 16.0 s. What is its acceleration during braking?
items.workedSolution: During braking from t = 12 s to t = 16 s, a = (0 − 20) / (16 − 12) = -5.00 m s⁻².

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Finds the magnitude of deceleration but omits the negative sign required for signed acceleration.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Δt / Δv instead of computing Δv / Δt.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Divides the velocity drop by the full journey duration t₃ instead of the braking duration (t₃ − t₂).

items.stem: An accelerometer mounted on a centrifuge carrier pod records the 8.0 s profile shown, starting from an initial tangentially forward velocity of 9.0 m s⁻¹. Determine the greatest tangentially forward speed attained.
items.workedSolution: Speed increases while a > 0 (from t = 0.0 s until a = 0 at t = 4 s). Positive area Δv_max = (2)(6) + ½(2)(6) = 18.0 m s⁻¹. Maximum speed = u₀ + Δv_max = 9 + 18.0 = 27.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Integrates positive acceleration up to t = 4 s (18.0 m s⁻¹) and adds 9 m s⁻¹ to get 27.0 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: A 2.0 kg unit (a magnetic-launch coaster bogie) enters an instrumented zone at 7.0 m s⁻¹. From the resultant force–displacement graph over 16.0 m, calculate its exit speed at x = 16.0 m.
items.workedSolution: Positive work (0 to 12 m) = ½(12 + 6)(10) = 90.0 J. Resistive work (12 m to 16 m) = −½(4)(2) = −4.00 J. Net work W = 86.0 J. From ½mv² = ½mu₀² + W, v = √(7² + 2 × 86.0 / 2) = 11.6 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Finds net work W = 86.0 J and v = √(7² + 2W/2) = 11.6 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: The tensile stress–strain curve for a high-density polyethylene filament is linear from 0.0 to strain 0.25 and reaches strain 0.5. Determine the Young's modulus in MPa.
items.workedSolution: Up to the limit of proportionality at ε = 0.25, stress reaches 230 MPa. Young's modulus E = σ / ε = 230 / 0.25 = 920 MPa.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates initial linear gradient E = 230 / 0.25 = 920 MPa (B).

items.stem: Eliminating the constant probe-lead offset from the R versus L / A graph (plotted to 400.0 m⁻¹), find the resistivity ρ of a germanium crystal prism.
items.workedSolution: Since R = ρ(L / A) + R₀, resistivity ρ equals the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A) = (30 − 6) / 400 = 0.0600 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept R₀ = 6 Ω to obtain ρ = (30 − 6) / 400 = 0.0600 Ω m (D).

items.stem: How steep (in m s⁻²) is the linear v² versus s graph recorded over 2.0 m for a card-carrying glider on an inclined linear air track on a smooth slope (sin θ = 0.25, g = 9.8 m s⁻²)?
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 3 m² s⁻² and at s = 2 m, v² = 12.8 m² s⁻². Gradient = (12.8 − 3) / 2 = 2(9.8)(0.25) = 4.90 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 3 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.8 × 0.25) to get 4.90 m s⁻² (C).

items.stem: At t = 0.0 s, a solar-powered desert research rover is stationary at a position 45.0 m ahead of a base-camp beacon. It then moves forward along a straight guideway according to the velocity–time graph for 20.0 s. What is its final distance from the base-camp beacon at t = 20.0 s?
items.workedSolution: Displacement during the 20 s run equals the trapezium area: Δx = ½(20 + 8)(24) = 336 m. Final position from the base-camp beacon = x₀ + Δx = 45 + 336 = 381 m.

markScheme.criterion: Adds trapezium area (336 m) to initial offset (45 m) to get 381 m (D).

items.stem: Motion sensors track the momentum of a satellite attitude-test mass of mass 3.2 kg. Determine the magnitude of the resultant force acting from t = 3.0 s to t = 8.0 s.
items.workedSolution: By Newton's second law, F = Δp / Δt = (22.4 − 6.4) / (8 − 3) = 3.20 N.

items.stem: Having initial forward momentum 3.6 kg m s⁻¹, a rail-mounted docking target of mass 1.2 kg experiences a collinear spring buffer contact over 1.0 s as shown on the force–time graph. What is its change in speed Δv?
items.workedSolution: Impulse J = area under F–t trapezium = ½(1 + 0.4)(40) = 28.0 N s. Speed increase Δv = J / m = 28.0 / 1.2 = 23.3 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Computes J = 28.0 N s and Δv = J / 1.2 = 23.3 m s⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: By varying a rheostat connected to a vanadium redox flow single cell, terminal voltage V is graphed against current I up to 4.0 A. Find the signed slope ΔV / ΔI.
items.workedSolution: At I = 0.0 A, V = ε = 15 V; at I = 4 A, V = 5 V. Gradient = (5 − 15) / 4 = -2.50 V A⁻¹ (equal to −r).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates (5 − 15) / 4 = -2.50 V A⁻¹ (A).

items.stem: Examine the straight-line plot of v² against track distance s up to 2.0 m for a dual-photogate brass cylinder released past an upper light gate (ramp sin θ = 0.3, g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Evaluate its gradient.
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 2.5 m² s⁻² and at s = 2 m, v² = 14.272 m² s⁻². Gradient = (14.272 − 2.5) / 2 = 2(9.81)(0.3) = 5.89 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 2.5 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.81 × 0.3) to get 5.89 m s⁻² (D).

items.stem: To test Coulomb's inverse-square law using conductive carbon spheres mounted in a dry-nitrogen force cell with an unzeroed tare offset F₀, the force reading F is plotted against inverse-square separation (r⁻²) up to 100.0 m⁻², following F = k|Q₁Q₂|r⁻² + F₀. What is the gradient k|Q₁Q₂| of the line?
items.workedSolution: At r⁻² = 0.0 m⁻², tare offset F₀ = 0.2 N; at r⁻² = 100 m⁻², F = 1.8 N. Gradient = (1.8 − 0.2) / 100 = 0.0160 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts tare offset F₀ = 0.2 N to get (1.8 − 0.2) / 100 = 0.0160 N m² (B).

items.stem: On a straight test section, a drop-tower counterbalance carriage moves inside a vertical guide shaft (upward positive) as shown on the velocity–time graph. What is its net displacement from t = 0.0 s to t = 14.0 s?
items.workedSolution: Velocity reaches zero at t = 9 s. Positive area = 117 m and area below the axis has magnitude 27.0 m. Net displacement = 117 − 27.0 = 90.0 m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts reverse area (27.0 m) from forward area (117 m) to obtain 90.0 m (A).

items.stem: Beginning 32.0 m past a western end-stop, a shipyard gantry crane crab follows the velocity–time profile shown over 10.0 s. What is its mean speed during the 10.0 s journey?
items.workedSolution: Distance travelled Δx = ½(10 + 6)(19) = 152 m (independent of the 32 m starting offset). Mean speed = 152 / 10 = 15.2 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Divides trapezium distance (152 m) by 10 s to obtain 15.2 m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: Telemetry shows the forward acceleration of an electromagnetic catapult shuttle over 10.0 s. Given an initial forward velocity of 8.0 m s⁻¹ at t = 0.0 s, calculate the velocity at t = 10.0 s.
items.workedSolution: Positive a–t area (0 to 5 s) = 28.0 m s⁻¹; negative area magnitude (5 s to 10 s) = 16.0 m s⁻¹. Net Δv = 28.0 − 16.0 = 12.0 m s⁻¹. Final velocity = 8 + (12.0) = 20.0 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Before a 5.0 s pulsed ion-beam firing, a Hall-effect thruster test rig of mass 6.0 kg has momentum 18.0 kg m s⁻¹. Using the force–time plot, find its momentum immediately after the pulse.
items.workedSolution: Impulse Δp = ½(5 + 3)(40) = 160 N s. Final momentum p_f = p₀ + Δp = 18 + 160 = 178 kg m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Adds impulse (160 N s) to p₀ = 18 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 178 kg m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: The resultant force in the direction of motion of a linear dynamo test sled (mass 3.2 kg, initial speed 4.0 m s⁻¹) is plotted over 14.0 m. Determine its speed at x = 14.0 m.
items.workedSolution: Positive work (0 to 11 m) = ½(11 + 6)(16) = 136 J. Resistive work (11 m to 14 m) = −½(3)(4) = −6.00 J. Net work W = 130 J. From ½mv² = ½mu₀² + W, v = √(4² + 2 × 130 / 3.2) = 9.86 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Finds net work W = 130 J and v = √(4² + 2W/3.2) = 9.86 m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: Refer to the tensile stress–strain plot for a vulcanized neoprene damper rod, whose limit of proportionality lies at strain 0.5. Calculate its initial Young's modulus.
items.workedSolution: Up to the limit of proportionality at ε = 0.5, stress reaches 280 MPa. Young's modulus E = σ / ε = 280 / 0.5 = 560 MPa.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates initial linear gradient E = 280 / 0.5 = 560 MPa (C).

items.stem: Examine the linear V–I characteristic recorded for a portable photovoltaic module under constant irradiance between zero current and 1.0 A. What is its signed gradient?
items.workedSolution: At I = 0.0 A, V = ε = 5.5 V; at I = 1 A, V = 2.5 V. Gradient = (2.5 − 5.5) / 1 = -3.00 V A⁻¹ (equal to −r).

items.stem: Using crocodile clips with constant contact resistance R₀, a student measures total resistance R of an isotropic graphite heating element for different length-to-area ratios (L / A) up to 200.0 m⁻¹, so R = ρ(L / A) + R₀. From the plotted line, what is the resistivity ρ of the material?
items.workedSolution: Since R = ρ(L / A) + R₀, resistivity ρ equals the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A) = (25 − 5) / 200 = 0.100 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept R₀ = 5 Ω to obtain ρ = (25 − 5) / 200 = 0.100 Ω m (A).

items.stem: Readings F from isolated brass domes mounted above an electronic microbalance are linearized against r⁻² from 0.0 m⁻² to 40.0 m⁻². Accounting for the systematic zero-offset F₀, determine the gradient ΔF / Δ(r⁻²).
items.workedSolution: At r⁻² = 0.0 m⁻², tare offset F₀ = 0.15 N; at r⁻² = 40 m⁻², F = 1.35 N. Gradient = (1.35 − 0.15) / 40 = 0.0300 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts tare offset F₀ = 0.15 N to get (1.35 − 0.15) / 40 = 0.0300 N m² (A).

items.stem: In the velocity–time record for an underground mine haulage skip (initially 38.0 m from the shaft loading datum), uniform braking begins at t = 12.0 s and ends at rest at t = 16.0 s. Find the signed braking acceleration.
items.workedSolution: During braking from t = 12 s to t = 16 s, a = (0 − 16) / (16 − 12) = -4.00 m s⁻².

items.stem: The graph displays the linear momentum of a low-friction dynamics trolley (mass 6.0 kg) against time. What resultant force acts on it between t = 4.0 s and t = 10.0 s?
items.workedSolution: By Newton's second law, F = Δp / Δt = (36 − 12) / (10 − 4) = 4.00 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F = Δp / Δt = (36 − 12) / (6) = 4.00 N (D).

items.stem: Calculate the mean resultant force exerted during the 2.0 s controlled gas-jet pulse on a ballistic pendulum carriage (mass 2.0 kg, initial momentum 8.0 kg m s⁻¹) from the plotted F–t curve.
items.workedSolution: Total impulse J = ½(2 + 1)(35) = 52.5 N s. Mean force F_mean = J / Δt = 52.5 / 2 = 26.3 N.

markScheme.criterion: Divides impulse (52.5 N s) by 2 s to obtain 26.3 N (C).

items.stem: The stress–strain graph shows a high-density polyethylene filament stretched reversibly through two piecewise-linear stages up to strain 0.6 (kink at strain 0.3). What work is done per unit volume in stretching the specimen to strain 0.6?
items.workedSolution: Work per unit volume equals area under the σ–ε graph (1 MPa × 1 = 1 MJ m⁻³): u = ½(0.3)(180) + ½(180 + 250)(0.3) = 91.5 MJ m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Sums triangle and trapezium areas under σ–ε curve to obtain 91.5 MJ m⁻³ (B).

items.stem: Total circuit resistance R (including lead resistance R₀) is plotted against geometric ratio L / A up to 250.0 m⁻¹ for a germanium crystal prism. Calculate the electrical resistivity ρ.
items.workedSolution: Since R = ρ(L / A) + R₀, resistivity ρ equals the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A) = (32 − 8) / 250 = 0.0960 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept R₀ = 8 Ω to obtain ρ = (32 − 8) / 250 = 0.0960 Ω m (A).

items.stem: An optical timer measures speed v of a card-carrying glider on an inclined linear air track at positions up to s = 2.5 m along a frictionless incline (sin θ = 0.2, g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What is the slope of the resulting v²–s graph?
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 2.8 m² s⁻² and at s = 2.5 m, v² = 12.61 m² s⁻². Gradient = (12.61 − 2.8) / 2.5 = 2(9.81)(0.2) = 3.92 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 2.8 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.81 × 0.2) to get 3.92 m s⁻² (B).

items.stem: The velocity–time profile shows an automated rail inspection trolley reversing motion along a straight viaduct rail with eastward defined as positive. Calculate the total scalar distance travelled between t = 0.0 s and t = 10.0 s.
items.workedSolution: Velocity crosses zero at t = 7 s. Forward area (0 to 7 s) = ½(2)(16) + (3)(16) + ½(2)(16) = 80.0 m. Reverse area magnitude (7 s to 10 s) = ½(1)(8) + (2)(8) = 20.0 m. Total distance = 80.0 + 20.0 = 100 m.

markScheme.criterion: Sums unsigned positive (80.0 m) and negative (20.0 m) velocity–time areas to obtain 100 m (A).

items.stem: Moving forward at 11.0 m s⁻¹ at t = 0.0 s, an aerotow winch launch carriage experiences the acceleration–time history plotted over 10.0 s. Find its peak speed.
items.workedSolution: Speed increases while a > 0 (from t = 0.0 s until a = 0 at t = 4 s). Positive area Δv_max = (2)(10) + ½(2)(10) = 30.0 m s⁻¹. Maximum speed = u₀ + Δv_max = 11 + 30.0 = 41.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Integrates positive acceleration up to t = 4 s (30.0 m s⁻¹) and adds 11 m s⁻¹ to get 41.0 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: A stator current pulse acts for 0.8 s in the direction of motion of a linear-motor launch shuttle (mass 2.0 kg, initial momentum 6.0 kg m s⁻¹). Using the plotted force–time profile, determine Δv.
items.workedSolution: Impulse J = area under F–t trapezium = ½(0.8 + 0.4)(50) = 30.0 N s. Speed increase Δv = J / m = 30.0 / 2 = 15.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Computes J = 30.0 N s and Δv = J / 2 = 15.0 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: Passing x = 0.0 m with speed 5.0 m s⁻¹, a wind-propelled land-yacht rig of mass 2.0 kg experiences the collinear resultant force plotted against displacement up to x = 10.0 m. What is its speed at x = 10.0 m?
items.workedSolution: Positive work (0 to 8 m) = ½(8 + 4)(12) = 72.0 J. Resistive work (8 m to 10 m) = −½(2)(4) = −4.00 J. Net work W = 68.0 J. From ½mv² = ½mu₀² + W, v = √(5² + 2 × 68.0 / 2) = 9.64 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Finds net work W = 68.0 J and v = √(5² + 2W/2) = 9.64 m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: In a tensile materials test, a bio-derived collagen fibre bundle obeys Hooke's law up to a strain of 0.2 before softening up to strain 0.4, as shown on the stress–strain graph. What is the Young's modulus of the material in the initial linear region?
items.workedSolution: Up to the limit of proportionality at ε = 0.2, stress reaches 150 MPa. Young's modulus E = σ / ε = 150 / 0.2 = 750 MPa.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates initial linear gradient E = 150 / 0.2 = 750 MPa (B).

items.stem: A variable load resistor is connected across a vanadium redox flow single cell, and the terminal potential difference V is plotted against current I up to 2.0 A. According to V = ε − Ir, what is the signed gradient of this graph?
items.workedSolution: At I = 0.0 A, V = ε = 7 V; at I = 2 A, V = 3.4 V. Gradient = (3.4 − 7) / 2 = -1.80 V A⁻¹ (equal to −r).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates (3.4 − 7) / 2 = -1.80 V A⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: Using two light gates in a gravitational field g = 9.8 m s⁻², a student records speed v of a dual-photogate brass cylinder released past an upper light gate (inclination sin θ = 0.35) after passing an initial gate at s = 0.0 m with speed u₀ > 0, plotting v² against distance s up to 2.0 m. According to v² = u₀² + 2as, what is the gradient Δ(v²) / Δs of the line?
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 4 m² s⁻² and at s = 2 m, v² = 17.72 m² s⁻². Gradient = (17.72 − 4) / 2 = 2(9.8)(0.35) = 6.86 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 4 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.8 × 0.35) to get 6.86 m s⁻² (B).

items.stem: The linearized Coulomb plot shows balance force F versus inverse-square separation r⁻² up to 50.0 m⁻² for conductive carbon spheres mounted in a dry-nitrogen force cell. Calculate the gradient of the line in N m².
items.workedSolution: At r⁻² = 0.0 m⁻², tare offset F₀ = 0.25 N; at r⁻² = 50 m⁻², F = 1.65 N. Gradient = (1.65 − 0.25) / 50 = 0.0280 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts tare offset F₀ = 0.25 N to get (1.65 − 0.25) / 50 = 0.0280 N m² (B).

items.stem: A motion sensor tracks a magnetic-levitation shuttle pod on a horizontal vacuum test guideway for 12.0 s, taking to the right velocity as positive. Find the net signed displacement at t = 12.0 s relative to its starting point.
items.workedSolution: Velocity reaches zero at t = 8 s. Positive area = 96.0 m and area below the axis has magnitude 28.0 m. Net displacement = 96.0 − 28.0 = 68.0 m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts reverse area (28.0 m) from forward area (96.0 m) to obtain 68.0 m (C).

items.stem: Over a 12.0 s transfer starting at x = 30.0 m from the nozzle datum line, a wind-tunnel moving-ground carriage has the velocity–time graph shown. Calculate its average speed over the 12.0 s interval.
items.workedSolution: Distance travelled Δx = ½(12 + 5)(14) = 119 m (independent of the 30 m starting offset). Mean speed = 119 / 12 = 9.92 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Divides trapezium distance (119 m) by 12 s to obtain 9.92 m s⁻¹ (D).

options.distractorRationale: Confuses the cruise plateau velocity with the journey-wide mean speed.

options.label: C

items.stem: After passing t = 0.0 s with forward speed 13.0 m s⁻¹, an electromagnetic catapult shuttle experiences the 10.0 s acceleration curve plotted. Determine its final velocity at t = 10.0 s.
items.workedSolution: Positive a–t area (0 to 5 s) = 24.0 m s⁻¹; negative area magnitude (5 s to 10 s) = 14.0 m s⁻¹. Net Δv = 24.0 − 14.0 = 10.0 m s⁻¹. Final velocity = 13 + (10.0) = 23.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Combines net signed area (10.0 m s⁻¹) with u₀ = 13 m s⁻¹ to obtain 23.0 m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: Motion sensors track the momentum of a linear air-bearing carriage of mass 1.6 kg. Determine the magnitude of the resultant force acting from t = 2.0 s to t = 5.0 s.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies Δp by Δt instead of evaluating the rate of change of momentum Δp / Δt.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Divides Δp / Δt by mass m, obtaining acceleration rather than resultant force.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes the secant ratio p₂ / t₂ from the origin, ignoring both initial momentum p₁ and start time t₁.

items.stem: Evaluate the net work done by the resultant force on an automated mining skip (mass 4.0 kg, initial speed 4.0 m s⁻¹) between x = 0.0 m and x = 12.0 m using the graph.
items.workedSolution: Forward work (0 to 10 m) = 120 J; resistive work (10 m to 12 m) = −4.00 J. Net work = 120 − 4.00 = 116 J.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts resistive triangle (4.00 J) from positive trapezium (120 J) to get 116 J (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Adds the area below the displacement axis instead of subtracting negative resistive work.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes total final kinetic energy (½mu₀² + W) rather than the net work done W.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Integrates only up to x = x₃ where F = 0 and ignores the braking region from x₃ to x₄.

items.stem: Determine the strain energy stored per unit volume (in MJ m⁻³) when an extruded fluoropolymer ribbon is loaded from zero strain to 0.5 along the plotted stress–strain curve (proportional limit at 0.2).
items.workedSolution: Work per unit volume equals area under the σ–ε graph (1 MPa × 1 = 1 MJ m⁻³): u = ½(0.2)(190) + ½(190 + 290)(0.3) = 91.0 MJ m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Sums triangle and trapezium areas under σ–ε curve to obtain 91.0 MJ m⁻³ (C).

items.stem: The linearized graph shows measured resistance R versus L / A for an isotropic graphite heating element over 0.0 m⁻¹ to 500.0 m⁻¹. Accounting for the non-zero contact-resistance intercept, determine ρ.
items.workedSolution: Since R = ρ(L / A) + R₀, resistivity ρ equals the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A) = (51 − 12) / 500 = 0.0780 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept R₀ = 12 Ω to obtain ρ = (51 − 12) / 500 = 0.0780 Ω m (B).

items.stem: In a kinematics linearization lab (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²), a levitated neodymium shuttle descending an inclined guide on a frictionless slope with sin θ = 0.6 passes s = 0.0 m at speed u₀ and continues to s = 1.0 m. Determine the gradient of the plotted v² versus s graph.
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 3.2 m² s⁻² and at s = 1 m, v² = 14.972 m² s⁻². Gradient = (14.972 − 3.2) / 1 = 2(9.81)(0.6) = 11.8 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 3.2 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.81 × 0.6) to get 11.8 m s⁻² (C).

items.stem: Starting at x = 35.0 m from a concourse datum post, an inter-terminal airport monorail completes the 16.0 s journey shown on the velocity–time graph, braking uniformly from t = 10.0 s to t = 16.0 s. What is its acceleration during braking?
items.workedSolution: During braking from t = 10 s to t = 16 s, a = (0 − 19) / (16 − 10) = -3.17 m s⁻².

items.stem: The momentum–time graph is recorded for an air-track glider (mass 2.4 kg) travelling along a straight guide. Calculate the net work done on the object from t = 3.0 s to t = 7.0 s.
items.workedSolution: Using E_k = p² / (2m), net work W = ΔE_k = (16.8² − 4.8²) / (2 × 2.4) = 54.0 J.

items.stem: During a 2.0 s cold-gas thruster burn, a cold-gas attitude probe (mass 4.0 kg, initial momentum 12.0 kg m s⁻¹) experiences the force–time profile shown. What is the time-averaged resultant force over the 2.0 s interval?
items.workedSolution: Total impulse J = ½(2 + 1)(42) = 63.0 N s. Mean force F_mean = J / Δt = 63.0 / 2 = 31.5 N.

markScheme.criterion: Divides impulse (63.0 N s) by 2 s to obtain 31.5 N (D).

items.stem: Inspect the linear discharge characteristic V versus I (0.0 A to 2.5 A) for an alkaline lantern battery. What is the mean value of V across this interval?
items.workedSolution: Terminal p.d. varies linearly from 10 V at I = 0.0 A to 4 V at I = 2.5 A, so V_mean = ½(10 + 4) = 7.00 V.

markScheme.criterion: Averages endpoint voltages ½(10 + 4) = 7.00 V (D).

items.stem: Photogate data for a steel ball bearing rolling in a V-channel with negligible rotational loss accelerating down an incline (sin θ = 0.25, g = 9.8 m s⁻²) from s = 0.0 m to s = 1.6 m are linearized by plotting v² against s. What gradient does the best-fit line have?
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 4.2 m² s⁻² and at s = 1.6 m, v² = 12.04 m² s⁻². Gradient = (12.04 − 4.2) / 1.6 = 2(9.8)(0.25) = 4.90 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 4.2 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.8 × 0.25) to get 4.90 m s⁻² (C).

items.stem: In an electrostatics investigation with precision electrostatic spheres on a sapphire-pivot balance, F is plotted against r⁻² up to 25.0 m⁻². Extract the proportionality constant k|Q₁Q₂| given by the slope.
items.workedSolution: At r⁻² = 0.0 m⁻², tare offset F₀ = 0.1 N; at r⁻² = 25 m⁻², F = 1.25 N. Gradient = (1.25 − 0.1) / 25 = 0.0460 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts tare offset F₀ = 0.1 N to get (1.25 − 0.1) / 25 = 0.0460 N m² (A).

items.stem: Engineers log the signed velocity of a cable-hauled alpine service car on a straight haulage section over 10.0 s. How much total distance does it cover before the recording ends at t = 10.0 s?
items.workedSolution: Velocity crosses zero at t = 7 s. Forward area (0 to 7 s) = ½(2)(12) + (2)(12) + ½(3)(12) = 54.0 m. Reverse area magnitude (7 s to 10 s) = ½(1)(4) + (2)(4) = 10.0 m. Total distance = 54.0 + 10.0 = 64.0 m.

markScheme.criterion: Sums unsigned positive (54.0 m) and negative (10.0 m) velocity–time areas to obtain 64.0 m (C).

items.stem: Sensors record a linear-induction baggage carrier initially at x = 22.0 m relative to a sorting-hall origin sensor. Using the velocity–time plot up to t = 8.0 s, determine its final coordinate x.
items.workedSolution: Displacement during the 8 s run equals the trapezium area: Δx = ½(8 + 4)(12) = 72.0 m. Final position from the sorting-hall origin sensor = x₀ + Δx = 22 + 72.0 = 94.0 m.

markScheme.criterion: Adds trapezium area (72.0 m) to initial offset (22 m) to get 94.0 m (C).

items.stem: How fast is an aerotow winch launch carriage travelling at its instant of greatest speed during the 12.0 s acceleration–time record shown, given an initial forward velocity of 14.0 m s⁻¹?
items.workedSolution: Speed increases while a > 0 (from t = 0.0 s until a = 0 at t = 6 s). Positive area Δv_max = (2)(6) + ½(4)(6) = 24.0 m s⁻¹. Maximum speed = u₀ + Δv_max = 14 + 24.0 = 38.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Integrates positive acceleration up to t = 6 s (24.0 m s⁻¹) and adds 14 m s⁻¹ to get 38.0 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: Refer to the force–time profile of a hydraulic arrester pulse on a crash-barrier test sled of mass 1.5 kg (initial momentum 4.5 kg m s⁻¹). By how much does its speed increase over the 1.6 s pulse?
items.workedSolution: Impulse J = area under F–t trapezium = ½(1.6 + 0.8)(40) = 48.0 N s. Speed increase Δv = J / m = 48.0 / 1.5 = 32.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Computes J = 48.0 N s and Δv = J / 1.5 = 32.0 m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: Moving forward from x = 0.0 m with initial speed 5.0 m s⁻¹, a pneumatic factory transfer cart (mass 5.0 kg) is subjected to the resultant force–displacement profile shown up to x = 16.0 m. How much net work is done on it over the 16.0 m displacement?
items.workedSolution: Forward work (0 to 14 m) = 200 J; resistive work (14 m to 16 m) = −5.00 J. Net work = 200 − 5.00 = 195 J.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts resistive triangle (5.00 J) from positive trapezium (200 J) to get 195 J (D).

items.stem: The stress–strain graph shows a bio-derived collagen fibre bundle stretched reversibly through two piecewise-linear stages up to strain 0.8 (kink at strain 0.4). What work is done per unit volume in stretching the specimen to strain 0.8?
items.workedSolution: Work per unit volume equals area under the σ–ε graph (1 MPa × 1 = 1 MJ m⁻³): u = ½(0.4)(230) + ½(230 + 320)(0.4) = 156 MJ m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Sums triangle and trapezium areas under σ–ε curve to obtain 156 MJ m⁻³ (B).

options.distractorRationale: Multiplies peak stress by maximum strain without integrating the piecewise area.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Integrates only up to the limit of proportionality at ε₁ and omits the trapezium from ε₁ to ε_max.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Approximates the entire bilinear curve as a single triangle from (0, 0) to (ε_max, σ_max).

items.stem: Refer to the terminal potential difference–current plot for a vanadium redox flow single cell over 0.0 A to 1.6 A. What value does the signed slope of the best-fit line take?
items.workedSolution: At I = 0.0 A, V = ε = 5.8 V; at I = 1.6 A, V = 2.6 V. Gradient = (2.6 − 5.8) / 1.6 = -2.00 V A⁻¹ (equal to −r).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates internal resistance r = |ΔV / ΔI| but omits the negative sign of the downward V–I gradient.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Inverts ΔI / ΔV instead of computing ΔV / ΔI.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Assumes the line meets V = 0 at I = I_max instead of reading the non-zero terminal voltage V(I_max).

items.stem: To find the resistivity ρ of a sintered silicon-carbide heating rod, total resistance R = ρ(L / A) + R₀ is plotted against L / A up to 100.0 m⁻¹. What value of ρ does the graph give?
items.workedSolution: Since R = ρ(L / A) + R₀, resistivity ρ equals the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A) = (24 − 4) / 100 = 0.200 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept R₀ = 4 Ω to obtain ρ = (24 − 4) / 100 = 0.200 Ω m (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Adds the zero-offset intercept R₀ to R_max instead of subtracting it when finding ΔR.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes the secant ratio R_max / (L/A)_max from the origin and fails to subtract the non-zero contact-resistance intercept R₀.

options.distractorRationale: Inverts Δ(L/A) / ΔR (electrical conductivity σ) instead of ΔR / Δ(L/A).

items.stem: Varying centre-to-centre separation up to r⁻² = 40.0 m⁻² for conductive carbon spheres mounted in a dry-nitrogen force cell yields the linear F versus r⁻² trace shown. Evaluate the slope ΔF / Δ(r⁻²).
items.workedSolution: At r⁻² = 0.0 m⁻², tare offset F₀ = 0.2 N; at r⁻² = 40 m⁻², F = 1.6 N. Gradient = (1.6 − 0.2) / 40 = 0.0350 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts tare offset F₀ = 0.2 N to get (1.6 − 0.2) / 40 = 0.0350 N m² (A).

items.stem: Examine the 20.0 s velocity–time curve for a canal lock towing locomotive (initial coordinate 40.0 m from the lock-gate reference mark). What mean speed is achieved during this movement?
items.workedSolution: Distance travelled Δx = ½(20 + 10)(18) = 270 m (independent of the 40 m starting offset). Mean speed = 270 / 20 = 13.5 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Divides trapezium distance (270 m) by 20 s to obtain 13.5 m s⁻¹ (C).

options.distractorRationale: Divides the final coordinate (x₀ + Δx) by total time rather than dividing the distance travelled Δx by total time.

options.distractorRationale: Confuses the cruise plateau velocity with the journey-wide mean speed.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Takes half of the peak velocity as if there were no constant-speed cruise plateau.

items.stem: A thruster acts from t = 4.0 s to t = 8.0 s on a magnetic rail cart of mass 4.0 kg, producing the momentum–time trace shown. What kinetic energy gain (net work) occurs over this interval?
items.workedSolution: Using E_k = p² / (2m), net work W = ΔE_k = (28² − 8²) / (2 × 4) = 90.0 J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies W = (p₂² − p₁²) / (2m) = (28² − 8²) / (8) = 90.0 J (B).

items.stem: Before a 4.0 s solenoid kicker stroke, a robotic soccer puck of mass 5.0 kg has momentum 15.0 kg m s⁻¹. Using the force–time plot, find its momentum immediately after the pulse.
items.workedSolution: Impulse Δp = ½(4 + 2)(35) = 105 N s. Final momentum p_f = p₀ + Δp = 15 + 105 = 120 kg m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Adds impulse (105 N s) to p₀ = 15 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 120 kg m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: Refer to the tensile stress–strain plot for an extruded fluoropolymer ribbon, whose limit of proportionality lies at strain 0.3. Calculate its initial Young's modulus.
items.workedSolution: Up to the limit of proportionality at ε = 0.3, stress reaches 210 MPa. Young's modulus E = σ / ε = 210 / 0.3 = 700 MPa.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates initial linear gradient E = 210 / 0.3 = 700 MPa (A).

items.stem: Two-wire resistance readings R across an isotropic graphite heating element include a fixed fixture offset R₀ when graphed against L / A from zero to 250.0 m⁻¹. Evaluate the resistivity ρ in Ω m.
items.workedSolution: Since R = ρ(L / A) + R₀, resistivity ρ equals the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A) = (41 − 7) / 250 = 0.136 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept R₀ = 7 Ω to obtain ρ = (41 − 7) / 250 = 0.136 Ω m (C).

items.stem: Taking g = 9.8 m s⁻², a levitated neodymium shuttle descending an inclined guide descends a smooth plane inclined at sin θ = 0.3, passing s = 0.0 m already in motion. From the v² against s plot up to 2.5 m, find the slope Δ(v²) / Δs.
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 3.5 m² s⁻² and at s = 2.5 m, v² = 18.2 m² s⁻². Gradient = (18.2 − 3.5) / 2.5 = 2(9.8)(0.3) = 5.88 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 3.5 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.8 × 0.3) to get 5.88 m s⁻² (A).

items.stem: Between t = 7.0 s and t = 10.0 s, a reverse thrust acts on an underwater ROV thruster sled along a taut calibration tether. Determine the acceleration indicated by the velocity–time plot.
items.workedSolution: Between t = 7 s and t = 10 s, velocity changes from +20 m s⁻¹ to −10 m s⁻¹. Acceleration a = Δv / Δt = (−10 − 20) / (10 − 7) = -10.0 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δv / Δt = (−10 − 20) / (3) = -10.0 m s⁻² (A).

items.stem: Use the signed 12.0 s acceleration–time graph to find the terminal upward velocity of a deep-sea winch capsule, which starts at 18.0 m s⁻¹ when t = 0.0 s.
items.workedSolution: Positive a–t area (0 to 6 s) = 36.0 m s⁻¹; negative area magnitude (6 s to 12 s) = 18.0 m s⁻¹. Net Δv = 36.0 − 18.0 = 18.0 m s⁻¹. Final velocity = 18 + (18.0) = 36.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Combines net signed area (18.0 m s⁻¹) with u₀ = 18 m s⁻¹ to obtain 36.0 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: Calculate the mean resultant force exerted during the 0.5 s spring buffer contact on a rail-mounted docking target (mass 0.8 kg, initial momentum 2.4 kg m s⁻¹) from the plotted F–t curve.
items.workedSolution: Total impulse J = ½(0.5 + 0.3)(42) = 16.8 N s. Mean force F_mean = J / Δt = 16.8 / 0.5 = 33.6 N.

markScheme.criterion: Divides impulse (16.8 N s) by 0.5 s to obtain 33.6 N (A).

items.stem: Evaluate the net work done by the resultant force on a cable-towed hydroplane model (mass 3.0 kg, initial speed 6.0 m s⁻¹) between x = 0.0 m and x = 15.0 m using the graph.
items.workedSolution: Forward work (0 to 12 m) = 162 J; resistive work (12 m to 15 m) = −9.00 J. Net work = 162 − 9.00 = 153 J.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts resistive triangle (9.00 J) from positive trapezium (162 J) to get 153 J (C).

items.stem: Determine the strain energy stored per unit volume (in MJ m⁻³) when a synthetic polyurethane tendon cord is loaded from zero strain to 0.4 along the plotted stress–strain curve (proportional limit at 0.2).
items.workedSolution: Work per unit volume equals area under the σ–ε graph (1 MPa × 1 = 1 MJ m⁻³): u = ½(0.2)(120) + ½(120 + 180)(0.2) = 42.0 MJ m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Sums triangle and trapezium areas under σ–ε curve to obtain 42.0 MJ m⁻³ (C).

items.stem: Over load currents uniformly spanning 0.0 A to 0.8 A, an alkaline lantern battery exhibits the linear V–I plot shown. Calculate the average terminal potential difference across the plotted interval.
items.workedSolution: Terminal p.d. varies linearly from 4.2 V at I = 0.0 A to 2.2 V at I = 0.8 A, so V_mean = ½(4.2 + 2.2) = 3.20 V.

markScheme.criterion: Averages endpoint voltages ½(4.2 + 2.2) = 3.20 V (D).

items.stem: Speed-squared readings v² are graphed against displacement s (0.0 m to 2.0 m) for a steel ball bearing rolling in a V-channel with negligible rotational loss on a frictionless ramp of sin θ = 0.2 where g = 9.81 m s⁻². Calculate the gradient of the line.
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 2.2 m² s⁻² and at s = 2 m, v² = 10.048 m² s⁻². Gradient = (10.048 − 2.2) / 2 = 2(9.81)(0.2) = 3.92 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 2.2 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.81 × 0.2) to get 3.92 m s⁻² (D).

items.stem: Subtracting the constant zero-offset intercept on the F versus r⁻² plot (0.0 m⁻² to 50.0 m⁻²) for precision electrostatic spheres on a sapphire-pivot balance, find the gradient in N m².
items.workedSolution: At r⁻² = 0.0 m⁻², tare offset F₀ = 0.3 N; at r⁻² = 50 m⁻², F = 1.9 N. Gradient = (1.9 − 0.3) / 50 = 0.0320 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts tare offset F₀ = 0.3 N to get (1.9 − 0.3) / 50 = 0.0320 N m² (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the slope to Δ(r⁻²) / ΔF instead of ΔF / Δ(r⁻²).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes the secant F_max / (r⁻²)_max from (0, 0) without subtracting the non-zero balance tare offset F₀.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies ΔF by (r⁻²)_max instead of dividing ΔF by Δ(r⁻²).

items.stem: During a dynamic acceptance trial, a cleanroom wafer transport shuttle moves along a linear air bearing, taking to the right as positive. Using the velocity–time graph recorded from t = 0.0 s to t = 12.0 s, determine the total distance travelled.
items.workedSolution: Velocity crosses zero at t = 8 s. Forward area (0 to 8 s) = ½(2)(24) + (3)(24) + ½(3)(24) = 132 m. Reverse area magnitude (8 s to 12 s) = ½(1)(8) + (3)(8) = 28.0 m. Total distance = 132 + 28.0 = 160 m.

markScheme.criterion: Sums unsigned positive (132 m) and negative (28.0 m) velocity–time areas to obtain 160 m (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies peak forward velocity by the entire duration without accounting for ramps or direction reversal.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts the area below the time axis from the positive area, giving net signed displacement rather than total distance.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Integrates only up to the zero-velocity instant and omits the distance travelled after reversing direction.

items.stem: At t = 0.0 s, a shipyard gantry crane crab is stationary at a position 28.0 m ahead of a western end-stop. It then moves forward along a straight guideway according to the velocity–time graph for 16.0 s. What is its final distance from the western end-stop at t = 16.0 s?
items.workedSolution: Displacement during the 16 s run equals the trapezium area: Δx = ½(16 + 8)(20) = 240 m. Final position from the western end-stop = x₀ + Δx = 28 + 240 = 268 m.

markScheme.criterion: Adds trapezium area (240 m) to initial offset (28 m) to get 268 m (B).

items.stem: From the 16.0 s acceleration–time trace for an aerotow winch launch carriage (initial forward speed 13.0 m s⁻¹), calculate the maximum speed reached before braking reduces its velocity.
items.workedSolution: Speed increases while a > 0 (from t = 0.0 s until a = 0 at t = 10 s). Positive area Δv_max = (4)(5) + ½(6)(5) = 35.0 m s⁻¹. Maximum speed = u₀ + Δv_max = 13 + 35.0 = 48.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Integrates positive acceleration up to t = 10 s (35.0 m s⁻¹) and adds 13 m s⁻¹ to get 48.0 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: In a linear dynamics experiment, a superconducting levitation carrier of mass 5.0 kg moves in a straight line with momentum varying as shown. How much net work is done on it between t = 2.0 s and t = 7.0 s?
items.workedSolution: Using E_k = p² / (2m), net work W = ΔE_k = (30² − 10²) / (2 × 5) = 80.0 J.

items.stem: Passing x = 0.0 m with speed 7.0 m s⁻¹, a linear dynamo test sled of mass 2.0 kg experiences the collinear resultant force plotted against displacement up to x = 16.0 m. What is its speed at x = 16.0 m?
items.workedSolution: Positive work (0 to 12 m) = ½(12 + 6)(10) = 90.0 J. Resistive work (12 m to 16 m) = −½(4)(2) = −4.00 J. Net work W = 86.0 J. From ½mv² = ½mu₀² + W, v = √(7² + 2 × 86.0 / 2) = 11.6 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Finds net work W = 86.0 J and v = √(7² + 2W/2) = 11.6 m s⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: In a tensile materials test, a braided aramid-polymer composite tape obeys Hooke's law up to a strain of 0.25 before softening up to strain 0.5, as shown on the stress–strain graph. What is the Young's modulus of the material in the initial linear region?
items.workedSolution: Up to the limit of proportionality at ε = 0.25, stress reaches 230 MPa. Young's modulus E = σ / ε = 230 / 0.25 = 920 MPa.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates initial linear gradient E = 230 / 0.25 = 920 MPa (A).

items.stem: In a materials conductivity test on a sintered silicon-carbide heating rod, measured resistance R varies linearly with L / A up to 80.0 m⁻¹ as shown. Extract the bulk resistivity ρ.
items.workedSolution: Since R = ρ(L / A) + R₀, resistivity ρ equals the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A) = (25 − 5) / 80 = 0.250 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept R₀ = 5 Ω to obtain ρ = (25 − 5) / 80 = 0.250 Ω m (A).

items.stem: How steep (in m s⁻²) is the linear v² versus s graph recorded over 4.0 m for an optical-interruptor sled coasting down an inclined bench on a smooth slope (sin θ = 0.15, g = 9.8 m s⁻²)?
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 2.6 m² s⁻² and at s = 4 m, v² = 14.36 m² s⁻². Gradient = (14.36 − 2.6) / 4 = 2(9.8)(0.15) = 2.94 m s⁻².

items.stem: Beginning 45.0 m past a shaft loading datum, an underground mine haulage skip follows the velocity–time profile shown over 20.0 s. What is its mean speed during the 20.0 s journey?
items.workedSolution: Distance travelled Δx = ½(20 + 8)(24) = 336 m (independent of the 45 m starting offset). Mean speed = 336 / 20 = 16.8 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Divides trapezium distance (336 m) by 20 s to obtain 16.8 m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: The graph displays the linear momentum of a low-friction dynamics trolley (mass 3.2 kg) against time. What resultant force acts on it between t = 3.0 s and t = 8.0 s?
items.workedSolution: By Newton's second law, F = Δp / Δt = (22.4 − 6.4) / (8 − 3) = 3.20 N.

items.stem: Moving in a straight line with initial momentum 3.6 kg m s⁻¹, a ballistic pendulum carriage (mass 1.2 kg) undergoes the 1.0 s controlled gas-jet pulse shown. What is its final momentum at t = 1.0 s?
items.workedSolution: Impulse Δp = ½(1 + 0.4)(40) = 28.0 N s. Final momentum p_f = p₀ + Δp = 3.6 + 28.0 = 31.6 kg m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Adds impulse (28.0 N s) to p₀ = 3.6 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 31.6 kg m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: By varying a rheostat connected to a nickel-metal-hydride battery pack, terminal voltage V is graphed against current I up to 4.0 A. Find the signed slope ΔV / ΔI.
items.workedSolution: At I = 0.0 A, V = ε = 15 V; at I = 4 A, V = 5 V. Gradient = (5 − 15) / 4 = -2.50 V A⁻¹ (equal to −r).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates (5 − 15) / 4 = -2.50 V A⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: Examine the straight-line plot of v² against track distance s up to 1.2 m for a wheeled telemetry trolley accelerating along a tilted track (ramp sin θ = 0.45, g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Evaluate its gradient.
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 3.8 m² s⁻² and at s = 1.2 m, v² = 14.3948 m² s⁻². Gradient = (14.3948 − 3.8) / 1.2 = 2(9.81)(0.45) = 8.83 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 3.8 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.81 × 0.45) to get 8.83 m s⁻² (A).

items.stem: How large is the slope ΔF / Δ(r⁻²) of the inverse-square linearization graph recorded up to 60.0 m⁻² using charged metallized spheres in a Coulomb torsion-balance rig?
items.workedSolution: At r⁻² = 0.0 m⁻², tare offset F₀ = 0.3 N; at r⁻² = 60 m⁻², F = 1.9 N. Gradient = (1.9 − 0.3) / 60 = 0.0267 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts tare offset F₀ = 0.3 N to get (1.9 − 0.3) / 60 = 0.0267 N m² (C).

items.stem: While operating inside a vertical guide shaft (upward positive), a drop-tower counterbalance carriage brakes and reverses direction between t = 6.0 s and t = 10.0 s. From the velocity–time graph, what is its acceleration during this interval?
items.workedSolution: Between t = 6 s and t = 10 s, velocity changes from +18 m s⁻¹ to −6 m s⁻¹. Acceleration a = Δv / Δt = (−6 − 18) / (10 − 6) = -6.00 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δv / Δt = (−6 − 18) / (4) = -6.00 m s⁻² (B).

items.stem: Starting at x = 32.0 m from a optical home flag, a high-speed bottling-line transfer sled completes the 10.0 s journey shown on the velocity–time graph, braking uniformly from t = 8.0 s to t = 10.0 s. What is its acceleration during braking?
items.workedSolution: During braking from t = 8 s to t = 10 s, a = (0 − 19) / (10 − 8) = -9.50 m s⁻².

items.stem: Over an interval of 6.0 s, a deep-sea winch capsule (initial velocity 9.0 m s⁻¹ upward) follows the plotted acceleration profile. What velocity does it have when t = 6.0 s?
items.workedSolution: Positive a–t area (0 to 3 s) = 24.0 m s⁻¹; negative area magnitude (3 s to 6 s) = 15.0 m s⁻¹. Net Δv = 24.0 − 15.0 = 9.00 m s⁻¹. Final velocity = 9 + (9.00) = 18.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Combines net signed area (9.00 m s⁻¹) with u₀ = 9 m s⁻¹ to obtain 18.0 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: During a 5.0 s stator current pulse, a linear-motor launch shuttle (mass 6.0 kg, initial momentum 18.0 kg m s⁻¹) experiences the force–time profile shown. What is the time-averaged resultant force over the 5.0 s interval?
items.workedSolution: Total impulse J = ½(5 + 3)(40) = 160 N s. Mean force F_mean = J / Δt = 160 / 5 = 32.0 N.

markScheme.criterion: Divides impulse (160 N s) by 5 s to obtain 32.0 N (B).

items.stem: A 3.2 kg unit (a wind-propelled land-yacht rig) enters an instrumented zone at 4.0 m s⁻¹. From the resultant force–displacement graph over 14.0 m, calculate its exit speed at x = 14.0 m.
items.workedSolution: Positive work (0 to 11 m) = ½(11 + 6)(16) = 136 J. Resistive work (11 m to 14 m) = −½(3)(4) = −6.00 J. Net work W = 130 J. From ½mv² = ½mu₀² + W, v = √(4² + 2 × 130 / 3.2) = 9.86 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Finds net work W = 130 J and v = √(4² + 2W/3.2) = 9.86 m s⁻¹ (D).

options.distractorRationale: Adds the resistive negative-force area to work done instead of subtracting it.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Adds √(2W/m) linearly to u₀ rather than adding kinetic energies before taking the square root.

items.stem: The tensile stress–strain curve for a synthetic polyurethane tendon cord is linear from 0.0 to strain 0.5 and reaches strain 1.0. Determine the Young's modulus in MPa.
items.workedSolution: Up to the limit of proportionality at ε = 0.5, stress reaches 280 MPa. Young's modulus E = σ / ε = 280 / 0.5 = 560 MPa.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates initial linear gradient E = 280 / 0.5 = 560 MPa (C).

items.stem: Evaluate the average terminal potential difference delivered by an alkaline lantern battery across the plotted current domain 0.0 A to 1.0 A.
items.workedSolution: Terminal p.d. varies linearly from 5.5 V at I = 0.0 A to 2.5 V at I = 1 A, so V_mean = ½(5.5 + 2.5) = 4.00 V.

markScheme.criterion: Averages endpoint voltages ½(5.5 + 2.5) = 4.00 V (D).

items.stem: Inspect the linear plot of measured resistance R versus L / A (spanning 0.0 m⁻¹ to 50.0 m⁻¹) for a conductive silicone sensor strip. What is the material's resistivity ρ?
items.workedSolution: Since R = ρ(L / A) + R₀, resistivity ρ equals the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A) = (20 − 4) / 50 = 0.320 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept R₀ = 4 Ω to obtain ρ = (20 − 4) / 50 = 0.320 Ω m (C).

items.stem: Examine the straight-line graph of balance force F against r⁻² (spanning 0.0 m⁻² to 16.0 m⁻²) for precision electrostatic spheres on a sapphire-pivot balance. What value does its gradient take?
items.workedSolution: At r⁻² = 0.0 m⁻², tare offset F₀ = 0.12 N; at r⁻² = 16 m⁻², F = 1.16 N. Gradient = (1.16 − 0.12) / 16 = 0.0650 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts tare offset F₀ = 0.12 N to get (1.16 − 0.12) / 16 = 0.0650 N m² (D).

items.stem: Starting 38.0 m beyond the nozzle datum line at t = 0.0 s, a wind-tunnel moving-ground carriage executes the 16.0 s velocity–time profile shown. How far from the nozzle datum line does it come to rest?
items.workedSolution: Displacement during the 16 s run equals the trapezium area: Δx = ½(16 + 7)(16) = 184 m. Final position from the nozzle datum line = x₀ + Δx = 38 + 184 = 222 m.

markScheme.criterion: Adds trapezium area (184 m) to initial offset (38 m) to get 222 m (C).

items.stem: Motion sensors track the momentum of a linear air-bearing carriage of mass 6.0 kg. Determine the magnitude of the resultant force acting from t = 4.0 s to t = 10.0 s.
items.workedSolution: By Newton's second law, F = Δp / Δt = (36 − 12) / (10 − 4) = 4.00 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F = Δp / Δt = (36 − 12) / (6) = 4.00 N (C).

items.stem: A docking vernier firing acts for 2.0 s in the direction of motion of a microgravity cargo pod (mass 2.0 kg, initial momentum 8.0 kg m s⁻¹). Using the plotted force–time profile, determine Δv.
items.workedSolution: Impulse J = area under F–t trapezium = ½(2 + 1)(35) = 52.5 N s. Speed increase Δv = J / m = 52.5 / 2 = 26.3 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Computes J = 52.5 N s and Δv = J / 2 = 26.3 m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: Determine the strain energy stored per unit volume (in MJ m⁻³) when a braided aramid-polymer composite tape is loaded from zero strain to 0.6 along the plotted stress–strain curve (proportional limit at 0.3).
items.workedSolution: Work per unit volume equals area under the σ–ε graph (1 MPa × 1 = 1 MJ m⁻³): u = ½(0.3)(180) + ½(180 + 250)(0.3) = 91.5 MJ m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Sums triangle and trapezium areas under σ–ε curve to obtain 91.5 MJ m⁻³ (D).

items.stem: Eliminating the constant probe-lead offset from the R versus L / A graph (plotted to 400.0 m⁻¹), find the resistivity ρ of a sintered silicon-carbide heating rod.
items.workedSolution: Since R = ρ(L / A) + R₀, resistivity ρ equals the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A) = (30 − 6) / 400 = 0.0600 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept R₀ = 6 Ω to obtain ρ = (30 − 6) / 400 = 0.0600 Ω m (A).

items.stem: An optical timer measures speed v of an optical-interruptor sled coasting down an inclined bench at positions up to s = 2.0 m along a frictionless incline (sin θ = 0.25, g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What is the slope of the resulting v²–s graph?
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 3 m² s⁻² and at s = 2 m, v² = 12.81 m² s⁻². Gradient = (12.81 − 3) / 2 = 2(9.81)(0.25) = 4.91 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 3 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.81 × 0.25) to get 4.91 m s⁻² (A).

items.stem: A motion sensor tracks an automated rail inspection trolley along a straight viaduct rail for 10.0 s, taking eastward velocity as positive. Find the net signed displacement at t = 10.0 s relative to its starting point.
items.workedSolution: Velocity reaches zero at t = 7 s. Positive area = 80.0 m and area below the axis has magnitude 20.0 m. Net displacement = 80.0 − 20.0 = 60.0 m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts reverse area (20.0 m) from forward area (80.0 m) to obtain 60.0 m (C).

items.stem: A data logger captures 10.0 s of signed upward acceleration for a vertical-launch sounding sled, which passes t = 0.0 s at 10.0 m s⁻¹. Evaluate the peak speed achieved.
items.workedSolution: Speed increases while a > 0 (from t = 0.0 s until a = 0 at t = 6 s). Positive area Δv_max = (3)(4) + ½(3)(4) = 18.0 m s⁻¹. Maximum speed = u₀ + Δv_max = 10 + 18.0 = 28.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Integrates positive acceleration up to t = 6 s (18.0 m s⁻¹) and adds 10 m s⁻¹ to get 28.0 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: Before a 0.8 s cold-gas thruster burn, a cold-gas attitude probe of mass 2.0 kg has momentum 6.0 kg m s⁻¹. Using the force–time plot, find its momentum immediately after the pulse.
items.workedSolution: Impulse Δp = ½(0.8 + 0.4)(50) = 30.0 N s. Final momentum p_f = p₀ + Δp = 6 + 30.0 = 36.0 kg m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Adds impulse (30.0 N s) to p₀ = 6 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 36.0 kg m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: The resultant force in the direction of motion of an instrumented crash-test carriage (mass 2.0 kg, initial speed 5.0 m s⁻¹) is plotted over 10.0 m. Determine its speed at x = 10.0 m.
items.workedSolution: Positive work (0 to 8 m) = ½(8 + 4)(12) = 72.0 J. Resistive work (8 m to 10 m) = −½(2)(4) = −4.00 J. Net work W = 68.0 J. From ½mv² = ½mu₀² + W, v = √(5² + 2 × 68.0 / 2) = 9.64 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Finds net work W = 68.0 J and v = √(5² + 2W/2) = 9.64 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: Refer to the tensile stress–strain plot for a thermoplastic elastomer tether, whose limit of proportionality lies at strain 0.2. Calculate its initial Young's modulus.
items.workedSolution: Up to the limit of proportionality at ε = 0.2, stress reaches 150 MPa. Young's modulus E = σ / ε = 150 / 0.2 = 750 MPa.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates initial linear gradient E = 150 / 0.2 = 750 MPa (C).

items.stem: A variable load resistor is connected across a nickel-metal-hydride battery pack, and the terminal potential difference V is plotted against current I up to 2.0 A. According to V = ε − Ir, what is the signed gradient of this graph?
items.workedSolution: At I = 0.0 A, V = ε = 7 V; at I = 2 A, V = 3.4 V. Gradient = (3.4 − 7) / 2 = -1.80 V A⁻¹ (equal to −r).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates (3.4 − 7) / 2 = -1.80 V A⁻¹ (A).

items.stem: Using two light gates in a gravitational field g = 9.8 m s⁻², a student records speed v of a wheeled telemetry trolley accelerating along a tilted track (inclination sin θ = 0.3) after passing an initial gate at s = 0.0 m with speed u₀ > 0, plotting v² against distance s up to 2.0 m. According to v² = u₀² + 2as, what is the gradient Δ(v²) / Δs of the line?
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 2.5 m² s⁻² and at s = 2 m, v² = 14.26 m² s⁻². Gradient = (14.26 − 2.5) / 2 = 2(9.8)(0.3) = 5.88 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 2.5 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.8 × 0.3) to get 5.88 m s⁻² (B).

items.stem: To test Coulomb's inverse-square law using charged metallized spheres in a Coulomb torsion-balance rig with an unzeroed tare offset F₀, the force reading F is plotted against inverse-square separation (r⁻²) up to 100.0 m⁻², following F = k|Q₁Q₂|r⁻² + F₀. What is the gradient k|Q₁Q₂| of the line?
items.workedSolution: At r⁻² = 0.0 m⁻², tare offset F₀ = 0.2 N; at r⁻² = 100 m⁻², F = 1.8 N. Gradient = (1.8 − 0.2) / 100 = 0.0160 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts tare offset F₀ = 0.2 N to get (1.8 − 0.2) / 100 = 0.0160 N m² (B).

items.stem: Inspect the constant-gradient reversal stage from t = 6.0 s to t = 9.0 s for a magnetic-levitation shuttle pod moving on a horizontal vacuum test guideway. What signed acceleration acts over this stage?
items.workedSolution: Between t = 6 s and t = 9 s, velocity changes from +16 m s⁻¹ to −8 m s⁻¹. Acceleration a = Δv / Δt = (−8 − 16) / (9 − 6) = -8.00 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δv / Δt = (−8 − 16) / (3) = -8.00 m s⁻² (D).

items.stem: In the velocity–time record for a linear-induction baggage carrier (initially 30.0 m from the sorting-hall origin sensor), uniform braking begins at t = 8.0 s and ends at rest at t = 12.0 s. Find the signed braking acceleration.
items.workedSolution: During braking from t = 8 s to t = 12 s, a = (0 − 14) / (12 − 8) = -3.50 m s⁻².

items.stem: Calculate the upward velocity at t = 10.0 s for a deep-sea winch capsule, given u = 8.0 m s⁻¹ at t = 0.0 s and the acceleration–time trace shown.
items.workedSolution: Positive a–t area (0 to 5 s) = 28.0 m s⁻¹; negative area magnitude (5 s to 10 s) = 16.0 m s⁻¹. Net Δv = 28.0 − 16.0 = 12.0 m s⁻¹. Final velocity = 8 + (12.0) = 20.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Combines net signed area (12.0 m s⁻¹) with u₀ = 8 m s⁻¹ to obtain 20.0 m s⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: The graph displays the linear momentum of a frictionless puck on an air table (mass 1.6 kg) against time. What resultant force acts on it between t = 2.0 s and t = 5.0 s?
items.workedSolution: By Newton's second law, F = Δp / Δt = (12.8 − 3.2) / (5 − 2) = 3.20 N.

options.label: B

items.stem: Moving forward from x = 0.0 m with initial speed 4.0 m s⁻¹, a pneumatic factory transfer cart (mass 4.0 kg) is subjected to the resultant force–displacement profile shown up to x = 12.0 m. How much net work is done on it over the 12.0 m displacement?
items.workedSolution: Forward work (0 to 10 m) = 120 J; resistive work (10 m to 12 m) = −4.00 J. Net work = 120 − 4.00 = 116 J.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts resistive triangle (4.00 J) from positive trapezium (120 J) to get 116 J (A).
