options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Adds the area below the displacement axis instead of subtracting negative resistive work.

items.stem: The stress–strain graph shows a drawn nylon monofilament stretched reversibly through two piecewise-linear stages up to strain 0.5 (kink at strain 0.2). What work is done per unit volume in stretching the specimen to strain 0.5?
items.workedSolution: Work per unit volume equals area under the σ–ε graph (1 MPa × 1 = 1 MJ m⁻³): u = ½(0.2)(190) + ½(190 + 290)(0.3) = 91.0 MJ m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Sums triangle and trapezium areas under σ–ε curve to obtain 91.0 MJ m⁻³ (D).

items.stem: Using crocodile clips with constant contact resistance R₀, a student measures total resistance R of a conductive silicone sensor strip for different length-to-area ratios (L / A) up to 200.0 m⁻¹, so R = ρ(L / A) + R₀. From the plotted line, what is the resistivity ρ of the material?
items.workedSolution: Since R = ρ(L / A) + R₀, resistivity ρ equals the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A) = (25 − 5) / 200 = 0.100 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept R₀ = 5 Ω to obtain ρ = (25 − 5) / 200 = 0.100 Ω m (A).

items.stem: In a kinematics linearization lab (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²), a low-friction dynamics cart descending a tilted aluminium runway on a frictionless slope with sin θ = 0.4 passes s = 0.0 m at speed u₀ and continues to s = 1.6 m. Determine the gradient of the plotted v² versus s graph.
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 3.4 m² s⁻² and at s = 1.6 m, v² = 15.9568 m² s⁻². Gradient = (15.9568 − 3.4) / 1.6 = 2(9.81)(0.4) = 7.85 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 3.4 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.81 × 0.4) to get 7.85 m s⁻² (A).

items.stem: Sensors record a canal lock towing locomotive initially at x = 35.0 m relative to a lock-gate reference mark. Using the velocity–time plot up to t = 16.0 s, determine its final coordinate x.
items.workedSolution: Displacement during the 16 s run equals the trapezium area: Δx = ½(16 + 6)(19) = 209 m. Final position from the lock-gate reference mark = x₀ + Δx = 35 + 209 = 244 m.

markScheme.criterion: Adds trapezium area (209 m) to initial offset (35 m) to get 244 m (B).

items.stem: In a linear dynamics experiment, a magnetic rail cart of mass 2.4 kg moves in a straight line with momentum varying as shown. How much net work is done on it between t = 3.0 s and t = 7.0 s?
items.workedSolution: Using E_k = p² / (2m), net work W = ΔE_k = (16.8² − 4.8²) / (2 × 2.4) = 54.0 J.

items.stem: Refer to the force–time profile of a solenoid kicker stroke on a robotic soccer puck of mass 4.0 kg (initial momentum 12.0 kg m s⁻¹). By how much does its speed increase over the 2.0 s pulse?
items.workedSolution: Impulse J = area under F–t trapezium = ½(2 + 1)(42) = 63.0 N s. Speed increase Δv = J / m = 63.0 / 4 = 15.8 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Computes J = 63.0 N s and Δv = J / 4 = 15.8 m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: In an internal-resistance experiment on a silver-oxide instrument battery, a student plots terminal potential difference V versus current I from 0.0 A to 2.5 A. Determine the gradient ΔV / ΔI of the line.
items.workedSolution: At I = 0.0 A, V = ε = 10 V; at I = 2.5 A, V = 4 V. Gradient = (4 − 10) / 2.5 = -2.40 V A⁻¹ (equal to −r).

options.distractorRationale: Inverts ΔI / ΔV instead of computing ΔV / ΔI.

items.stem: Photogate data for an air-bearing carriage coasting down a Precision granite incline accelerating down an incline (sin θ = 0.2, g = 9.8 m s⁻²) from s = 0.0 m to s = 2.5 m are linearized by plotting v² against s. What gradient does the best-fit line have?
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 2.8 m² s⁻² and at s = 2.5 m, v² = 12.6 m² s⁻². Gradient = (12.6 − 2.8) / 2.5 = 2(9.8)(0.2) = 3.92 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 2.8 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.8 × 0.2) to get 3.92 m s⁻² (C).

items.stem: Readings F from charged copper electrodes on a laser-deflection cantilever are linearized against r⁻² from 0.0 m⁻² to 80.0 m⁻². Accounting for the systematic zero-offset F₀, determine the gradient ΔF / Δ(r⁻²).
items.workedSolution: At r⁻² = 0.0 m⁻², tare offset F₀ = 0.2 N; at r⁻² = 80 m⁻², F = 2.2 N. Gradient = (2.2 − 0.2) / 80 = 0.0250 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts tare offset F₀ = 0.2 N to get (2.2 − 0.2) / 80 = 0.0250 N m² (C).

items.stem: Refer to the signed velocity–time graph for a cable-hauled alpine service car travelling on a straight haulage section. Determine the resultant displacement after 10.0 s.
items.workedSolution: Velocity reaches zero at t = 7 s. Positive area = 54.0 m and area below the axis has magnitude 10.0 m. Net displacement = 54.0 − 10.0 = 44.0 m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts reverse area (10.0 m) from forward area (54.0 m) to obtain 44.0 m (B).

items.stem: Examine the 8.0 s velocity–time curve for a solar-powered desert research rover (initial coordinate 22.0 m from the base-camp beacon). What mean speed is achieved during this movement?
items.workedSolution: Distance travelled Δx = ½(8 + 4)(12) = 72.0 m (independent of the 22 m starting offset). Mean speed = 72.0 / 8 = 9.00 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Divides trapezium distance (72.0 m) by 8 s to obtain 9.00 m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: Given that a vertical-launch sounding sled has velocity 11.0 m s⁻¹ upward when t = 0.0 s, use the 10.0 s acceleration–time plot to find its maximum speed.
items.workedSolution: Speed increases while a > 0 (from t = 0.0 s until a = 0 at t = 4 s). Positive area Δv_max = (2)(10) + ½(2)(10) = 30.0 m s⁻¹. Maximum speed = u₀ + Δv_max = 11 + 30.0 = 41.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Integrates positive acceleration up to t = 4 s (30.0 m s⁻¹) and adds 11 m s⁻¹ to get 41.0 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: Moving in a straight line with initial momentum 4.5 kg m s⁻¹, a rail-mounted docking target (mass 1.5 kg) undergoes the 1.6 s spring buffer contact shown. What is its final momentum at t = 1.6 s?
items.workedSolution: Impulse Δp = ½(1.6 + 0.8)(40) = 48.0 N s. Final momentum p_f = p₀ + Δp = 4.5 + 48.0 = 52.5 kg m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Adds impulse (48.0 N s) to p₀ = 4.5 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 52.5 kg m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: Evaluate the net work done by the resultant force on a cable-towed hydroplane model (mass 5.0 kg, initial speed 5.0 m s⁻¹) between x = 0.0 m and x = 16.0 m using the graph.
items.workedSolution: Forward work (0 to 14 m) = 200 J; resistive work (14 m to 16 m) = −5.00 J. Net work = 200 − 5.00 = 195 J.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts resistive triangle (5.00 J) from positive trapezium (200 J) to get 195 J (D).

items.stem: Determine the strain energy stored per unit volume (in MJ m⁻³) when a thermoplastic elastomer tether is loaded from zero strain to 0.8 along the plotted stress–strain curve (proportional limit at 0.4).
items.workedSolution: Work per unit volume equals area under the σ–ε graph (1 MPa × 1 = 1 MJ m⁻³): u = ½(0.4)(230) + ½(230 + 320)(0.4) = 156 MJ m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Sums triangle and trapezium areas under σ–ε curve to obtain 156 MJ m⁻³ (B).

items.stem: Refer to the terminal potential difference–current plot for a nickel-metal-hydride battery pack over 0.0 A to 1.6 A. What value does the signed slope of the best-fit line take?
items.workedSolution: At I = 0.0 A, V = ε = 5.8 V; at I = 1.6 A, V = 2.6 V. Gradient = (2.6 − 5.8) / 1.6 = -2.00 V A⁻¹ (equal to −r).

items.stem: Total circuit resistance R (including lead resistance R₀) is plotted against geometric ratio L / A up to 400.0 m⁻¹ for a conductive carbon-polymer rod. Calculate the electrical resistivity ρ.
items.workedSolution: Since R = ρ(L / A) + R₀, resistivity ρ equals the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A) = (46 − 10) / 400 = 0.0900 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept R₀ = 10 Ω to obtain ρ = (46 − 10) / 400 = 0.0900 Ω m (D).

options.distractorRationale: Adds the zero-offset intercept R₀ to R_max instead of subtracting it when finding ΔR.

items.stem: The linearized Coulomb plot shows balance force F versus inverse-square separation r⁻² up to 50.0 m⁻² for charged metallized spheres in a Coulomb torsion-balance rig. Calculate the gradient of the line in N m².
items.workedSolution: At r⁻² = 0.0 m⁻², tare offset F₀ = 0.25 N; at r⁻² = 50 m⁻², F = 1.65 N. Gradient = (1.65 − 0.25) / 50 = 0.0280 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts tare offset F₀ = 0.25 N to get (1.65 − 0.25) / 50 = 0.0280 N m² (D).

items.stem: Starting at x = 40.0 m from a western end-stop, a shipyard gantry crane crab completes the 20.0 s journey shown on the velocity–time graph, braking uniformly from t = 15.0 s to t = 20.0 s. What is its acceleration during braking?
items.workedSolution: During braking from t = 15 s to t = 20 s, a = (0 − 18) / (20 − 15) = -3.60 m s⁻².

items.stem: The momentum–time graph is recorded for a superconducting levitation carrier (mass 4.0 kg) travelling along a straight guide. Calculate the net work done on the object from t = 4.0 s to t = 8.0 s.
items.workedSolution: Using E_k = p² / (2m), net work W = ΔE_k = (28² − 8²) / (2 × 4) = 90.0 J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies W = (p₂² − p₁²) / (2m) = (28² − 8²) / (8) = 90.0 J (D).

items.stem: During a 4.0 s pulsed ion-beam firing, a Hall-effect thruster test rig (mass 5.0 kg, initial momentum 15.0 kg m s⁻¹) experiences the force–time profile shown. What is the time-averaged resultant force over the 4.0 s interval?
items.workedSolution: Total impulse J = ½(4 + 2)(35) = 105 N s. Mean force F_mean = J / Δt = 105 / 4 = 26.3 N.

markScheme.criterion: Divides impulse (105 N s) by 4 s to obtain 26.3 N (C).

items.stem: The tensile stress–strain curve for a drawn nylon monofilament is linear from 0.0 to strain 0.3 and reaches strain 0.6. Determine the Young's modulus in MPa.
items.workedSolution: Up to the limit of proportionality at ε = 0.3, stress reaches 210 MPa. Young's modulus E = σ / ε = 210 / 0.3 = 700 MPa.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates initial linear gradient E = 210 / 0.3 = 700 MPa (D).

items.stem: The linearized graph shows measured resistance R versus L / A for a conductive silicone sensor strip over 0.0 m⁻¹ to 500.0 m⁻¹. Accounting for the non-zero contact-resistance intercept, determine ρ.
items.workedSolution: Since R = ρ(L / A) + R₀, resistivity ρ equals the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A) = (51 − 12) / 500 = 0.0780 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept R₀ = 12 Ω to obtain ρ = (51 − 12) / 500 = 0.0780 Ω m (B).

items.stem: Taking g = 9.8 m s⁻², a low-friction dynamics cart descending a tilted aluminium runway descends a smooth plane inclined at sin θ = 0.6, passing s = 0.0 m already in motion. From the v² against s plot up to 1.0 m, find the slope Δ(v²) / Δs.
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 3.2 m² s⁻² and at s = 1 m, v² = 14.96 m² s⁻². Gradient = (14.96 − 3.2) / 1 = 2(9.8)(0.6) = 11.8 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 3.2 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.8 × 0.6) to get 11.8 m s⁻² (A).

items.stem: Engineers log the signed velocity of an underwater ROV thruster sled along a taut calibration tether over 15.0 s. How much total distance does it cover before the recording ends at t = 15.0 s?
items.workedSolution: Velocity crosses zero at t = 9 s. Forward area (0 to 9 s) = ½(3)(20) + (4)(20) + ½(2)(20) = 130 m. Reverse area magnitude (9 s to 15 s) = ½(1)(10) + (5)(10) = 55.0 m. Total distance = 130 + 55.0 = 185 m.

markScheme.criterion: Sums unsigned positive (130 m) and negative (55.0 m) velocity–time areas to obtain 185 m (A).

items.stem: Sensors aboard a drop-shaft recovery gondola record the 12.0 s acceleration history shown from an initial upward speed of 16.0 m s⁻¹. Find its velocity at the end of the 12.0 s window.
items.workedSolution: Positive a–t area (0 to 8 s) = 24.0 m s⁻¹; negative area magnitude (8 s to 12 s) = 15.0 m s⁻¹. Net Δv = 24.0 − 15.0 = 9.00 m s⁻¹. Final velocity = 16 + (9.00) = 25.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Combines net signed area (9.00 m s⁻¹) with u₀ = 16 m s⁻¹ to obtain 25.0 m s⁻¹ (A).

items.stem: Having initial forward momentum 2.4 kg m s⁻¹, a ballistic pendulum carriage of mass 0.8 kg experiences a collinear controlled gas-jet pulse over 0.5 s as shown on the force–time graph. What is its change in speed Δv?
items.workedSolution: Impulse J = area under F–t trapezium = ½(0.5 + 0.3)(42) = 16.8 N s. Speed increase Δv = J / m = 16.8 / 0.8 = 21.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Computes J = 16.8 N s and Δv = J / 0.8 = 21.0 m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: Moving forward from x = 0.0 m with initial speed 6.0 m s⁻¹, a warehouse pallet shuttle (mass 3.0 kg) is subjected to the resultant force–displacement profile shown up to x = 15.0 m. How much net work is done on it over the 15.0 m displacement?
items.workedSolution: Forward work (0 to 12 m) = 162 J; resistive work (12 m to 15 m) = −9.00 J. Net work = 162 − 9.00 = 153 J.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts resistive triangle (9.00 J) from positive trapezium (162 J) to get 153 J (D).

items.stem: The stress–strain graph shows a polypropylene surgical suture stretched reversibly through two piecewise-linear stages up to strain 0.4 (kink at strain 0.2). What work is done per unit volume in stretching the specimen to strain 0.4?
items.workedSolution: Work per unit volume equals area under the σ–ε graph (1 MPa × 1 = 1 MJ m⁻³): u = ½(0.2)(120) + ½(120 + 180)(0.2) = 42.0 MJ m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Sums triangle and trapezium areas under σ–ε curve to obtain 42.0 MJ m⁻³ (B).

items.stem: Load tests on a silver-oxide instrument battery up to I = 0.8 A produce the straight-line V–I trace shown. Calculate the signed gradient of the graph in V A⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: At I = 0.0 A, V = ε = 4.2 V; at I = 0.8 A, V = 2.2 V. Gradient = (2.2 − 4.2) / 0.8 = -2.50 V A⁻¹ (equal to −r).

items.stem: Speed-squared readings v² are graphed against displacement s (0.0 m to 1.6 m) for an air-bearing carriage coasting down a Precision granite incline on a frictionless ramp of sin θ = 0.25 where g = 9.81 m s⁻². Calculate the gradient of the line.
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 4.2 m² s⁻² and at s = 1.6 m, v² = 12.048 m² s⁻². Gradient = (12.048 − 4.2) / 1.6 = 2(9.81)(0.25) = 4.91 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 4.2 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.81 × 0.25) to get 4.91 m s⁻² (A).

items.stem: In an electrostatics investigation with charged copper electrodes on a laser-deflection cantilever, F is plotted against r⁻² up to 25.0 m⁻². Extract the proportionality constant k|Q₁Q₂| given by the slope.
items.workedSolution: At r⁻² = 0.0 m⁻², tare offset F₀ = 0.1 N; at r⁻² = 25 m⁻², F = 1.25 N. Gradient = (1.25 − 0.1) / 25 = 0.0460 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts tare offset F₀ = 0.1 N to get (1.25 − 0.1) / 25 = 0.0460 N m² (C).

items.stem: On a straight test section, a cleanroom wafer transport shuttle moves along a linear air bearing (to the right positive) as shown on the velocity–time graph. What is its net displacement from t = 0.0 s to t = 12.0 s?
items.workedSolution: Velocity reaches zero at t = 8 s. Positive area = 132 m and area below the axis has magnitude 28.0 m. Net displacement = 132 − 28.0 = 104 m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts reverse area (28.0 m) from forward area (132 m) to obtain 104 m (D).

items.stem: Beginning 28.0 m past a optical home flag, a high-speed bottling-line transfer sled follows the velocity–time profile shown over 16.0 s. What is its mean speed during the 16.0 s journey?
items.workedSolution: Distance travelled Δx = ½(16 + 8)(20) = 240 m (independent of the 28 m starting offset). Mean speed = 240 / 16 = 15.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Divides trapezium distance (240 m) by 16 s to obtain 15.0 m s⁻¹ (A).

items.stem: At t = 0.0 s, a vertical-launch sounding sled is already moving upward at 14.0 m s⁻¹. Its signed acceleration over the next 12.0 s (upward positive) is plotted. What maximum speed does it reach during the 12.0 s interval?
items.workedSolution: Speed increases while a > 0 (from t = 0.0 s until a = 0 at t = 6 s). Positive area Δv_max = (2)(6) + ½(4)(6) = 24.0 m s⁻¹. Maximum speed = u₀ + Δv_max = 14 + 24.0 = 38.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Integrates positive acceleration up to t = 6 s (24.0 m s⁻¹) and adds 14 m s⁻¹ to get 38.0 m s⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: A thruster acts from t = 2.0 s to t = 7.0 s on an ice-rink calibration sled of mass 5.0 kg, producing the momentum–time trace shown. What kinetic energy gain (net work) occurs over this interval?
items.workedSolution: Using E_k = p² / (2m), net work W = ΔE_k = (30² − 10²) / (2 × 5) = 80.0 J.

items.stem: The resultant force in the direction of motion of a wind-propelled land-yacht rig (mass 2.0 kg, initial speed 7.0 m s⁻¹) is plotted over 16.0 m. Determine its speed at x = 16.0 m.
items.workedSolution: Positive work (0 to 12 m) = ½(12 + 6)(10) = 90.0 J. Resistive work (12 m to 16 m) = −½(4)(2) = −4.00 J. Net work W = 86.0 J. From ½mv² = ½mu₀² + W, v = √(7² + 2 × 86.0 / 2) = 11.6 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Finds net work W = 86.0 J and v = √(7² + 2W/2) = 11.6 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: Refer to the tensile stress–strain plot for a regenerated silk-fibroin strand, whose limit of proportionality lies at strain 0.25. Calculate its initial Young's modulus.
items.workedSolution: Up to the limit of proportionality at ε = 0.25, stress reaches 230 MPa. Young's modulus E = σ / ε = 230 / 0.25 = 920 MPa.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates initial linear gradient E = 230 / 0.25 = 920 MPa (D).

items.stem: To find the resistivity ρ of a conductive carbon-polymer rod, total resistance R = ρ(L / A) + R₀ is plotted against L / A up to 100.0 m⁻¹. What value of ρ does the graph give?
items.workedSolution: Since R = ρ(L / A) + R₀, resistivity ρ equals the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A) = (24 − 4) / 100 = 0.200 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept R₀ = 4 Ω to obtain ρ = (24 − 4) / 100 = 0.200 Ω m (C).

items.stem: How steep (in m s⁻²) is the linear v² versus s graph recorded over 2.0 m for a low-drag calibration capsule descending a straight guide rail on a smooth slope (sin θ = 0.4, g = 9.8 m s⁻²)?
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 5 m² s⁻² and at s = 2 m, v² = 20.68 m² s⁻². Gradient = (20.68 − 5) / 2 = 2(9.8)(0.4) = 7.84 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 5 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.8 × 0.4) to get 7.84 m s⁻² (D).

items.stem: In the velocity–time record for a wind-tunnel moving-ground carriage (initially 45.0 m from the nozzle datum line), uniform braking begins at t = 14.0 s and ends at rest at t = 20.0 s. Find the signed braking acceleration.
items.workedSolution: During braking from t = 14 s to t = 20 s, a = (0 − 24) / (20 − 14) = -4.00 m s⁻².

items.stem: Motion sensors track the momentum of a linear air-bearing carriage of mass 3.2 kg. Determine the magnitude of the resultant force acting from t = 3.0 s to t = 8.0 s.
items.workedSolution: By Newton's second law, F = Δp / Δt = (22.4 − 6.4) / (8 − 3) = 3.20 N.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Divides Δp / Δt by mass m, obtaining acceleration rather than resultant force.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies Δp by Δt instead of evaluating the rate of change of momentum Δp / Δt.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes the secant ratio p₂ / t₂ from the origin, ignoring both initial momentum p₁ and start time t₁.

items.stem: Calculate the mean resultant force exerted during the 1.0 s docking vernier firing on a microgravity cargo pod (mass 1.2 kg, initial momentum 3.6 kg m s⁻¹) from the plotted F–t curve.
items.workedSolution: Total impulse J = ½(1 + 0.4)(40) = 28.0 N s. Mean force F_mean = J / Δt = 28.0 / 1 = 28.0 N.

markScheme.criterion: Divides impulse (28.0 N s) by 1 s to obtain 28.0 N (A).

options.label: C

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Assumes mean force is half the peak force, ignoring the flat plateau duration.

items.stem: Evaluate the average terminal potential difference delivered by a hydrogen proton-exchange fuel cell across the plotted current domain 0.0 A to 4.0 A.
items.workedSolution: Terminal p.d. varies linearly from 15 V at I = 0.0 A to 5 V at I = 4 A, so V_mean = ½(15 + 5) = 10.0 V.

markScheme.criterion: Averages endpoint voltages ½(15 + 5) = 10.0 V (C).

items.stem: Examine the straight-line plot of v² against track distance s up to 2.5 m for a magnetic-cushion puck sliding down a tilted glass rail (ramp sin θ = 0.3, g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Evaluate its gradient.
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 3.5 m² s⁻² and at s = 2.5 m, v² = 18.215 m² s⁻². Gradient = (18.215 − 3.5) / 2.5 = 2(9.81)(0.3) = 5.89 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 3.5 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.81 × 0.3) to get 5.89 m s⁻² (B).

items.stem: Varying centre-to-centre separation up to r⁻² = 80.0 m⁻² for insulated aluminium spheres monitored by a strain-gauge beam yields the linear F versus r⁻² trace shown. Evaluate the slope ΔF / Δ(r⁻²).
items.workedSolution: At r⁻² = 0.0 m⁻², tare offset F₀ = 0.4 N; at r⁻² = 80 m⁻², F = 2.4 N. Gradient = (2.4 − 0.4) / 80 = 0.0250 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts tare offset F₀ = 0.4 N to get (2.4 − 0.4) / 80 = 0.0250 N m² (B).

items.stem: During a dynamic acceptance trial, a drop-tower counterbalance carriage moves inside a vertical guide shaft, taking upward as positive. Using the velocity–time graph recorded from t = 0.0 s to t = 14.0 s, determine the total distance travelled.
items.workedSolution: Velocity crosses zero at t = 9 s. Forward area (0 to 9 s) = ½(2)(18) + (4)(18) + ½(3)(18) = 117 m. Reverse area magnitude (9 s to 14 s) = ½(1)(6) + (4)(6) = 27.0 m. Total distance = 117 + 27.0 = 144 m.

markScheme.criterion: Sums unsigned positive (117 m) and negative (27.0 m) velocity–time areas to obtain 144 m (C).

items.stem: Starting 32.0 m beyond the concourse datum post at t = 0.0 s, an inter-terminal airport monorail executes the 10.0 s velocity–time profile shown. How far from the concourse datum post does it come to rest?
items.workedSolution: Displacement during the 10 s run equals the trapezium area: Δx = ½(10 + 6)(19) = 152 m. Final position from the concourse datum post = x₀ + Δx = 32 + 152 = 184 m.

markScheme.criterion: Adds trapezium area (152 m) to initial offset (32 m) to get 184 m (D).

items.stem: Initially travelling upward at 18.0 m s⁻¹, a drop-shaft recovery gondola undergoes the signed acceleration–time profile shown for 12.0 s. What is its velocity at t = 12.0 s?
items.workedSolution: Positive a–t area (0 to 6 s) = 36.0 m s⁻¹; negative area magnitude (6 s to 12 s) = 18.0 m s⁻¹. Net Δv = 36.0 − 18.0 = 18.0 m s⁻¹. Final velocity = 18 + (18.0) = 36.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Combines net signed area (18.0 m s⁻¹) with u₀ = 18 m s⁻¹ to obtain 36.0 m s⁻¹ (A).

items.stem: A cold-gas thruster burn acts for 5.0 s in the direction of motion of a cold-gas attitude probe (mass 6.0 kg, initial momentum 18.0 kg m s⁻¹). Using the plotted force–time profile, determine Δv.
items.workedSolution: Impulse J = area under F–t trapezium = ½(5 + 3)(40) = 160 N s. Speed increase Δv = J / m = 160 / 6 = 26.7 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Computes J = 160 N s and Δv = J / 6 = 26.7 m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: Passing x = 0.0 m with speed 4.0 m s⁻¹, an instrumented crash-test carriage of mass 3.2 kg experiences the collinear resultant force plotted against displacement up to x = 14.0 m. What is its speed at x = 14.0 m?
items.workedSolution: Positive work (0 to 11 m) = ½(11 + 6)(16) = 136 J. Resistive work (11 m to 14 m) = −½(3)(4) = −6.00 J. Net work W = 130 J. From ½mv² = ½mu₀² + W, v = √(4² + 2 × 130 / 3.2) = 9.86 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Finds net work W = 130 J and v = √(4² + 2W/3.2) = 9.86 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: In a tensile materials test, a polypropylene surgical suture obeys Hooke's law up to a strain of 0.5 before softening up to strain 1.0, as shown on the stress–strain graph. What is the Young's modulus of the material in the initial linear region?
items.workedSolution: Up to the limit of proportionality at ε = 0.5, stress reaches 280 MPa. Young's modulus E = σ / ε = 280 / 0.5 = 560 MPa.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates initial linear gradient E = 280 / 0.5 = 560 MPa (B).

items.stem: Examine the linear V–I characteristic recorded for a silver-oxide instrument battery between zero current and 1.0 A. What is its signed gradient?
items.workedSolution: At I = 0.0 A, V = ε = 5.5 V; at I = 1 A, V = 2.5 V. Gradient = (2.5 − 5.5) / 1 = -3.00 V A⁻¹ (equal to −r).

items.stem: Two-wire resistance readings R across an aqueous copper-sulfate capillary cell include a fixed fixture offset R₀ when graphed against L / A from zero to 400.0 m⁻¹. Evaluate the resistivity ρ in Ω m.
items.workedSolution: Since R = ρ(L / A) + R₀, resistivity ρ equals the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A) = (36 − 8) / 400 = 0.0700 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept R₀ = 8 Ω to obtain ρ = (36 − 8) / 400 = 0.0700 Ω m (B).

items.stem: Subtracting the constant zero-offset intercept on the F versus r⁻² plot (0.0 m⁻² to 50.0 m⁻²) for charged copper electrodes on a laser-deflection cantilever, find the gradient in N m².
items.workedSolution: At r⁻² = 0.0 m⁻², tare offset F₀ = 0.3 N; at r⁻² = 50 m⁻², F = 1.9 N. Gradient = (1.9 − 0.3) / 50 = 0.0320 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts tare offset F₀ = 0.3 N to get (1.9 − 0.3) / 50 = 0.0320 N m² (B).

items.stem: Over a 16.0 s transfer starting at x = 38.0 m from the sorting-hall origin sensor, a linear-induction baggage carrier has the velocity–time graph shown. Calculate its average speed over the 16.0 s interval.
items.workedSolution: Distance travelled Δx = ½(16 + 7)(16) = 184 m (independent of the 38 m starting offset). Mean speed = 184 / 16 = 11.5 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Divides trapezium distance (184 m) by 16 s to obtain 11.5 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: The graph displays the linear momentum of a frictionless puck on an air table (mass 6.0 kg) against time. What resultant force acts on it between t = 4.0 s and t = 10.0 s?
items.workedSolution: By Newton's second law, F = Δp / Δt = (36 − 12) / (10 − 4) = 4.00 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F = Δp / Δt = (36 − 12) / (6) = 4.00 N (D).

items.stem: Moving in a straight line with initial momentum 8.0 kg m s⁻¹, a crash-barrier test sled (mass 2.0 kg) undergoes the 2.0 s hydraulic arrester pulse shown. What is its final momentum at t = 2.0 s?
items.workedSolution: Impulse Δp = ½(2 + 1)(35) = 52.5 N s. Final momentum p_f = p₀ + Δp = 8 + 52.5 = 60.5 kg m s⁻¹.

items.stem: The stress–strain graph shows a regenerated silk-fibroin strand stretched reversibly through two piecewise-linear stages up to strain 0.6 (kink at strain 0.3). What work is done per unit volume in stretching the specimen to strain 0.6?
items.workedSolution: Work per unit volume equals area under the σ–ε graph (1 MPa × 1 = 1 MJ m⁻³): u = ½(0.3)(180) + ½(180 + 250)(0.3) = 91.5 MJ m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Sums triangle and trapezium areas under σ–ε curve to obtain 91.5 MJ m⁻³ (D).

items.stem: In a materials conductivity test on a conductive carbon-polymer rod, measured resistance R varies linearly with L / A up to 80.0 m⁻¹ as shown. Extract the bulk resistivity ρ.
items.workedSolution: Since R = ρ(L / A) + R₀, resistivity ρ equals the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A) = (25 − 5) / 80 = 0.250 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept R₀ = 5 Ω to obtain ρ = (25 − 5) / 80 = 0.250 Ω m (D).

options.distractorRationale: Adds the zero-offset intercept R₀ to R_max instead of subtracting it when finding ΔR.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Δ(L/A) / ΔR (electrical conductivity σ) instead of ΔR / Δ(L/A).

items.stem: An optical timer measures speed v of a low-drag calibration capsule descending a straight guide rail at positions up to s = 4.0 m along a frictionless incline (sin θ = 0.15, g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What is the slope of the resulting v²–s graph?
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 2.6 m² s⁻² and at s = 4 m, v² = 14.372 m² s⁻². Gradient = (14.372 − 2.6) / 4 = 2(9.81)(0.15) = 2.94 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 2.6 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.81 × 0.15) to get 2.94 m s⁻² (C).

items.stem: Inspect the constant-gradient reversal stage from t = 5.0 s to t = 8.0 s for an automated rail inspection trolley moving along a straight viaduct rail. What signed acceleration acts over this stage?
items.workedSolution: Between t = 5 s and t = 8 s, velocity changes from +16 m s⁻¹ to −8 m s⁻¹. Acceleration a = Δv / Δt = (−8 − 16) / (8 − 5) = -8.00 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δv / Δt = (−8 − 16) / (3) = -8.00 m s⁻² (B).

items.stem: An accelerometer mounted on a linear-motor brake-test bogie records the 20.0 s profile shown, starting from an initial along the track velocity of 17.0 m s⁻¹. Determine the greatest along the track speed attained.
items.workedSolution: Speed increases while a > 0 (from t = 0.0 s until a = 0 at t = 10 s). Positive area Δv_max = (6)(6) + ½(4)(6) = 48.0 m s⁻¹. Maximum speed = u₀ + Δv_max = 17 + 48.0 = 65.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Integrates positive acceleration up to t = 10 s (48.0 m s⁻¹) and adds 17 m s⁻¹ to get 65.0 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: During a 0.8 s solenoid kicker stroke, a robotic soccer puck (mass 2.0 kg, initial momentum 6.0 kg m s⁻¹) experiences the force–time profile shown. What is the time-averaged resultant force over the 0.8 s interval?
items.workedSolution: Total impulse J = ½(0.8 + 0.4)(50) = 30.0 N s. Mean force F_mean = J / Δt = 30.0 / 0.8 = 37.5 N.

markScheme.criterion: Divides impulse (30.0 N s) by 0.8 s to obtain 37.5 N (A).

items.stem: A 2.0 kg unit (a magnetic-launch coaster bogie) enters an instrumented zone at 5.0 m s⁻¹. From the resultant force–displacement graph over 10.0 m, calculate its exit speed at x = 10.0 m.
items.workedSolution: Positive work (0 to 8 m) = ½(8 + 4)(12) = 72.0 J. Resistive work (8 m to 10 m) = −½(2)(4) = −4.00 J. Net work W = 68.0 J. From ½mv² = ½mu₀² + W, v = √(5² + 2 × 68.0 / 2) = 9.64 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Finds net work W = 68.0 J and v = √(5² + 2W/2) = 9.64 m s⁻¹ (A).

items.stem: The tensile stress–strain curve for a cross-linked elastomer strip is linear from 0.0 to strain 0.2 and reaches strain 0.4. Determine the Young's modulus in MPa.
items.workedSolution: Up to the limit of proportionality at ε = 0.2, stress reaches 150 MPa. Young's modulus E = σ / ε = 150 / 0.2 = 750 MPa.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates initial linear gradient E = 150 / 0.2 = 750 MPa (B).

items.stem: The terminal potential difference V of a hydrogen proton-exchange fuel cell decreases linearly with load current I from 0.0 A to 2.0 A, as shown. What is the mean terminal potential difference across this current range?
items.workedSolution: Terminal p.d. varies linearly from 7 V at I = 0.0 A to 3.4 V at I = 2 A, so V_mean = ½(7 + 3.4) = 5.20 V.

markScheme.criterion: Averages endpoint voltages ½(7 + 3.4) = 5.20 V (D).

options.distractorRationale: Halves the EMF as if terminal voltage dropped to zero at I_max.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes the lost volts ΔV at I_max rather than the mean terminal potential difference.

options.label: C

items.stem: Using two light gates in a gravitational field g = 9.8 m s⁻², a student records speed v of a magnetic-cushion puck sliding down a tilted glass rail (inclination sin θ = 0.45) after passing an initial gate at s = 0.0 m with speed u₀ > 0, plotting v² against distance s up to 1.2 m. According to v² = u₀² + 2as, what is the gradient Δ(v²) / Δs of the line?
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 3.8 m² s⁻² and at s = 1.2 m, v² = 14.384 m² s⁻². Gradient = (14.384 − 3.8) / 1.2 = 2(9.8)(0.45) = 8.82 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 3.8 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.8 × 0.45) to get 8.82 m s⁻² (D).

items.workedSolution: At r⁻² = 0.0 m⁻², tare offset F₀ = 0.3 N; at r⁻² = 60 m⁻², F = 1.9 N. Gradient = (1.9 − 0.3) / 60 = 0.0267 N m².

items.stem: Telemetry from a magnetic-levitation shuttle pod operating on a horizontal vacuum test guideway is plotted on the velocity–time axes shown (to the right positive). What total path distance is covered over the 12.0 s run?
items.workedSolution: Velocity crosses zero at t = 8 s. Forward area (0 to 8 s) = ½(2)(16) + (4)(16) + ½(2)(16) = 96.0 m. Reverse area magnitude (8 s to 12 s) = ½(1)(8) + (3)(8) = 28.0 m. Total distance = 96.0 + 28.0 = 124 m.

markScheme.criterion: Sums unsigned positive (96.0 m) and negative (28.0 m) velocity–time areas to obtain 124 m (A).

items.stem: Sensors record a solar-powered desert research rover initially at x = 30.0 m relative to a base-camp beacon. Using the velocity–time plot up to t = 12.0 s, determine its final coordinate x.
items.workedSolution: Displacement during the 12 s run equals the trapezium area: Δx = ½(12 + 5)(14) = 119 m. Final position from the base-camp beacon = x₀ + Δx = 30 + 119 = 149 m.

markScheme.criterion: Adds trapezium area (119 m) to initial offset (30 m) to get 149 m (C).

items.stem: Telemetry shows the upward acceleration of a drop-shaft recovery gondola over 6.0 s. Given an initial upward velocity of 9.0 m s⁻¹ at t = 0.0 s, calculate the velocity at t = 6.0 s.
items.workedSolution: Positive a–t area (0 to 3 s) = 24.0 m s⁻¹; negative area magnitude (3 s to 6 s) = 15.0 m s⁻¹. Net Δv = 24.0 − 15.0 = 9.00 m s⁻¹. Final velocity = 9 + (9.00) = 18.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Combines net signed area (9.00 m s⁻¹) with u₀ = 9 m s⁻¹ to obtain 18.0 m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: Determine the strain energy stored per unit volume (in MJ m⁻³) when a vulcanized neoprene damper rod is loaded from zero strain to 0.5 along the plotted stress–strain curve (proportional limit at 0.2).
items.workedSolution: Work per unit volume equals area under the σ–ε graph (1 MPa × 1 = 1 MJ m⁻³): u = ½(0.2)(190) + ½(190 + 290)(0.3) = 91.0 MJ m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Sums triangle and trapezium areas under σ–ε curve to obtain 91.0 MJ m⁻³ (C).

options.distractorRationale: Integrates only up to the limit of proportionality at ε₁ and omits the trapezium from ε₁ to ε_max.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Approximates the entire bilinear curve as a single triangle from (0, 0) to (ε_max, σ_max).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies peak stress by maximum strain without integrating the piecewise area.

items.stem: Inspect the linear plot of measured resistance R versus L / A (spanning 0.0 m⁻¹ to 50.0 m⁻¹) for an aqueous copper-sulfate capillary cell. What is the material's resistivity ρ?
items.workedSolution: Since R = ρ(L / A) + R₀, resistivity ρ equals the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A) = (20 − 4) / 50 = 0.320 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept R₀ = 4 Ω to obtain ρ = (20 − 4) / 50 = 0.320 Ω m (C).

items.stem: In a kinematics linearization lab (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²), a PTFE-shod test block sliding down a polished low-friction chute on a frictionless slope with sin θ = 0.3 passes s = 0.0 m at speed u₀ and continues to s = 1.5 m. Determine the gradient of the plotted v² versus s graph.
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 4.5 m² s⁻² and at s = 1.5 m, v² = 13.329 m² s⁻². Gradient = (13.329 − 4.5) / 1.5 = 2(9.81)(0.3) = 5.89 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 4.5 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.81 × 0.3) to get 5.89 m s⁻² (A).

items.stem: Examine the 16.0 s velocity–time curve for a shipyard gantry crane crab (initial coordinate 35.0 m from the western end-stop). What mean speed is achieved during this movement?
items.workedSolution: Distance travelled Δx = ½(16 + 6)(19) = 209 m (independent of the 35 m starting offset). Mean speed = 209 / 16 = 13.1 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Divides trapezium distance (209 m) by 16 s to obtain 13.1 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: A thruster acts from t = 3.0 s to t = 7.0 s on a superconducting levitation carrier of mass 2.4 kg, producing the momentum–time trace shown. What kinetic energy gain (net work) occurs over this interval?
items.workedSolution: Using E_k = p² / (2m), net work W = ΔE_k = (16.8² − 4.8²) / (2 × 2.4) = 54.0 J.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates (Δp)² / (2m) instead of the change in kinetic energy (p₂² − p₁²) / (2m).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes the final kinetic energy p₂² / (2m) without subtracting the initial kinetic energy p₁² / (2m).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2 in the denominator of E_k = p² / (2m).

items.stem: Before a 2.0 s pulsed ion-beam firing, a Hall-effect thruster test rig of mass 4.0 kg has momentum 12.0 kg m s⁻¹. Using the force–time plot, find its momentum immediately after the pulse.
items.workedSolution: Impulse Δp = ½(2 + 1)(42) = 63.0 N s. Final momentum p_f = p₀ + Δp = 12 + 63.0 = 75.0 kg m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Adds impulse (63.0 N s) to p₀ = 12 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 75.0 kg m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: In an internal-resistance experiment on a lithium-iron-phosphate storage cell, a student plots terminal potential difference V versus current I from 0.0 A to 2.5 A. Determine the gradient ΔV / ΔI of the line.
items.workedSolution: At I = 0.0 A, V = ε = 10 V; at I = 2.5 A, V = 4 V. Gradient = (4 − 10) / 2.5 = -2.40 V A⁻¹ (equal to −r).

items.stem: Photogate data for a card-carrying glider on an inclined linear air track accelerating down an incline (sin θ = 0.25, g = 9.8 m s⁻²) from s = 0.0 m to s = 2.0 m are linearized by plotting v² against s. What gradient does the best-fit line have?
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 3 m² s⁻² and at s = 2 m, v² = 12.8 m² s⁻². Gradient = (12.8 − 3) / 2 = 2(9.8)(0.25) = 4.90 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 3 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.8 × 0.25) to get 4.90 m s⁻² (A).

items.stem: Examine the straight-line graph of balance force F against r⁻² (spanning 0.0 m⁻² to 50.0 m⁻²) for two conducting pith spheres on a digital top-pan balance. What value does its gradient take?
items.workedSolution: At r⁻² = 0.0 m⁻², tare offset F₀ = 0.1 N; at r⁻² = 50 m⁻², F = 1.3 N. Gradient = (1.3 − 0.1) / 50 = 0.0240 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts tare offset F₀ = 0.1 N to get (1.3 − 0.1) / 50 = 0.0240 N m² (D).

items.stem: Between t = 4.0 s and t = 8.0 s, a reverse thrust acts on a cable-hauled alpine service car on a straight haulage section. Determine the acceleration indicated by the velocity–time plot.
items.workedSolution: Between t = 4 s and t = 8 s, velocity changes from +12 m s⁻¹ to −4 m s⁻¹. Acceleration a = Δv / Δt = (−4 − 12) / (8 − 4) = -4.00 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δv / Δt = (−4 − 12) / (4) = -4.00 m s⁻² (D).

items.stem: In the velocity–time record for an underground mine haulage skip (initially 22.0 m from the shaft loading datum), uniform braking begins at t = 6.0 s and ends at rest at t = 8.0 s. Find the signed braking acceleration.
items.workedSolution: During braking from t = 6 s to t = 8 s, a = (0 − 12) / (8 − 6) = -6.00 m s⁻².

options.distractorRationale: Finds the magnitude of deceleration but omits the negative sign required for signed acceleration.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Δt / Δv instead of computing Δv / Δt.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Divides the velocity drop by the full journey duration t₃ instead of the braking duration (t₃ − t₂).

items.stem: Moving along the track at 10.0 m s⁻¹ at t = 0.0 s, a linear-motor brake-test bogie experiences the acceleration–time history plotted over 10.0 s. Find its peak speed.
items.workedSolution: Speed increases while a > 0 (from t = 0.0 s until a = 0 at t = 6 s). Positive area Δv_max = (3)(4) + ½(3)(4) = 18.0 m s⁻¹. Maximum speed = u₀ + Δv_max = 10 + 18.0 = 28.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Integrates positive acceleration up to t = 6 s (18.0 m s⁻¹) and adds 10 m s⁻¹ to get 28.0 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: Calculate the mean resultant force exerted during the 1.6 s controlled gas-jet pulse on a ballistic pendulum carriage (mass 1.5 kg, initial momentum 4.5 kg m s⁻¹) from the plotted F–t curve.
items.workedSolution: Total impulse J = ½(1.6 + 0.8)(40) = 48.0 N s. Mean force F_mean = J / Δt = 48.0 / 1.6 = 30.0 N.

markScheme.criterion: Divides impulse (48.0 N s) by 1.6 s to obtain 30.0 N (D).

items.stem: The stress–strain graph shows a cross-linked elastomer strip stretched reversibly through two piecewise-linear stages up to strain 0.8 (kink at strain 0.4). What work is done per unit volume in stretching the specimen to strain 0.8?
items.workedSolution: Work per unit volume equals area under the σ–ε graph (1 MPa × 1 = 1 MJ m⁻³): u = ½(0.4)(230) + ½(230 + 320)(0.4) = 156 MJ m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Sums triangle and trapezium areas under σ–ε curve to obtain 156 MJ m⁻³ (C).

items.stem: As current drawn from a hydrogen proton-exchange fuel cell rises steadily from zero to 1.6 A, V follows the straight line on the graph. Determine the mean terminal voltage over this range.
items.workedSolution: Terminal p.d. varies linearly from 5.8 V at I = 0.0 A to 2.6 V at I = 1.6 A, so V_mean = ½(5.8 + 2.6) = 4.20 V.

markScheme.criterion: Averages endpoint voltages ½(5.8 + 2.6) = 4.20 V (A).

items.stem: Eliminating the constant probe-lead offset from the R versus L / A graph (plotted to 500.0 m⁻¹), find the resistivity ρ of a concentrated saline conductivity column.
items.workedSolution: Since R = ρ(L / A) + R₀, resistivity ρ equals the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A) = (36 − 7) / 500 = 0.0580 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept R₀ = 7 Ω to obtain ρ = (36 − 7) / 500 = 0.0580 Ω m (A).

items.stem: To test Coulomb's inverse-square law using insulated aluminium spheres monitored by a strain-gauge beam with an unzeroed tare offset F₀, the force reading F is plotted against inverse-square separation (r⁻²) up to 100.0 m⁻², following F = k|Q₁Q₂|r⁻² + F₀. What is the gradient k|Q₁Q₂| of the line?
items.workedSolution: At r⁻² = 0.0 m⁻², tare offset F₀ = 0.2 N; at r⁻² = 100 m⁻², F = 1.8 N. Gradient = (1.8 − 0.2) / 100 = 0.0160 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts tare offset F₀ = 0.2 N to get (1.8 − 0.2) / 100 = 0.0160 N m² (C).

items.stem: At t = 0.0 s, a high-speed bottling-line transfer sled is stationary at a position 40.0 m ahead of a optical home flag. It then moves forward along a straight guideway according to the velocity–time graph for 20.0 s. What is its final distance from the optical home flag at t = 20.0 s?
items.workedSolution: Displacement during the 20 s run equals the trapezium area: Δx = ½(20 + 10)(18) = 270 m. Final position from the optical home flag = x₀ + Δx = 40 + 270 = 310 m.

markScheme.criterion: Adds trapezium area (270 m) to initial offset (40 m) to get 310 m (C).

items.stem: In a linear dynamics experiment, an ice-rink calibration sled of mass 4.0 kg moves in a straight line with momentum varying as shown. How much net work is done on it between t = 4.0 s and t = 8.0 s?
items.workedSolution: Using E_k = p² / (2m), net work W = ΔE_k = (28² − 8²) / (2 × 4) = 90.0 J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies W = (p₂² − p₁²) / (2m) = (28² − 8²) / (8) = 90.0 J (B).

items.stem: Having initial forward momentum 15.0 kg m s⁻¹, a linear-motor launch shuttle of mass 5.0 kg experiences a collinear stator current pulse over 4.0 s as shown on the force–time graph. What is its change in speed Δv?
items.workedSolution: Impulse J = area under F–t trapezium = ½(4 + 2)(35) = 105 N s. Speed increase Δv = J / m = 105 / 5 = 21.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Computes J = 105 N s and Δv = J / 5 = 21.0 m s⁻¹ (A).

items.stem: In a tensile materials test, a vulcanized neoprene damper rod obeys Hooke's law up to a strain of 0.3 before softening up to strain 0.6, as shown on the stress–strain graph. What is the Young's modulus of the material in the initial linear region?
items.workedSolution: Up to the limit of proportionality at ε = 0.3, stress reaches 210 MPa. Young's modulus E = σ / ε = 210 / 0.3 = 700 MPa.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates initial linear gradient E = 210 / 0.3 = 700 MPa (A).

items.stem: Using crocodile clips with constant contact resistance R₀, a student measures total resistance R of an aqueous copper-sulfate capillary cell for different length-to-area ratios (L / A) up to 200.0 m⁻¹, so R = ρ(L / A) + R₀. From the plotted line, what is the resistivity ρ of the material?
items.workedSolution: Since R = ρ(L / A) + R₀, resistivity ρ equals the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A) = (25 − 5) / 200 = 0.100 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept R₀ = 5 Ω to obtain ρ = (25 − 5) / 200 = 0.100 Ω m (D).

items.stem: Taking g = 9.8 m s⁻², a PTFE-shod test block sliding down a polished low-friction chute descends a smooth plane inclined at sin θ = 0.4, passing s = 0.0 m already in motion. From the v² against s plot up to 1.6 m, find the slope Δ(v²) / Δs.
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 3.4 m² s⁻² and at s = 1.6 m, v² = 15.944 m² s⁻². Gradient = (15.944 − 3.4) / 1.6 = 2(9.8)(0.4) = 7.84 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 3.4 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.8 × 0.4) to get 7.84 m s⁻² (A).

items.stem: On a straight test section, an underwater ROV thruster sled moves along a taut calibration tether (away from the dock positive) as shown on the velocity–time graph. What is its net displacement from t = 0.0 s to t = 15.0 s?
items.workedSolution: Velocity reaches zero at t = 9 s. Positive area = 130 m and area below the axis has magnitude 55.0 m. Net displacement = 130 − 55.0 = 75.0 m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts reverse area (55.0 m) from forward area (130 m) to obtain 75.0 m (D).

items.stem: After passing t = 0.0 s with upward speed 12.0 m s⁻¹, a mine hoist cage experiences the 12.0 s acceleration curve plotted. Determine its final velocity at t = 12.0 s.
items.workedSolution: Positive a–t area (0 to 6 s) = 25.0 m s⁻¹; negative area magnitude (6 s to 12 s) = 9.00 m s⁻¹. Net Δv = 25.0 − 9.00 = 16.0 m s⁻¹. Final velocity = 12 + (16.0) = 28.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Combines net signed area (16.0 m s⁻¹) with u₀ = 12 m s⁻¹ to obtain 28.0 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: Moving in a straight line with initial momentum 2.4 kg m s⁻¹, a microgravity cargo pod (mass 0.8 kg) undergoes the 0.5 s docking vernier firing shown. What is its final momentum at t = 0.5 s?
items.workedSolution: Impulse Δp = ½(0.5 + 0.3)(42) = 16.8 N s. Final momentum p_f = p₀ + Δp = 2.4 + 16.8 = 19.2 kg m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Adds impulse (16.8 N s) to p₀ = 2.4 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 19.2 kg m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: Determine the strain energy stored per unit volume (in MJ m⁻³) when a high-density polyethylene filament is loaded from zero strain to 0.4 along the plotted stress–strain curve (proportional limit at 0.2).
items.workedSolution: Work per unit volume equals area under the σ–ε graph (1 MPa × 1 = 1 MJ m⁻³): u = ½(0.2)(120) + ½(120 + 180)(0.2) = 42.0 MJ m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Sums triangle and trapezium areas under σ–ε curve to obtain 42.0 MJ m⁻³ (D).

items.stem: Load tests on a lithium-iron-phosphate storage cell up to I = 0.8 A produce the straight-line V–I trace shown. Calculate the signed gradient of the graph in V A⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: At I = 0.0 A, V = ε = 4.2 V; at I = 0.8 A, V = 2.2 V. Gradient = (2.2 − 4.2) / 0.8 = -2.50 V A⁻¹ (equal to −r).

items.stem: Speed-squared readings v² are graphed against displacement s (0.0 m to 2.5 m) for a card-carrying glider on an inclined linear air track on a frictionless ramp of sin θ = 0.2 where g = 9.81 m s⁻². Calculate the gradient of the line.
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 2.8 m² s⁻² and at s = 2.5 m, v² = 12.61 m² s⁻². Gradient = (12.61 − 2.8) / 2.5 = 2(9.81)(0.2) = 3.92 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 2.8 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.81 × 0.2) to get 3.92 m s⁻² (C).

items.stem: Readings F from two conducting pith spheres on a digital top-pan balance are linearized against r⁻² from 0.0 m⁻² to 80.0 m⁻². Accounting for the systematic zero-offset F₀, determine the gradient ΔF / Δ(r⁻²).
items.workedSolution: At r⁻² = 0.0 m⁻², tare offset F₀ = 0.2 N; at r⁻² = 80 m⁻², F = 2.2 N. Gradient = (2.2 − 0.2) / 80 = 0.0250 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts tare offset F₀ = 0.2 N to get (2.2 − 0.2) / 80 = 0.0250 N m² (C).

items.stem: While operating along a linear air bearing (to the right positive), a cleanroom wafer transport shuttle brakes and reverses direction between t = 5.0 s and t = 9.0 s. From the velocity–time graph, what is its acceleration during this interval?
items.workedSolution: Between t = 5 s and t = 9 s, velocity changes from +24 m s⁻¹ to −8 m s⁻¹. Acceleration a = Δv / Δt = (−8 − 24) / (9 − 5) = -8.00 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δv / Δt = (−8 − 24) / (4) = -8.00 m s⁻² (D).

items.stem: Starting at x = 28.0 m from a concourse datum post, an inter-terminal airport monorail completes the 16.0 s journey shown on the velocity–time graph, braking uniformly from t = 12.0 s to t = 16.0 s. What is its acceleration during braking?
items.workedSolution: During braking from t = 12 s to t = 16 s, a = (0 − 20) / (16 − 12) = -5.00 m s⁻².

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Δt / Δv instead of computing Δv / Δt.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Divides the velocity drop by the full journey duration t₃ instead of the braking duration (t₃ − t₂).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Finds the magnitude of deceleration but omits the negative sign required for signed acceleration.

items.stem: How fast is a linear-motor brake-test bogie travelling at its instant of greatest speed during the 10.0 s acceleration–time record shown, given an initial along the track velocity of 11.0 m s⁻¹?
items.workedSolution: Speed increases while a > 0 (from t = 0.0 s until a = 0 at t = 4 s). Positive area Δv_max = (2)(10) + ½(2)(10) = 30.0 m s⁻¹. Maximum speed = u₀ + Δv_max = 11 + 30.0 = 41.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Integrates positive acceleration up to t = 4 s (30.0 m s⁻¹) and adds 11 m s⁻¹ to get 41.0 m s⁻¹ (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Treats the entire positive acceleration region as a rectangle of height a_max, ignoring the linear ramp down to zero.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates the speed at the end of the interval (t = t_end) rather than at the instant acceleration changes sign.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Integrates the positive acceleration area up to a = 0 correctly but omits the initial speed u₀.

items.stem: The momentum–time graph is recorded for an air-track glider (mass 5.0 kg) travelling along a straight guide. Calculate the net work done on the object from t = 2.0 s to t = 7.0 s.
items.workedSolution: Using E_k = p² / (2m), net work W = ΔE_k = (30² − 10²) / (2 × 5) = 80.0 J.

items.stem: A 2.0 kg unit (an instrumented crash-test carriage) enters an instrumented zone at 7.0 m s⁻¹. From the resultant force–displacement graph over 16.0 m, calculate its exit speed at x = 16.0 m.
items.workedSolution: Positive work (0 to 12 m) = ½(12 + 6)(10) = 90.0 J. Resistive work (12 m to 16 m) = −½(4)(2) = −4.00 J. Net work W = 86.0 J. From ½mv² = ½mu₀² + W, v = √(7² + 2 × 86.0 / 2) = 11.6 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Finds net work W = 86.0 J and v = √(7² + 2W/2) = 11.6 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: The tensile stress–strain curve for a bio-derived collagen fibre bundle is linear from 0.0 to strain 0.25 and reaches strain 0.5. Determine the Young's modulus in MPa.
items.workedSolution: Up to the limit of proportionality at ε = 0.25, stress reaches 230 MPa. Young's modulus E = σ / ε = 230 / 0.25 = 920 MPa.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates initial linear gradient E = 230 / 0.25 = 920 MPa (D).

items.stem: Total circuit resistance R (including lead resistance R₀) is plotted against geometric ratio L / A up to 400.0 m⁻¹ for a concentrated saline conductivity column. Calculate the electrical resistivity ρ.
items.workedSolution: Since R = ρ(L / A) + R₀, resistivity ρ equals the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A) = (46 − 10) / 400 = 0.0900 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept R₀ = 10 Ω to obtain ρ = (46 − 10) / 400 = 0.0900 Ω m (A).

items.stem: How steep (in m s⁻²) is the linear v² versus s graph recorded over 2.0 m for a dual-photogate brass cylinder released past an upper light gate on a smooth slope (sin θ = 0.35, g = 9.8 m s⁻²)?
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 4 m² s⁻² and at s = 2 m, v² = 17.72 m² s⁻². Gradient = (17.72 − 4) / 2 = 2(9.8)(0.35) = 6.86 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 4 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.8 × 0.35) to get 6.86 m s⁻² (C).

items.stem: Starting 45.0 m beyond the sorting-hall origin sensor at t = 0.0 s, a linear-induction baggage carrier executes the 20.0 s velocity–time profile shown. How far from the sorting-hall origin sensor does it come to rest?
items.workedSolution: Displacement during the 20 s run equals the trapezium area: Δx = ½(20 + 8)(24) = 336 m. Final position from the sorting-hall origin sensor = x₀ + Δx = 45 + 336 = 381 m.

markScheme.criterion: Adds trapezium area (336 m) to initial offset (45 m) to get 381 m (A).

items.stem: A hydraulic arrester pulse acts for 1.0 s in the direction of motion of a crash-barrier test sled (mass 1.2 kg, initial momentum 3.6 kg m s⁻¹). Using the plotted force–time profile, determine Δv.
items.workedSolution: Impulse J = area under F–t trapezium = ½(1 + 0.4)(40) = 28.0 N s. Speed increase Δv = J / m = 28.0 / 1.2 = 23.3 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Computes J = 28.0 N s and Δv = J / 1.2 = 23.3 m s⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: By varying a rheostat connected to a zinc-carbon dry cell, terminal voltage V is graphed against current I up to 4.0 A. Find the signed slope ΔV / ΔI.
items.workedSolution: At I = 0.0 A, V = ε = 15 V; at I = 4 A, V = 5 V. Gradient = (5 − 15) / 4 = -2.50 V A⁻¹ (equal to −r).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates (5 − 15) / 4 = -2.50 V A⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: Examine the straight-line plot of v² against track distance s up to 1.0 m for a levitated neodymium shuttle descending an inclined guide (ramp sin θ = 0.6, g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Evaluate its gradient.
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 3.2 m² s⁻² and at s = 1 m, v² = 14.972 m² s⁻². Gradient = (14.972 − 3.2) / 1 = 2(9.81)(0.6) = 11.8 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 3.2 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.81 × 0.6) to get 11.8 m s⁻² (B).

items.stem: The linearized Coulomb plot shows balance force F versus inverse-square separation r⁻² up to 100.0 m⁻² for nickel-plated hollow spheres suspended over an analytical balance. Calculate the gradient of the line in N m².
items.workedSolution: At r⁻² = 0.0 m⁻², tare offset F₀ = 0.1 N; at r⁻² = 100 m⁻², F = 1.2 N. Gradient = (1.2 − 0.1) / 100 = 0.0110 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts tare offset F₀ = 0.1 N to get (1.2 − 0.1) / 100 = 0.0110 N m² (D).

items.stem: A motion sensor tracks a drop-tower counterbalance carriage inside a vertical guide shaft for 14.0 s, taking upward velocity as positive. Find the net signed displacement at t = 14.0 s relative to its starting point.
items.workedSolution: Velocity reaches zero at t = 9 s. Positive area = 117 m and area below the axis has magnitude 27.0 m. Net displacement = 117 − 27.0 = 90.0 m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts reverse area (27.0 m) from forward area (117 m) to obtain 90.0 m (C).

items.stem: Over a 10.0 s transfer starting at x = 32.0 m from the lock-gate reference mark, a canal lock towing locomotive has the velocity–time graph shown. Calculate its average speed over the 10.0 s interval.
items.workedSolution: Distance travelled Δx = ½(10 + 6)(19) = 152 m (independent of the 32 m starting offset). Mean speed = 152 / 10 = 15.2 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Divides trapezium distance (152 m) by 10 s to obtain 15.2 m s⁻¹ (B).

options.distractorRationale: Confuses the cruise plateau velocity with the journey-wide mean speed.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Takes half of the peak velocity as if there were no constant-speed cruise plateau.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides the final coordinate (x₀ + Δx) by total time rather than dividing the distance travelled Δx by total time.

items.stem: Use the signed 12.0 s acceleration–time graph to find the terminal upward velocity of a mine hoist cage, which starts at 16.0 m s⁻¹ when t = 0.0 s.
items.workedSolution: Positive a–t area (0 to 8 s) = 24.0 m s⁻¹; negative area magnitude (8 s to 12 s) = 15.0 m s⁻¹. Net Δv = 24.0 − 15.0 = 9.00 m s⁻¹. Final velocity = 16 + (9.00) = 25.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Combines net signed area (9.00 m s⁻¹) with u₀ = 16 m s⁻¹ to obtain 25.0 m s⁻¹ (A).

options.distractorRationale: Adds the unsigned deceleration area instead of subtracting the area below the time axis.

options.distractorRationale: Computes net velocity change Δv from the signed area but forgets to add the initial velocity u₀.

items.stem: Before a 5.0 s solenoid kicker stroke, a robotic soccer puck of mass 6.0 kg has momentum 18.0 kg m s⁻¹. Using the force–time plot, find its momentum immediately after the pulse.
items.workedSolution: Impulse Δp = ½(5 + 3)(40) = 160 N s. Final momentum p_f = p₀ + Δp = 18 + 160 = 178 kg m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Adds impulse (160 N s) to p₀ = 18 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 178 kg m s⁻¹ (A).

items.stem: The resultant force in the direction of motion of a magnetic-launch coaster bogie (mass 3.2 kg, initial speed 4.0 m s⁻¹) is plotted over 14.0 m. Determine its speed at x = 14.0 m.
items.workedSolution: Positive work (0 to 11 m) = ½(11 + 6)(16) = 136 J. Resistive work (11 m to 14 m) = −½(3)(4) = −6.00 J. Net work W = 130 J. From ½mv² = ½mu₀² + W, v = √(4² + 2 × 130 / 3.2) = 9.86 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Finds net work W = 130 J and v = √(4² + 2W/3.2) = 9.86 m s⁻¹ (A).

items.stem: Refer to the tensile stress–strain plot for a high-density polyethylene filament, whose limit of proportionality lies at strain 0.5. Calculate its initial Young's modulus.
items.workedSolution: Up to the limit of proportionality at ε = 0.5, stress reaches 280 MPa. Young's modulus E = σ / ε = 280 / 0.5 = 560 MPa.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates initial linear gradient E = 280 / 0.5 = 560 MPa (C).

items.stem: Examine the linear V–I characteristic recorded for a lithium-iron-phosphate storage cell between zero current and 1.0 A. What is its signed gradient?
items.workedSolution: At I = 0.0 A, V = ε = 5.5 V; at I = 1 A, V = 2.5 V. Gradient = (2.5 − 5.5) / 1 = -3.00 V A⁻¹ (equal to −r).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Assumes the line meets V = 0 at I = I_max instead of reading the non-zero terminal voltage V(I_max).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Inverts ΔI / ΔV instead of computing ΔV / ΔI.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates internal resistance r = |ΔV / ΔI| but omits the negative sign of the downward V–I gradient.

items.stem: The linearized graph shows measured resistance R versus L / A for a potassium-chloride electrolyte tube over 0.0 m⁻¹ to 200.0 m⁻¹. Accounting for the non-zero contact-resistance intercept, determine ρ.
items.workedSolution: Since R = ρ(L / A) + R₀, resistivity ρ equals the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A) = (34 − 6) / 200 = 0.140 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept R₀ = 6 Ω to obtain ρ = (34 − 6) / 200 = 0.140 Ω m (D).

options.distractorRationale: Computes the secant ratio R_max / (L/A)_max from the origin and fails to subtract the non-zero contact-resistance intercept R₀.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Adds the zero-offset intercept R₀ to R_max instead of subtracting it when finding ΔR.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Δ(L/A) / ΔR (electrical conductivity σ) instead of ΔR / Δ(L/A).

items.stem: In an electrostatics investigation with two conducting pith spheres on a digital top-pan balance, F is plotted against r⁻² up to 25.0 m⁻². Extract the proportionality constant k|Q₁Q₂| given by the slope.
items.workedSolution: At r⁻² = 0.0 m⁻², tare offset F₀ = 0.1 N; at r⁻² = 25 m⁻², F = 1.25 N. Gradient = (1.25 − 0.1) / 25 = 0.0460 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts tare offset F₀ = 0.1 N to get (1.25 − 0.1) / 25 = 0.0460 N m² (A).

items.stem: In the velocity–time record for a solar-powered desert research rover (initially 38.0 m from the base-camp beacon), uniform braking begins at t = 12.0 s and ends at rest at t = 16.0 s. Find the signed braking acceleration.
items.workedSolution: During braking from t = 12 s to t = 16 s, a = (0 − 16) / (16 − 12) = -4.00 m s⁻².

items.stem: Calculate the mean resultant force exerted during the 2.0 s spring buffer contact on a rail-mounted docking target (mass 2.0 kg, initial momentum 8.0 kg m s⁻¹) from the plotted F–t curve.
items.workedSolution: Total impulse J = ½(2 + 1)(35) = 52.5 N s. Mean force F_mean = J / Δt = 52.5 / 2 = 26.3 N.

markScheme.criterion: Divides impulse (52.5 N s) by 2 s to obtain 26.3 N (B).

items.stem: Determine the strain energy stored per unit volume (in MJ m⁻³) when a bio-derived collagen fibre bundle is loaded from zero strain to 0.6 along the plotted stress–strain curve (proportional limit at 0.3).
items.workedSolution: Work per unit volume equals area under the σ–ε graph (1 MPa × 1 = 1 MJ m⁻³): u = ½(0.3)(180) + ½(180 + 250)(0.3) = 91.5 MJ m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Sums triangle and trapezium areas under σ–ε curve to obtain 91.5 MJ m⁻³ (B).

items.stem: To find the resistivity ρ of a concentrated saline conductivity column, total resistance R = ρ(L / A) + R₀ is plotted against L / A up to 100.0 m⁻¹. What value of ρ does the graph give?
items.workedSolution: Since R = ρ(L / A) + R₀, resistivity ρ equals the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A) = (24 − 4) / 100 = 0.200 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept R₀ = 4 Ω to obtain ρ = (24 − 4) / 100 = 0.200 Ω m (A).

items.stem: An optical timer measures speed v of a dual-photogate brass cylinder released past an upper light gate at positions up to s = 2.0 m along a frictionless incline (sin θ = 0.4, g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What is the slope of the resulting v²–s graph?
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 5 m² s⁻² and at s = 2 m, v² = 20.696 m² s⁻². Gradient = (20.696 − 5) / 2 = 2(9.81)(0.4) = 7.85 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 5 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.81 × 0.4) to get 7.85 m s⁻² (D).

items.stem: From the 15.0 s acceleration–time trace for a railgun armature test sled (initial downrange speed 15.0 m s⁻¹), calculate the maximum speed reached before braking reduces its velocity.
items.workedSolution: Speed increases while a > 0 (from t = 0.0 s until a = 0 at t = 8 s). Positive area Δv_max = (5)(8) + ½(3)(8) = 52.0 m s⁻¹. Maximum speed = u₀ + Δv_max = 15 + 52.0 = 67.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Integrates positive acceleration up to t = 8 s (52.0 m s⁻¹) and adds 15 m s⁻¹ to get 67.0 m s⁻¹ (A).

items.stem: Refer to the force–time profile of a pulsed ion-beam firing on a Hall-effect thruster test rig of mass 2.0 kg (initial momentum 6.0 kg m s⁻¹). By how much does its speed increase over the 0.8 s pulse?
items.workedSolution: Impulse J = area under F–t trapezium = ½(0.8 + 0.4)(50) = 30.0 N s. Speed increase Δv = J / m = 30.0 / 2 = 15.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Computes J = 30.0 N s and Δv = J / 2 = 15.0 m s⁻¹ (A).

items.stem: Passing x = 0.0 m with speed 5.0 m s⁻¹, a linear dynamo test sled of mass 2.0 kg experiences the collinear resultant force plotted against displacement up to x = 10.0 m. What is its speed at x = 10.0 m?
items.workedSolution: Positive work (0 to 8 m) = ½(8 + 4)(12) = 72.0 J. Resistive work (8 m to 10 m) = −½(2)(4) = −4.00 J. Net work W = 68.0 J. From ½mv² = ½mu₀² + W, v = √(5² + 2 × 68.0 / 2) = 9.64 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Finds net work W = 68.0 J and v = √(5² + 2W/2) = 9.64 m s⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: In a tensile materials test, an extruded fluoropolymer ribbon obeys Hooke's law up to a strain of 0.2 before softening up to strain 0.4, as shown on the stress–strain graph. What is the Young's modulus of the material in the initial linear region?
items.workedSolution: Up to the limit of proportionality at ε = 0.2, stress reaches 150 MPa. Young's modulus E = σ / ε = 150 / 0.2 = 750 MPa.

items.stem: A variable load resistor is connected across a zinc-carbon dry cell, and the terminal potential difference V is plotted against current I up to 2.0 A. According to V = ε − Ir, what is the signed gradient of this graph?
items.workedSolution: At I = 0.0 A, V = ε = 7 V; at I = 2 A, V = 3.4 V. Gradient = (3.4 − 7) / 2 = -1.80 V A⁻¹ (equal to −r).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates (3.4 − 7) / 2 = -1.80 V A⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: Using two light gates in a gravitational field g = 9.8 m s⁻², a student records speed v of a levitated neodymium shuttle descending an inclined guide (inclination sin θ = 0.3) after passing an initial gate at s = 0.0 m with speed u₀ > 0, plotting v² against distance s up to 2.5 m. According to v² = u₀² + 2as, what is the gradient Δ(v²) / Δs of the line?
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 3.5 m² s⁻² and at s = 2.5 m, v² = 18.2 m² s⁻². Gradient = (18.2 − 3.5) / 2.5 = 2(9.8)(0.3) = 5.88 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 3.5 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.8 × 0.3) to get 5.88 m s⁻² (A).

items.stem: Varying centre-to-centre separation up to r⁻² = 80.0 m⁻² for nickel-plated hollow spheres suspended over an analytical balance yields the linear F versus r⁻² trace shown. Evaluate the slope ΔF / Δ(r⁻²).
items.workedSolution: At r⁻² = 0.0 m⁻², tare offset F₀ = 0.4 N; at r⁻² = 80 m⁻², F = 2.4 N. Gradient = (2.4 − 0.4) / 80 = 0.0250 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts tare offset F₀ = 0.4 N to get (2.4 − 0.4) / 80 = 0.0250 N m² (C).

items.stem: Refer to the signed velocity–time graph for a magnetic-levitation shuttle pod travelling on a horizontal vacuum test guideway. Determine the resultant displacement after 12.0 s.
items.workedSolution: Velocity reaches zero at t = 8 s. Positive area = 96.0 m and area below the axis has magnitude 28.0 m. Net displacement = 96.0 − 28.0 = 68.0 m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts reverse area (28.0 m) from forward area (96.0 m) to obtain 68.0 m (B).

items.stem: Examine the 12.0 s velocity–time curve for an underground mine haulage skip (initial coordinate 30.0 m from the shaft loading datum). What mean speed is achieved during this movement?
items.workedSolution: Distance travelled Δx = ½(12 + 5)(14) = 119 m (independent of the 30 m starting offset). Mean speed = 119 / 12 = 9.92 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Divides trapezium distance (119 m) by 12 s to obtain 9.92 m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: Over an interval of 12.0 s, a mine hoist cage (initial velocity 18.0 m s⁻¹ upward) follows the plotted acceleration profile. What velocity does it have when t = 12.0 s?
items.workedSolution: Positive a–t area (0 to 6 s) = 36.0 m s⁻¹; negative area magnitude (6 s to 12 s) = 18.0 m s⁻¹. Net Δv = 36.0 − 18.0 = 18.0 m s⁻¹. Final velocity = 18 + (18.0) = 36.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Combines net signed area (18.0 m s⁻¹) with u₀ = 18 m s⁻¹ to obtain 36.0 m s⁻¹ (A).

options.distractorRationale: Stops integrating when acceleration reaches zero and ignores the subsequent negative-acceleration stage.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes net velocity change Δv from the signed area but forgets to add the initial velocity u₀.

items.stem: The stress–strain graph shows a synthetic polyurethane tendon cord stretched reversibly through two piecewise-linear stages up to strain 0.5 (kink at strain 0.2). What work is done per unit volume in stretching the specimen to strain 0.5?
items.workedSolution: Work per unit volume equals area under the σ–ε graph (1 MPa × 1 = 1 MJ m⁻³): u = ½(0.2)(190) + ½(190 + 290)(0.3) = 91.0 MJ m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Sums triangle and trapezium areas under σ–ε curve to obtain 91.0 MJ m⁻³ (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Approximates the entire bilinear curve as a single triangle from (0, 0) to (ε_max, σ_max).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Integrates only up to the limit of proportionality at ε₁ and omits the trapezium from ε₁ to ε_max.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies peak stress by maximum strain without integrating the piecewise area.

items.stem: At t = 0.0 s, a shipyard gantry crane crab rests at a position 25.0 m ahead of a western end-stop. The velocity–time graph shows its forward motion over 10.0 s, with uniform braking applied from t = 7.0 s until t = 10.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Trapezium area Δx = ½(10 + 5)(16) = 120 m. (b) Final distance from datum = 25 + 120 = 145 m. (c) Mean speed = 120 / 10 = 12.0 m s⁻¹. (d) Braking acceleration = (0 − 16) / (10 − 7) = -5.33 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Identifies distance travelled as the area under the v–t trapezium.
Obtains Δx = 120 m.
Adds 25 m offset to obtain 145 m.
Divides distance travelled from (a) by 10 s.
Obtains mean speed = 12.0 m s⁻¹.
Obtains braking acceleration = -5.33 m s⁻².

items.stem: Along a horizontal guideway, a superconducting levitation carrier of mass 1.0 kg moves in a fixed direction. Its momentum–time graph shows an impulse stage from t = 2.0 s to t = 6.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Resultant force F = Δp / Δt = (9 − 3) / (6 − 2) = 1.50 N. (b) Net work W = ΔE_k = (9² − 3²) / (2 × 1) = 36.0 J.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies resultant force as gradient Δp / Δt of the p–t graph.
Obtains F = 1.50 N.
Relates net work to ΔE_k = (p₂² − p₁²) / (2m).
Substitutes p₁ = 3 kg m s⁻¹, p₂ = 9 kg m s⁻¹, and m = 1 kg.
Obtains W = 36.0 J.

items.stem: Travelling in a straight line with initial momentum 10.0 kg m s⁻¹, a ballistic pendulum carriage of mass 2.5 kg is acted upon by a collinear controlled gas-jet pulse for 1.0 s, as shown on the force–time graph.
items.workedSolution: (a) Impulse J = ½(1 + 0.6)(60) = 48.0 N s. (b) Final momentum p_f = 10 + 48.0 = 58.0 kg m s⁻¹. (c) Speed increase Δv = 48.0 / 2.5 = 19.2 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Computes impulse from the trapezium area under the F–t curve.
Obtains J = 48.0 N s.
Adds 10 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 58.0 kg m s⁻¹.
Divides impulse from (a) by 2.5 kg.
Obtains Δv = 19.2 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: A student connects an ammeter, high-impedance voltmeter, and rheostat to an alkaline lantern battery, obtaining the linear V–I plot over 0.0 A to 4.0 A.
items.workedSolution: (a) Open-circuit intercept gives ε = 13.0 V. (b) Gradient = (7 − 13) / 4 = -1.50 V A⁻¹. (c) Mean terminal p.d. = ½(13 + 7) = 10.0 V.

markScheme.criterion: Reads ε = 13.0 V at I = 0.
Evaluates (7 − 13) / 4 including negative sign.
Obtains -1.50 V A⁻¹.
Uses ½(13 + 7) or area divided by 4 A.
Obtains 10.0 V.

items.stem: A data logger records the signed velocity of a robotic warehouse retrieval carriage moving along a straight aisle rail (forward positive) over a 12.0 s cycle, with constant braking and reversal applied between t = 6.0 s and t = 10.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Zero-velocity crossing is at t = 9 s. Positive area = 108 m and unsigned negative area = 15.0 m, giving total distance = 123 m. (b) Net displacement = 108 − 15.0 = 93.0 m; average velocity = 93.0 / 12 = 7.75 m s⁻¹. (c) Acceleration = (−6 − 18) / (10 − 6) = -6.00 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Finds zero-crossing t = 9 s and evaluates both unsigned areas (108 m and 15.0 m).
Obtains total distance = 123 m.
Subtracts areas for net displacement (93.0 m) and divides by 12 s.
Obtains average velocity = 7.75 m s⁻¹.
Obtains acceleration = -6.00 m s⁻² including negative sign.

items.stem: At t = 0.0 s, a drop-shaft recovery gondola moves upward with an initial velocity of 18.0 m s⁻¹. The graph shows how its acceleration varies with time over 12.0 s (upward positive).
items.workedSolution: (a) Maximum speed occurs when acceleration crosses zero from positive to negative at t = 6.00 s. (b) Positive area = 36.0 m s⁻¹, giving v_max = 18 + 36.0 = 54.0 m s⁻¹. (c) Negative area magnitude = 18.0 m s⁻¹, so v_final = 54.0 − 18.0 = 36.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: States t = 6.00 s.
Evaluates positive area up to 6 s (36.0 m s⁻¹) and adds u₀ = 18 m s⁻¹.
Obtains v_max = 54.0 m s⁻¹.
Subtracts negative area (18.0 m s⁻¹) from v_max.
Obtains final velocity = 36.0 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: During mechanical characterization of a bio-derived collagen fibre bundle, the specimen follows a straight Hookean slope up to strain 0.25 and continues reversibly to strain 0.5.
items.workedSolution: (a) Young's modulus E = 180 / 0.25 = 720 MPa. (b) Energy per unit volume = ½(0.25)(180) + ½(180 + 260)(0.25) = 77.5 MJ m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates initial gradient σ / ε up to ε = 0.25.
Obtains E = 720 MPa.

Splits area into initial triangle plus upper trapezium.
Obtains 77.5 MJ m⁻³.

items.stem: In an electrical properties lab, resistance readings across a polypyrrole conductive polymer film are linearized against geometric factor L / A up to 400.0 m⁻¹, revealing a non-zero contact offset R₀.
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical intercept R₀ = 8.00 Ω. (b) Resistivity ρ = (36 − 8) / 400 = 0.0700 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: States R₀ = 8.00 Ω.
Identifies ρ with the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A).
Subtracts R₀ = 8 Ω from 36 Ω before dividing by 400 m⁻¹.
Obtains ρ = 0.0700 Ω m.

items.stem: Data loggers record the linear momentum of a linear air-bearing carriage (mass 3.0 kg), which experiences a constant resultant force between t = 2.0 s and t = 6.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Resultant force F = Δp / Δt = (18 − 6) / (6 − 2) = 3.00 N. (b) Net work W = ΔE_k = (18² − 6²) / (2 × 3) = 48.0 J.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies resultant force as gradient Δp / Δt of the p–t graph.
Obtains F = 3.00 N.
Relates net work to ΔE_k = (p₂² − p₁²) / (2m).
Substitutes p₁ = 6 kg m s⁻¹, p₂ = 18 kg m s⁻¹, and m = 3 kg.
Obtains W = 48.0 J.

items.stem: In a laboratory motion trial, a linear-motor camera dolly travels on a studio optical bench with northward taken as positive. The velocity–time graph records its motion from t = 0.0 s to t = 16.0 s, including uniform reversal thrust from t = 8.0 s to t = 12.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Zero-velocity crossing is at t = 11 s. Positive area = 90.0 m and unsigned negative area = 18.0 m, giving total distance = 108 m. (b) Net displacement = 90.0 − 18.0 = 72.0 m; average velocity = 72.0 / 16 = 4.50 m s⁻¹. (c) Acceleration = (−4 − 12) / (12 − 8) = -4.00 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Finds zero-crossing t = 11 s and evaluates both unsigned areas (90.0 m and 18.0 m).
Obtains total distance = 108 m.
Subtracts areas for net displacement (72.0 m) and divides by 16 s.
Obtains average velocity = 4.50 m s⁻¹.
Obtains acceleration = -4.00 m s⁻² including negative sign.

items.stem: An inertial sensor logs the acceleration of a linear-motor brake-test bogie over a 20.0 s interval (along the track positive). At t = 0.0 s its velocity is 17.0 m s⁻¹ along the track.
items.workedSolution: (a) Maximum speed occurs when acceleration crosses zero from positive to negative at t = 10.0 s. (b) Positive area = 48.0 m s⁻¹, giving v_max = 17 + 48.0 = 65.0 m s⁻¹. (c) Negative area magnitude = 15.0 m s⁻¹, so v_final = 65.0 − 15.0 = 50.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: States t = 10.0 s.
Evaluates positive area up to 10 s (48.0 m s⁻¹) and adds u₀ = 17 m s⁻¹.
Obtains v_max = 65.0 m s⁻¹.
Subtracts negative area (15.0 m s⁻¹) from v_max.
Obtains final velocity = 50.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates positive (54.0 J) and negative (−4.00 J) areas.
Obtains net work W = 50.0 J.
Uses ½mv² = ½(1.6)(4.5²) + W.
Obtains v = 9.10 m s⁻¹.
Divides net work by 8 m to get 6.25 N.

workingSteps: Positive area (0 to 6 m) = ½(6 + 3)(12) = 54.0 J; negative area (6 m to 8 m) = −½(2)(4) = −4.00 J.

parts.prompt: Calculate its speed at x = 8.0 m.
State the mean resultant force over the 8.0 m displacement.

items.stem: Terminal voltage V across a hydrogen proton-exchange fuel cell is logged as load current I varies from zero up to 5.0 A, producing the downward straight line below.
items.workedSolution: (a) Open-circuit intercept gives ε = 16.0 V. (b) Gradient = (7 − 16) / 5 = -1.80 V A⁻¹. (c) Mean terminal p.d. = ½(16 + 7) = 11.5 V.

markScheme.criterion: Reads ε = 16.0 V at I = 0.
Evaluates (7 − 16) / 5 including negative sign.
Obtains -1.80 V A⁻¹.
Uses ½(16 + 7) or area divided by 5 A.
Obtains 11.5 V.

items.stem: Telemetry for a linear-induction baggage carrier begins at t = 0.0 s when it is stationary 50.0 m beyond the sorting-hall origin sensor. Its velocity–time profile over the 15.0 s run is plotted, with braking starting at t = 9.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Trapezium area Δx = ½(15 + 6)(22) = 231 m. (b) Final distance from datum = 50 + 231 = 281 m. (c) Mean speed = 231 / 15 = 15.4 m s⁻¹. (d) Braking acceleration = (0 − 22) / (15 − 9) = -3.67 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Identifies distance travelled as the area under the v–t trapezium.
Obtains Δx = 231 m.
Adds 50 m offset to obtain 281 m.
Divides distance travelled from (a) by 15 s.
Obtains mean speed = 15.4 m s⁻¹.
Obtains braking acceleration = -3.67 m s⁻².

items.stem: Along a horizontal guideway, a frictionless puck on an air table of mass 0.8 kg moves in a fixed direction. Its momentum–time graph shows an impulse stage from t = 1.0 s to t = 5.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Resultant force F = Δp / Δt = (7.2 − 1.6) / (5 − 1) = 1.40 N. (b) Net work W = ΔE_k = (7.2² − 1.6²) / (2 × 0.8) = 30.8 J.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies resultant force as gradient Δp / Δt of the p–t graph.
Obtains F = 1.40 N.
Relates net work to ΔE_k = (p₂² − p₁²) / (2m).
Substitutes p₁ = 1.6 kg m s⁻¹, p₂ = 7.2 kg m s⁻¹, and m = 0.8 kg.
Obtains W = 30.8 J.

items.stem: A force transducer logs a 2.5 s solenoid kicker stroke acting forward on a robotic soccer puck (mass 3.0 kg), which had momentum 9.0 kg m s⁻¹ at t = 0.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Impulse J = ½(2.5 + 1.5)(46) = 92.0 N s. (b) Final momentum p_f = 9 + 92.0 = 101 kg m s⁻¹. (c) Speed increase Δv = 92.0 / 3 = 30.7 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Computes impulse from the trapezium area under the F–t curve.
Obtains J = 92.0 N s.
Adds 9 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 101 kg m s⁻¹.
Divides impulse from (a) by 3 kg.
Obtains Δv = 30.7 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: During an electrical power-source practical, a lithium-iron-phosphate storage cell is discharged through a stepped load up to 2.0 A, yielding the V–I graph shown.
items.workedSolution: (a) Open-circuit intercept gives ε = 10.6 V. (b) Gradient = (5 − 10.6) / 2 = -2.80 V A⁻¹. (c) Mean terminal p.d. = ½(10.6 + 5) = 7.80 V.

markScheme.criterion: Reads ε = 10.6 V at I = 0.
Evaluates (5 − 10.6) / 2 including negative sign.
Obtains -2.80 V A⁻¹.
Uses ½(10.6 + 5) or area divided by 2 A.

items.workedSolution: (a) At r⁻² = 0, systematic tare offset F₀ = 0.100 N. (b) Gradient = (1.3 − 0.1) / 50 = 0.0240 N m².
