items.stem: In a laboratory motion trial, an autonomous harbour mooring buggy travels along a straight quay rail with southward taken as positive. The velocity–time graph records its motion from t = 0.0 s to t = 20.0 s, including uniform reversal thrust from t = 10.0 s to t = 15.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Zero-velocity crossing is at t = 13 s. Positive area = 228 m and unsigned negative area = 96.0 m, giving total distance = 324 m. (b) Net displacement = 228 − 96.0 = 132 m; average velocity = 132 / 20 = 6.60 m s⁻¹. (c) Acceleration = (−16 − 24) / (15 − 10) = -8.00 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Finds zero-crossing t = 13 s and evaluates both unsigned areas (228 m and 96.0 m).
Obtains total distance = 324 m.
Subtracts areas for net displacement (132 m) and divides by 20 s.
Obtains average velocity = 6.60 m s⁻¹.
Obtains acceleration = -8.00 m s⁻² including negative sign.

items.stem: During a 10.0 s test run, a high-rise express lift enters the instrumented section moving upward at 10.0 m s⁻¹. Its subsequent signed acceleration–time trace is shown.
items.workedSolution: (a) Maximum speed occurs when acceleration crosses zero from positive to negative at t = 6.00 s. (b) Positive area = 18.0 m s⁻¹, giving v_max = 10 + 18.0 = 28.0 m s⁻¹. (c) Negative area magnitude = 9.00 m s⁻¹, so v_final = 28.0 − 9.00 = 19.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: States t = 6.00 s.
Evaluates positive area up to 6 s (18.0 m s⁻¹) and adds u₀ = 10 m s⁻¹.
Obtains v_max = 28.0 m s⁻¹.
Subtracts negative area (9.00 m s⁻¹) from v_max.
Obtains final velocity = 19.0 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: The plotted tensile stress–strain profile for a thermoplastic elastomer tether exhibits a distinct gradient change at the limit of proportionality (strain 0.4) before reaching strain 0.8.
items.workedSolution: (a) Young's modulus E = 170 / 0.4 = 425 MPa. (b) Energy per unit volume = ½(0.4)(170) + ½(170 + 240)(0.4) = 116 MJ m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates initial gradient σ / ε up to ε = 0.4.
Obtains E = 425 MPa.
Identifies work per unit volume as total area under the σ–ε graph.
Splits area into initial triangle plus upper trapezium.
Obtains 116 MJ m⁻³.

parts.prompt: Determine the Young's modulus of the specimen over the proportional region (0.0 to 0.4).
Calculate the work done per unit volume in stretching the specimen from zero strain to 0.8.
workingSteps: Area from 0 to 0.4 = ½(0.4)(170) = 34.0 MJ m⁻³.
Area from 0.4 to 0.8 = ½(170 + 240)(0.4) = 82.0 MJ m⁻³; total = 116 MJ m⁻³.

items.stem: Because clamping electrodes introduce a fixed series resistance R₀, a researcher plots R against L / A up to 500.0 m⁻¹ for a conductive silicone sensor strip.
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical intercept R₀ = 7.00 Ω. (b) Resistivity ρ = (36 − 7) / 500 = 0.0580 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: States R₀ = 7.00 Ω.
Identifies ρ with the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A).
Subtracts R₀ = 7 Ω from 36 Ω before dividing by 500 m⁻¹.
Obtains ρ = 0.0580 Ω m.

items.stem: Data loggers record the linear momentum of a superconducting levitation carrier (mass 1.2 kg), which experiences a constant resultant force between t = 2.0 s and t = 5.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Resultant force F = Δp / Δt = (9.6 − 2.4) / (5 − 2) = 2.40 N. (b) Net work W = ΔE_k = (9.6² − 2.4²) / (2 × 1.2) = 36.0 J.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies resultant force as gradient Δp / Δt of the p–t graph.
Obtains F = 2.40 N.
Relates net work to ΔE_k = (p₂² − p₁²) / (2m).
Substitutes p₁ = 2.4 kg m s⁻¹, p₂ = 9.6 kg m s⁻¹, and m = 1.2 kg.
Obtains W = 36.0 J.

items.stem: The graph displays how the velocity of a seismic actuator test sled on a low-friction hydraulic guide varies with time over 20.0 s. Positive velocity corresponds to motion in the positive x-direction, and direction reversal occurs during the linear ramp between t = 10.0 s and t = 15.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Zero-velocity crossing is at t = 13.75 s. Positive area = 281 m and unsigned negative area = 56.3 m, giving total distance = 338 m. (b) Net displacement = 281 − 56.3 = 225 m; average velocity = 225 / 20 = 11.3 m s⁻¹. (c) Acceleration = (−10 − 30) / (15 − 10) = -8.00 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Finds zero-crossing t = 13.75 s and evaluates both unsigned areas (281 m and 56.3 m).
Obtains total distance = 338 m.
Subtracts areas for net displacement (225 m) and divides by 20 s.
Obtains average velocity = 11.3 m s⁻¹.
Obtains acceleration = -8.00 m s⁻² including negative sign.

items.stem: Engineers monitor a maglev propulsion test pod for 12.0 s starting from an initial eastward velocity of 12.0 m s⁻¹ at t = 0.0 s, obtaining the piecewise acceleration–time graph below.
items.workedSolution: (a) Maximum speed occurs when acceleration crosses zero from positive to negative at t = 6.00 s. (b) Positive area = 25.0 m s⁻¹, giving v_max = 12 + 25.0 = 37.0 m s⁻¹. (c) Negative area magnitude = 9.00 m s⁻¹, so v_final = 37.0 − 9.00 = 28.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: States t = 6.00 s.

Obtains v_max = 37.0 m s⁻¹.
Subtracts negative area (9.00 m s⁻¹) from v_max.
Obtains final velocity = 28.0 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Calibrated meters measure terminal potential difference V versus current I up to 5.0 A for a rechargeable nickel-cadmium pack, as plotted on the axes.
items.workedSolution: (a) Open-circuit intercept gives ε = 25.0 V. (b) Gradient = (10 − 25) / 5 = -3.00 V A⁻¹. (c) Mean terminal p.d. = ½(25 + 10) = 17.5 V.

markScheme.criterion: Reads ε = 25.0 V at I = 0.
Evaluates (10 − 25) / 5 including negative sign.
Obtains -3.00 V A⁻¹.
Uses ½(25 + 10) or area divided by 5 A.
Obtains 17.5 V.

workingSteps: As r → ∞, r⁻² → 0, where the vertical intercept gives F₀ = 0.200 N.

parts.prompt: Calculate the gradient k|Q₁Q₂| of the linearized plot over 0.0 m⁻² to 80.0 m⁻².
workingSteps: Read F = 2.2 N at r⁻² = 80 m⁻².

items.stem: At t = 0.0 s, a high-speed bottling-line transfer sled rests at a position 25.0 m ahead of a optical home flag. The velocity–time graph shows its forward motion over 10.0 s, with uniform braking applied from t = 7.0 s until t = 10.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Trapezium area Δx = ½(10 + 5)(16) = 120 m. (b) Final distance from datum = 25 + 120 = 145 m. (c) Mean speed = 120 / 10 = 12.0 m s⁻¹. (d) Braking acceleration = (0 − 16) / (10 − 7) = -5.33 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Identifies distance travelled as the area under the v–t trapezium.
Obtains Δx = 120 m.
Adds 25 m offset to obtain 145 m.
Divides distance travelled from (a) by 10 s.
Obtains mean speed = 12.0 m s⁻¹.
Obtains braking acceleration = -5.33 m s⁻².

items.stem: Along a horizontal guideway, an ice-rink calibration sled of mass 1.0 kg moves in a fixed direction. Its momentum–time graph shows an impulse stage from t = 2.0 s to t = 6.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Resultant force F = Δp / Δt = (9 − 3) / (6 − 2) = 1.50 N. (b) Net work W = ΔE_k = (9² − 3²) / (2 × 1) = 36.0 J.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies resultant force as gradient Δp / Δt of the p–t graph.
Obtains F = 1.50 N.
Relates net work to ΔE_k = (p₂² − p₁²) / (2m).
Substitutes p₁ = 3 kg m s⁻¹, p₂ = 9 kg m s⁻¹, and m = 1 kg.
Obtains W = 36.0 J.

items.stem: Travelling in a straight line with initial momentum 10.0 kg m s⁻¹, a microgravity cargo pod of mass 2.5 kg is acted upon by a collinear docking vernier firing for 1.0 s, as shown on the force–time graph.
items.workedSolution: (a) Impulse J = ½(1 + 0.6)(60) = 48.0 N s. (b) Final momentum p_f = 10 + 48.0 = 58.0 kg m s⁻¹. (c) Speed increase Δv = 48.0 / 2.5 = 19.2 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Computes impulse from the trapezium area under the F–t curve.
Obtains J = 48.0 N s.
Adds 10 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 58.0 kg m s⁻¹.
Divides impulse from (a) by 2.5 kg.
Obtains Δv = 19.2 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: To determine the EMF and internal resistance of a thermoelectric Seebeck generator, V is graphed against I over the current interval 0.0 A to 4.0 A.
items.workedSolution: (a) Open-circuit intercept gives ε = 13.0 V. (b) Gradient = (7 − 13) / 4 = -1.50 V A⁻¹. (c) Mean terminal p.d. = ½(13 + 7) = 10.0 V.

markScheme.criterion: Reads ε = 13.0 V at I = 0.
Evaluates (7 − 13) / 4 including negative sign.
Obtains -1.50 V A⁻¹.
Uses ½(13 + 7) or area divided by 4 A.
Obtains 10.0 V.

items.stem: Passing a timing marker at t = 0.0 s with speed 16.0 m s⁻¹ forward, an aerotow winch launch carriage undergoes positive then negative forward acceleration over 12.0 s as plotted.
items.workedSolution: (a) Maximum speed occurs when acceleration crosses zero from positive to negative at t = 8.00 s. (b) Positive area = 24.0 m s⁻¹, giving v_max = 16 + 24.0 = 40.0 m s⁻¹. (c) Negative area magnitude = 15.0 m s⁻¹, so v_final = 40.0 − 15.0 = 25.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: States t = 8.00 s.
Evaluates positive area up to 8 s (24.0 m s⁻¹) and adds u₀ = 16 m s⁻¹.
Obtains v_max = 40.0 m s⁻¹.
Subtracts negative area (15.0 m s⁻¹) from v_max.
Obtains final velocity = 25.0 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: At x = 0.0 m, an instrumented crash-test carriage of mass 2.5 kg moves in the positive x-direction at 6.0 m s⁻¹. The graph shows the resultant force acting along its line of motion from x = 0.0 m to x = 10.0 m.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates positive (82.5 J) and negative (−5.00 J) areas.
Obtains net work W = 77.5 J.
Uses ½mv² = ½(2.5)(6²) + W.

items.stem: Engineers test a cross-linked elastomer strip under axial tension up to strain 0.5, recording an initial linear elastic regime between zero strain and 0.25.
items.workedSolution: (a) Young's modulus E = 180 / 0.25 = 720 MPa. (b) Energy per unit volume = ½(0.25)(180) + ½(180 + 260)(0.25) = 77.5 MJ m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates initial gradient σ / ε up to ε = 0.25.
Obtains E = 720 MPa.
Identifies work per unit volume as total area under the σ–ε graph.
Splits area into initial triangle plus upper trapezium.
Obtains 77.5 MJ m⁻³.

items.stem: Data loggers record the linear momentum of a frictionless puck on an air table (mass 3.0 kg), which experiences a constant resultant force between t = 2.0 s and t = 6.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Resultant force F = Δp / Δt = (18 − 6) / (6 − 2) = 3.00 N. (b) Net work W = ΔE_k = (18² − 6²) / (2 × 3) = 48.0 J.

Obtains W = 48.0 J.

items.stem: The signed upward acceleration of a deep-sea winch capsule is plotted from t = 0.0 s to t = 15.0 s; at the start of the recording, its velocity is 15.0 m s⁻¹ upward.
items.workedSolution: (a) Maximum speed occurs when acceleration crosses zero from positive to negative at t = 8.00 s. (b) Positive area = 52.0 m s⁻¹, giving v_max = 15 + 52.0 = 67.0 m s⁻¹. (c) Negative area magnitude = 24.0 m s⁻¹, so v_final = 67.0 − 24.0 = 43.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: States t = 8.00 s.
Evaluates positive area up to 8 s (52.0 m s⁻¹) and adds u₀ = 15 m s⁻¹.
Obtains v_max = 67.0 m s⁻¹.
Subtracts negative area (24.0 m s⁻¹) from v_max.
Obtains final velocity = 43.0 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Force-transducer and encoder data for a magnetic-launch coaster bogie (mass 1.6 kg, speed 4.5 m s⁻¹ at x = 0.0 m) are plotted over a 8.0 m straight track.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates positive (54.0 J) and negative (−4.00 J) areas.
Obtains net work W = 50.0 J.
Uses ½mv² = ½(1.6)(4.5²) + W.
Obtains v = 9.10 m s⁻¹.
Divides net work by 8 m to get 6.25 N.

workingSteps: Positive area (0 to 6 m) = ½(6 + 3)(12) = 54.0 J; negative area (6 m to 8 m) = −½(2)(4) = −4.00 J.

parts.prompt: Calculate its speed at x = 8.0 m.
State the mean resultant force over the 8.0 m displacement.

items.stem: The straight-line plot below shows how the terminal potential difference of an alkaline lantern battery falls as load current increases from 0.0 A to 5.0 A.
items.workedSolution: (a) Open-circuit intercept gives ε = 16.0 V. (b) Gradient = (7 − 16) / 5 = -1.80 V A⁻¹. (c) Mean terminal p.d. = ½(16 + 7) = 11.5 V.

markScheme.criterion: Reads ε = 16.0 V at I = 0.
Evaluates (7 − 16) / 5 including negative sign.
Obtains -1.80 V A⁻¹.
Uses ½(16 + 7) or area divided by 5 A.
Obtains 11.5 V.

items.stem: Refer to the linearized Coulomb graph of balance reading F against r⁻² (up to 80.0 m⁻²) recorded using precision electrostatic spheres on a sapphire-pivot balance.
items.workedSolution: (a) At r⁻² = 0, systematic tare offset F₀ = 0.400 N. (b) Gradient = (2.4 − 0.4) / 80 = 0.0250 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Reads intercept F₀ = 0.400 N.
Evaluates ΔF = 2.4 − 0.4 using intercept from (a).
Divides ΔF by 80 m⁻² and states correct unit N m².
Obtains 0.0250 N m².

items.stem: Telemetry for a solar-powered desert research rover begins at t = 0.0 s when it is stationary 50.0 m beyond the base-camp beacon. Its velocity–time profile over the 15.0 s run is plotted, with braking starting at t = 9.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Trapezium area Δx = ½(15 + 6)(22) = 231 m. (b) Final distance from datum = 50 + 231 = 281 m. (c) Mean speed = 231 / 15 = 15.4 m s⁻¹. (d) Braking acceleration = (0 − 22) / (15 − 9) = -3.67 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Identifies distance travelled as the area under the v–t trapezium.
Obtains Δx = 231 m.
Adds 50 m offset to obtain 281 m.
Divides distance travelled from (a) by 15 s.
Obtains mean speed = 15.4 m s⁻¹.
Obtains braking acceleration = -3.67 m s⁻².

items.stem: Along a horizontal guideway, a satellite attitude-test mass of mass 0.8 kg moves in a fixed direction. Its momentum–time graph shows an impulse stage from t = 1.0 s to t = 5.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Resultant force F = Δp / Δt = (7.2 − 1.6) / (5 − 1) = 1.40 N. (b) Net work W = ΔE_k = (7.2² − 1.6²) / (2 × 0.8) = 30.8 J.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies resultant force as gradient Δp / Δt of the p–t graph.
Obtains F = 1.40 N.
Relates net work to ΔE_k = (p₂² − p₁²) / (2m).
Substitutes p₁ = 1.6 kg m s⁻¹, p₂ = 7.2 kg m s⁻¹, and m = 0.8 kg.
Obtains W = 30.8 J.

items.stem: To determine the resistivity ρ of a polypyrrole conductive polymer film despite probe and lead resistance R₀, a student plots total measured resistance R against the ratio L / A from 0.0 m⁻¹ to 400.0 m⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical intercept R₀ = 8.00 Ω. (b) Resistivity ρ = (36 − 8) / 400 = 0.0700 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: States R₀ = 8.00 Ω.
Identifies ρ with the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A).
Subtracts R₀ = 8 Ω from 36 Ω before dividing by 400 m⁻¹.
Obtains ρ = 0.0700 Ω m.

items.stem: A force transducer logs a 2.5 s pulsed ion-beam firing acting forward on a Hall-effect thruster test rig (mass 3.0 kg), which had momentum 9.0 kg m s⁻¹ at t = 0.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Impulse J = ½(2.5 + 1.5)(46) = 92.0 N s. (b) Final momentum p_f = 9 + 92.0 = 101 kg m s⁻¹. (c) Speed increase Δv = 92.0 / 3 = 30.7 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Computes impulse from the trapezium area under the F–t curve.
Obtains J = 92.0 N s.
Adds 9 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 101 kg m s⁻¹.
Divides impulse from (a) by 3 kg.
Obtains Δv = 30.7 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: In an experiment to characterize a nickel-metal-hydride battery pack, a variable resistor is adjusted while recording terminal potential difference V and current I from 0.0 A to 2.0 A. The resulting best-fit line is shown.
items.workedSolution: (a) Open-circuit intercept gives ε = 10.6 V. (b) Gradient = (5 − 10.6) / 2 = -2.80 V A⁻¹. (c) Mean terminal p.d. = ½(10.6 + 5) = 7.80 V.

markScheme.criterion: Reads ε = 10.6 V at I = 0.
Evaluates (5 − 10.6) / 2 including negative sign.
Obtains -2.80 V A⁻¹.
Uses ½(10.6 + 5) or area divided by 2 A.
Obtains 7.80 V.

items.workedSolution: (a) At r⁻² = 0, systematic tare offset F₀ = 0.100 N. (b) Gradient = (1.1 − 0.1) / 20 = 0.0500 N m².

Evaluates ΔF = 1.1 − 0.1 using intercept from (a).
Divides ΔF by 20 m⁻² and states correct unit N m².
Obtains 0.0500 N m².

items.stem: A 20.0 s accelerometer log is shown for a linear-motor brake-test bogie, which is already travelling along the track at 17.0 m s⁻¹ when t = 0.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Maximum speed occurs when acceleration crosses zero from positive to negative at t = 10.0 s. (b) Positive area = 48.0 m s⁻¹, giving v_max = 17 + 48.0 = 65.0 m s⁻¹. (c) Negative area magnitude = 15.0 m s⁻¹, so v_final = 65.0 − 15.0 = 50.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: States t = 10.0 s.
Evaluates positive area up to 10 s (48.0 m s⁻¹) and adds u₀ = 17 m s⁻¹.
Obtains v_max = 65.0 m s⁻¹.
Subtracts negative area (15.0 m s⁻¹) from v_max.
Obtains final velocity = 50.0 m s⁻¹.

parts.prompt: Calculate the net work done on the 4.0 kg object between x = 0.0 m and x = 10.0 m.
workingSteps: Positive area (0 to 8 m) = ½(8 + 4)(24) = 144 J; negative area (8 m to 10 m) = −½(2)(8) = −8.00 J.

parts.prompt: Calculate its speed at x = 10.0 m.
State the mean resultant force over the 10.0 m displacement.

items.stem: A tensile testing machine stretches an extruded fluoropolymer ribbon up to a strain of 0.8, producing the stress–strain curve shown. The limit of proportionality occurs at strain 0.4.
items.workedSolution: (a) Young's modulus E = 170 / 0.4 = 425 MPa. (b) Energy per unit volume = ½(0.4)(170) + ½(170 + 240)(0.4) = 116 MJ m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates initial gradient σ / ε up to ε = 0.4.
Obtains E = 425 MPa.
Identifies work per unit volume as total area under the σ–ε graph.
Splits area into initial triangle plus upper trapezium.
Obtains 116 MJ m⁻³.

parts.prompt: Determine the Young's modulus of the specimen over the proportional region (0.0 to 0.4).
Calculate the work done per unit volume in stretching the specimen from zero strain to 0.8.
workingSteps: Area from 0 to 0.4 = ½(0.4)(170) = 34.0 MJ m⁻³.
Area from 0.4 to 0.8 = ½(170 + 240)(0.4) = 82.0 MJ m⁻³; total = 116 MJ m⁻³.

items.stem: Measured resistance R is plotted against length-to-area ratio L / A up to 160.0 m⁻¹ for a germanium crystal prism, obeying R = ρ(L / A) + R₀ where R₀ is the constant lead resistance.
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical intercept R₀ = 6.00 Ω. (b) Resistivity ρ = (26 − 6) / 160 = 0.125 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: States R₀ = 6.00 Ω.
Identifies ρ with the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A).
Subtracts R₀ = 6 Ω from 26 Ω before dividing by 160 m⁻¹.
Obtains ρ = 0.125 Ω m.

items.stem: Data loggers record the linear momentum of an ice-rink calibration sled (mass 1.2 kg), which experiences a constant resultant force between t = 2.0 s and t = 5.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Resultant force F = Δp / Δt = (9.6 − 2.4) / (5 − 2) = 2.40 N. (b) Net work W = ΔE_k = (9.6² − 2.4²) / (2 × 1.2) = 36.0 J.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies resultant force as gradient Δp / Δt of the p–t graph.
Obtains F = 2.40 N.
Relates net work to ΔE_k = (p₂² − p₁²) / (2m).
Substitutes p₁ = 2.4 kg m s⁻¹, p₂ = 9.6 kg m s⁻¹, and m = 1.2 kg.
Obtains W = 36.0 J.

items.workedSolution: (a) Maximum speed occurs when acceleration crosses zero from positive to negative at t = 4.00 s. (b) Positive area = 18.0 m s⁻¹, giving v_max = 9 + 18.0 = 27.0 m s⁻¹. (c) Negative area magnitude = 12.0 m s⁻¹, so v_final = 27.0 − 12.0 = 15.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: States t = 4.00 s.
Evaluates positive area up to 4 s (18.0 m s⁻¹) and adds u₀ = 9 m s⁻¹.
Obtains v_max = 27.0 m s⁻¹.
Subtracts negative area (12.0 m s⁻¹) from v_max.
Obtains final velocity = 15.0 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: A student connects an ammeter, high-impedance voltmeter, and rheostat to a lithium-iron-phosphate storage cell, obtaining the linear V–I plot over 0.0 A to 5.0 A.
items.workedSolution: (a) Open-circuit intercept gives ε = 25.0 V. (b) Gradient = (10 − 25) / 5 = -3.00 V A⁻¹. (c) Mean terminal p.d. = ½(25 + 10) = 17.5 V.

markScheme.criterion: Reads ε = 25.0 V at I = 0.
Evaluates (10 − 25) / 5 including negative sign.
Obtains -3.00 V A⁻¹.
Uses ½(25 + 10) or area divided by 5 A.
Obtains 17.5 V.

items.stem: At t = 0.0 s, an inter-terminal airport monorail rests at a position 25.0 m ahead of a concourse datum post. The velocity–time graph shows its forward motion over 10.0 s, with uniform braking applied from t = 7.0 s until t = 10.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Trapezium area Δx = ½(10 + 5)(16) = 120 m. (b) Final distance from datum = 25 + 120 = 145 m. (c) Mean speed = 120 / 10 = 12.0 m s⁻¹. (d) Braking acceleration = (0 − 16) / (10 − 7) = -5.33 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Identifies distance travelled as the area under the v–t trapezium.
Obtains Δx = 120 m.
Adds 25 m offset to obtain 145 m.
Divides distance travelled from (a) by 10 s.
Obtains mean speed = 12.0 m s⁻¹.
Obtains braking acceleration = -5.33 m s⁻².

items.stem: Along a horizontal guideway, an air-track glider of mass 1.0 kg moves in a fixed direction. Its momentum–time graph shows an impulse stage from t = 2.0 s to t = 6.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Resultant force F = Δp / Δt = (9 − 3) / (6 − 2) = 1.50 N. (b) Net work W = ΔE_k = (9² − 3²) / (2 × 1) = 36.0 J.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies resultant force as gradient Δp / Δt of the p–t graph.
Obtains F = 1.50 N.
Relates net work to ΔE_k = (p₂² − p₁²) / (2m).
Substitutes p₁ = 3 kg m s⁻¹, p₂ = 9 kg m s⁻¹, and m = 1 kg.
Obtains W = 36.0 J.

items.stem: In an electrical properties lab, resistance readings across a conductive silicone sensor strip are linearized against geometric factor L / A up to 500.0 m⁻¹, revealing a non-zero contact offset R₀.
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical intercept R₀ = 7.00 Ω. (b) Resistivity ρ = (36 − 7) / 500 = 0.0580 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: States R₀ = 7.00 Ω.
Identifies ρ with the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A).
Subtracts R₀ = 7 Ω from 36 Ω before dividing by 500 m⁻¹.
Obtains ρ = 0.0580 Ω m.

items.stem: Terminal voltage V across a zinc-carbon dry cell is logged as load current I varies from zero up to 4.0 A, producing the downward straight line below.
items.workedSolution: (a) Open-circuit intercept gives ε = 13.0 V. (b) Gradient = (7 − 13) / 4 = -1.50 V A⁻¹. (c) Mean terminal p.d. = ½(13 + 7) = 10.0 V.

markScheme.criterion: Reads ε = 13.0 V at I = 0.
Evaluates (7 − 13) / 4 including negative sign.
Obtains -1.50 V A⁻¹.
Uses ½(13 + 7) or area divided by 4 A.
Obtains 10.0 V.

items.stem: At t = 0.0 s, a maglev propulsion test pod moves eastward with an initial velocity of 12.0 m s⁻¹. The graph shows how its acceleration varies with time over 12.0 s (eastward positive).
items.workedSolution: (a) Maximum speed occurs when acceleration crosses zero from positive to negative at t = 6.00 s. (b) Positive area = 25.0 m s⁻¹, giving v_max = 12 + 25.0 = 37.0 m s⁻¹. (c) Negative area magnitude = 9.00 m s⁻¹, so v_final = 37.0 − 9.00 = 28.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: States t = 6.00 s.
Evaluates positive area up to 6 s (25.0 m s⁻¹) and adds u₀ = 12 m s⁻¹.
Obtains v_max = 37.0 m s⁻¹.
Subtracts negative area (9.00 m s⁻¹) from v_max.
Obtains final velocity = 28.0 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: At x = 0.0 m, a magnetic-launch coaster bogie of mass 2.5 kg moves in the positive x-direction at 6.0 m s⁻¹. The graph shows the resultant force acting along its line of motion from x = 0.0 m to x = 10.0 m.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates positive (82.5 J) and negative (−5.00 J) areas.
Obtains net work W = 77.5 J.
Uses ½mv² = ½(2.5)(6²) + W.
Obtains v = 9.90 m s⁻¹.
Divides net work by 10 m to get 7.75 N.

items.stem: Stress–strain data for a drawn nylon monofilament are plotted up to strain 0.5, showing an initial Hookean region from 0.0 to strain 0.25 followed by reduced stiffness.
items.workedSolution: (a) Young's modulus E = 180 / 0.25 = 720 MPa. (b) Energy per unit volume = ½(0.25)(180) + ½(180 + 260)(0.25) = 77.5 MJ m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates initial gradient σ / ε up to ε = 0.25.
Obtains E = 720 MPa.
Identifies work per unit volume as total area under the σ–ε graph.
Splits area into initial triangle plus upper trapezium.
Obtains 77.5 MJ m⁻³.

items.stem: Data loggers record the linear momentum of a satellite attitude-test mass (mass 3.0 kg), which experiences a constant resultant force between t = 2.0 s and t = 6.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Resultant force F = Δp / Δt = (18 − 6) / (6 − 2) = 3.00 N. (b) Net work W = ΔE_k = (18² − 6²) / (2 × 3) = 48.0 J.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies resultant force as gradient Δp / Δt of the p–t graph.
Obtains F = 3.00 N.
Relates net work to ΔE_k = (p₂² − p₁²) / (2m).
Substitutes p₁ = 6 kg m s⁻¹, p₂ = 18 kg m s⁻¹, and m = 3 kg.
Obtains W = 48.0 J.

items.stem: An inertial sensor logs the acceleration of a centrifuge carrier pod over a 10.0 s interval (tangentially forward positive). At t = 0.0 s its velocity is 13.0 m s⁻¹ tangentially forward.
items.workedSolution: (a) Maximum speed occurs when acceleration crosses zero from positive to negative at t = 5.00 s. (b) Positive area = 24.0 m s⁻¹, giving v_max = 13 + 24.0 = 37.0 m s⁻¹. (c) Negative area magnitude = 14.0 m s⁻¹, so v_final = 37.0 − 14.0 = 23.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: States t = 5.00 s.
Evaluates positive area up to 5 s (24.0 m s⁻¹) and adds u₀ = 13 m s⁻¹.
Obtains v_max = 37.0 m s⁻¹.
Subtracts negative area (14.0 m s⁻¹) from v_max.
Obtains final velocity = 23.0 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: During an electrical power-source practical, a thermoelectric Seebeck generator is discharged through a stepped load up to 5.0 A, yielding the V–I graph shown.
items.workedSolution: (a) Open-circuit intercept gives ε = 16.0 V. (b) Gradient = (7 − 16) / 5 = -1.80 V A⁻¹. (c) Mean terminal p.d. = ½(16 + 7) = 11.5 V.

markScheme.criterion: Reads ε = 16.0 V at I = 0.
Evaluates (7 − 16) / 5 including negative sign.
Obtains -1.80 V A⁻¹.
Uses ½(16 + 7) or area divided by 5 A.
Obtains 11.5 V.

items.stem: Telemetry for an underground mine haulage skip begins at t = 0.0 s when it is stationary 50.0 m beyond the shaft loading datum. Its velocity–time profile over the 15.0 s run is plotted, with braking starting at t = 9.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Trapezium area Δx = ½(15 + 6)(22) = 231 m. (b) Final distance from datum = 50 + 231 = 281 m. (c) Mean speed = 231 / 15 = 15.4 m s⁻¹. (d) Braking acceleration = (0 − 22) / (15 − 9) = -3.67 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Identifies distance travelled as the area under the v–t trapezium.
Obtains Δx = 231 m.
Adds 50 m offset to obtain 281 m.
Divides distance travelled from (a) by 15 s.
Obtains mean speed = 15.4 m s⁻¹.
Obtains braking acceleration = -3.67 m s⁻².

items.stem: Along a horizontal guideway, a low-friction dynamics trolley of mass 0.8 kg moves in a fixed direction. Its momentum–time graph shows an impulse stage from t = 1.0 s to t = 5.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Resultant force F = Δp / Δt = (7.2 − 1.6) / (5 − 1) = 1.40 N. (b) Net work W = ΔE_k = (7.2² − 1.6²) / (2 × 0.8) = 30.8 J.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies resultant force as gradient Δp / Δt of the p–t graph.
Obtains F = 1.40 N.
Relates net work to ΔE_k = (p₂² − p₁²) / (2m).
Substitutes p₁ = 1.6 kg m s⁻¹, p₂ = 7.2 kg m s⁻¹, and m = 0.8 kg.
Obtains W = 30.8 J.

items.stem: Because clamping electrodes introduce a fixed series resistance R₀, a researcher plots R against L / A up to 200.0 m⁻¹ for a potassium-chloride electrolyte tube.
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical intercept R₀ = 6.00 Ω. (b) Resistivity ρ = (34 − 6) / 200 = 0.140 Ω m.

Subtracts R₀ = 6 Ω from 34 Ω before dividing by 200 m⁻¹.
Obtains ρ = 0.140 Ω m.

items.stem: Calibrated meters measure terminal potential difference V versus current I up to 2.0 A for a portable photovoltaic module under constant irradiance, as plotted on the axes.
items.workedSolution: (a) Open-circuit intercept gives ε = 10.6 V. (b) Gradient = (5 − 10.6) / 2 = -2.80 V A⁻¹. (c) Mean terminal p.d. = ½(10.6 + 5) = 7.80 V.

markScheme.criterion: Reads ε = 10.6 V at I = 0.
Evaluates (5 − 10.6) / 2 including negative sign.
Obtains -2.80 V A⁻¹.
Uses ½(10.6 + 5) or area divided by 2 A.
Obtains 7.80 V.

items.stem: Repulsive force data between isolated brass domes mounted above an electronic microbalance are transformed to F against r⁻² up to 40.0 m⁻², revealing a constant tare intercept.
items.workedSolution: (a) At r⁻² = 0, systematic tare offset F₀ = 0.200 N. (b) Gradient = (1.6 − 0.2) / 40 = 0.0350 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Reads intercept F₀ = 0.200 N.
Evaluates ΔF = 1.6 − 0.2 using intercept from (a).
Divides ΔF by 40 m⁻² and states correct unit N m².
Obtains 0.0350 N m².

items.stem: During a 15.0 s test run, a deep-sea winch capsule enters the instrumented section moving upward at 15.0 m s⁻¹. Its subsequent signed acceleration–time trace is shown.
items.workedSolution: (a) Maximum speed occurs when acceleration crosses zero from positive to negative at t = 8.00 s. (b) Positive area = 52.0 m s⁻¹, giving v_max = 15 + 52.0 = 67.0 m s⁻¹. (c) Negative area magnitude = 24.0 m s⁻¹, so v_final = 67.0 − 24.0 = 43.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: States t = 8.00 s.
Evaluates positive area up to 8 s (52.0 m s⁻¹) and adds u₀ = 15 m s⁻¹.
Obtains v_max = 67.0 m s⁻¹.
Subtracts negative area (24.0 m s⁻¹) from v_max.
Obtains final velocity = 43.0 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: In a materials laboratory, uniaxial tension applied to a vulcanized neoprene damper rod yields the bilinear stress–strain trace to strain 0.8, with proportional behaviour ending at 0.4.
items.workedSolution: (a) Young's modulus E = 170 / 0.4 = 425 MPa. (b) Energy per unit volume = ½(0.4)(170) + ½(170 + 240)(0.4) = 116 MJ m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates initial gradient σ / ε up to ε = 0.4.
Obtains E = 425 MPa.
Identifies work per unit volume as total area under the σ–ε graph.
Splits area into initial triangle plus upper trapezium.
Obtains 116 MJ m⁻³.

items.stem: Data loggers record the linear momentum of an air-track glider (mass 1.2 kg), which experiences a constant resultant force between t = 2.0 s and t = 5.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Resultant force F = Δp / Δt = (9.6 − 2.4) / (5 − 2) = 2.40 N. (b) Net work W = ΔE_k = (9.6² − 2.4²) / (2 × 1.2) = 36.0 J.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies resultant force as gradient Δp / Δt of the p–t graph.
Obtains F = 2.40 N.
Relates net work to ΔE_k = (p₂² − p₁²) / (2m).
Substitutes p₁ = 2.4 kg m s⁻¹, p₂ = 9.6 kg m s⁻¹, and m = 1.2 kg.
Obtains W = 36.0 J.

items.stem: Engineers monitor a vertical-launch sounding sled for 16.0 s starting from an initial upward velocity of 13.0 m s⁻¹ at t = 0.0 s, obtaining the piecewise acceleration–time graph below.
items.workedSolution: (a) Maximum speed occurs when acceleration crosses zero from positive to negative at t = 10.0 s. (b) Positive area = 35.0 m s⁻¹, giving v_max = 13 + 35.0 = 48.0 m s⁻¹. (c) Negative area magnitude = 12.0 m s⁻¹, so v_final = 48.0 − 12.0 = 36.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: States t = 10.0 s.
Evaluates positive area up to 10 s (35.0 m s⁻¹) and adds u₀ = 13 m s⁻¹.
Obtains v_max = 48.0 m s⁻¹.
Subtracts negative area (12.0 m s⁻¹) from v_max.
Obtains final velocity = 36.0 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: To determine the EMF and internal resistance of a nickel-metal-hydride battery pack, V is graphed against I over the current interval 0.0 A to 5.0 A.
items.workedSolution: (a) Open-circuit intercept gives ε = 25.0 V. (b) Gradient = (10 − 25) / 5 = -3.00 V A⁻¹. (c) Mean terminal p.d. = ½(25 + 10) = 17.5 V.

markScheme.criterion: Reads ε = 25.0 V at I = 0.
Evaluates (10 − 25) / 5 including negative sign.
Obtains -3.00 V A⁻¹.
Uses ½(25 + 10) or area divided by 5 A.
Obtains 17.5 V.

items.stem: During an electrostatics practical with charged metallized spheres in a Coulomb torsion-balance rig, readings of F are plotted versus r⁻² across 0.0 m⁻² to 20.0 m⁻² as shown.
items.workedSolution: (a) At r⁻² = 0, systematic tare offset F₀ = 0.100 N. (b) Gradient = (1.1 − 0.1) / 20 = 0.0500 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Reads intercept F₀ = 0.100 N.
Evaluates ΔF = 1.1 − 0.1 using intercept from (a).
Divides ΔF by 20 m⁻² and states correct unit N m².
Obtains 0.0500 N m².

items.stem: Varying specimen geometry up to L / A = 160.0 m⁻¹, a student obtains the straight-line R versus L / A plot shown for a germanium crystal prism.
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical intercept R₀ = 6.00 Ω. (b) Resistivity ρ = (26 − 6) / 160 = 0.125 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: States R₀ = 6.00 Ω.
Identifies ρ with the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A).
Subtracts R₀ = 6 Ω from 26 Ω before dividing by 160 m⁻¹.
Obtains ρ = 0.125 Ω m.

workingSteps: From R = ρ(L / A) + R₀, ρ equals the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A).

items.stem: The straight-line plot below shows how the terminal potential difference of a silver-oxide instrument battery falls as load current increases from 0.0 A to 4.0 A.
items.workedSolution: (a) Open-circuit intercept gives ε = 13.0 V. (b) Gradient = (7 − 13) / 4 = -1.50 V A⁻¹. (c) Mean terminal p.d. = ½(13 + 7) = 10.0 V.

markScheme.criterion: Reads ε = 13.0 V at I = 0.
Evaluates (7 − 13) / 4 including negative sign.
Obtains -1.50 V A⁻¹.
Uses ½(13 + 7) or area divided by 4 A.
Obtains 10.0 V.

items.stem: Refer to the linearized Coulomb graph of balance reading F against r⁻² (up to 16.0 m⁻²) recorded using charged copper electrodes on a laser-deflection cantilever.
items.workedSolution: (a) At r⁻² = 0, systematic tare offset F₀ = 0.120 N. (b) Gradient = (1.16 − 0.12) / 16 = 0.0650 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Reads intercept F₀ = 0.120 N.
Evaluates ΔF = 1.16 − 0.12 using intercept from (a).
Divides ΔF by 16 m⁻² and states correct unit N m².
Obtains 0.0650 N m².

workingSteps: As r → ∞, r⁻² → 0, where the vertical intercept gives F₀ = 0.120 N.

workingSteps: Read F = 1.16 N at r⁻² = 16 m⁻².

items.stem: Passing a timing marker at t = 0.0 s with speed 9.0 m s⁻¹ upward, a mine hoist cage undergoes positive then negative upward acceleration over 8.0 s as plotted.
items.workedSolution: (a) Maximum speed occurs when acceleration crosses zero from positive to negative at t = 4.00 s. (b) Positive area = 18.0 m s⁻¹, giving v_max = 9 + 18.0 = 27.0 m s⁻¹. (c) Negative area magnitude = 12.0 m s⁻¹, so v_final = 27.0 − 12.0 = 15.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: States t = 4.00 s.
Evaluates positive area up to 4 s (18.0 m s⁻¹) and adds u₀ = 9 m s⁻¹.
Obtains v_max = 27.0 m s⁻¹.
Subtracts negative area (12.0 m s⁻¹) from v_max.
Obtains final velocity = 15.0 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Extensometer and load-cell readings for a synthetic polyurethane tendon cord are converted to tensile stress and strain up to 0.5 (proportional limit 0.25) as graphed.
items.workedSolution: (a) Young's modulus E = 180 / 0.25 = 720 MPa. (b) Energy per unit volume = ½(0.25)(180) + ½(180 + 260)(0.25) = 77.5 MJ m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates initial gradient σ / ε up to ε = 0.25.
Obtains E = 720 MPa.
Identifies work per unit volume as total area under the σ–ε graph.
Splits area into initial triangle plus upper trapezium.
Obtains 77.5 MJ m⁻³.

items.stem: To determine the resistivity ρ of an isotropic graphite heating element despite probe and lead resistance R₀, a student plots total measured resistance R against the ratio L / A from 0.0 m⁻¹ to 400.0 m⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical intercept R₀ = 6.00 Ω. (b) Resistivity ρ = (30 − 6) / 400 = 0.0600 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: States R₀ = 6.00 Ω.
Identifies ρ with the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A).
Subtracts R₀ = 6 Ω from 30 Ω before dividing by 400 m⁻¹.
Obtains ρ = 0.0600 Ω m.

items.stem: The signed downrange acceleration of a railgun armature test sled is plotted from t = 0.0 s to t = 10.0 s; at the start of the recording, its velocity is 8.0 m s⁻¹ downrange.
items.workedSolution: (a) Maximum speed occurs when acceleration crosses zero from positive to negative at t = 5.00 s. (b) Positive area = 28.0 m s⁻¹, giving v_max = 8 + 28.0 = 36.0 m s⁻¹. (c) Negative area magnitude = 16.0 m s⁻¹, so v_final = 36.0 − 16.0 = 20.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: States t = 5.00 s.
Evaluates positive area up to 5 s (28.0 m s⁻¹) and adds u₀ = 8 m s⁻¹.
Obtains v_max = 36.0 m s⁻¹.
Subtracts negative area (16.0 m s⁻¹) from v_max.
Obtains final velocity = 20.0 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: In an experiment to characterize a zinc-carbon dry cell, a variable resistor is adjusted while recording terminal potential difference V and current I from 0.0 A to 5.0 A. The resulting best-fit line is shown.
items.workedSolution: (a) Open-circuit intercept gives ε = 16.0 V. (b) Gradient = (7 − 16) / 5 = -1.80 V A⁻¹. (c) Mean terminal p.d. = ½(16 + 7) = 11.5 V.

markScheme.criterion: Reads ε = 16.0 V at I = 0.
Evaluates (7 − 16) / 5 including negative sign.
Obtains -1.80 V A⁻¹.
Uses ½(16 + 7) or area divided by 5 A.
Obtains 11.5 V.

items.stem: In an experiment verifying Coulomb's inverse-square law using nickel-plated hollow spheres suspended over an analytical balance, total force reading F is plotted against inverse-square separation r⁻² up to 40.0 m⁻², obeying F = k|Q₁Q₂|r⁻² + F₀.
items.workedSolution: (a) At r⁻² = 0, systematic tare offset F₀ = 0.150 N. (b) Gradient = (1.35 − 0.15) / 40 = 0.0300 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Reads intercept F₀ = 0.150 N.
Evaluates ΔF = 1.35 − 0.15 using intercept from (a).
Divides ΔF by 40 m⁻² and states correct unit N m².
Obtains 0.0300 N m².

items.stem: Measured resistance R is plotted against length-to-area ratio L / A up to 250.0 m⁻¹ for a conductive carbon-polymer rod, obeying R = ρ(L / A) + R₀ where R₀ is the constant lead resistance.
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical intercept R₀ = 8.00 Ω. (b) Resistivity ρ = (32 − 8) / 250 = 0.0960 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: States R₀ = 8.00 Ω.
Identifies ρ with the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A).
Subtracts R₀ = 8 Ω from 32 Ω before dividing by 250 m⁻¹.
Obtains ρ = 0.0960 Ω m.

items.stem: A student connects an ammeter, high-impedance voltmeter, and rheostat to a lead-acid laboratory accumulator, obtaining the linear V–I plot over 0.0 A to 2.0 A.
items.workedSolution: (a) Open-circuit intercept gives ε = 10.6 V. (b) Gradient = (5 − 10.6) / 2 = -2.80 V A⁻¹. (c) Mean terminal p.d. = ½(10.6 + 5) = 7.80 V.

markScheme.criterion: Reads ε = 10.6 V at I = 0.
Evaluates (5 − 10.6) / 2 including negative sign.
Obtains -2.80 V A⁻¹.
Uses ½(10.6 + 5) or area divided by 2 A.
Obtains 7.80 V.

items.stem: A 10.0 s accelerometer log is shown for a centrifuge carrier pod, which is already travelling tangentially forward at 13.0 m s⁻¹ when t = 0.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Maximum speed occurs when acceleration crosses zero from positive to negative at t = 5.00 s. (b) Positive area = 24.0 m s⁻¹, giving v_max = 13 + 24.0 = 37.0 m s⁻¹. (c) Negative area magnitude = 14.0 m s⁻¹, so v_final = 37.0 − 14.0 = 23.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: States t = 5.00 s.
Evaluates positive area up to 5 s (24.0 m s⁻¹) and adds u₀ = 13 m s⁻¹.
Obtains v_max = 37.0 m s⁻¹.
Subtracts negative area (14.0 m s⁻¹) from v_max.
Obtains final velocity = 23.0 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: During mechanical characterization of a polypropylene surgical suture, the specimen follows a straight Hookean slope up to strain 0.4 and continues reversibly to strain 0.8.
items.workedSolution: (a) Young's modulus E = 170 / 0.4 = 425 MPa. (b) Energy per unit volume = ½(0.4)(170) + ½(170 + 240)(0.4) = 116 MJ m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates initial gradient σ / ε up to ε = 0.4.
Obtains E = 425 MPa.
Identifies work per unit volume as total area under the σ–ε graph.

items.stem: In an electrical properties lab, resistance readings across an aqueous copper-sulfate capillary cell are linearized against geometric factor L / A up to 500.0 m⁻¹, revealing a non-zero contact offset R₀.
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical intercept R₀ = 12.0 Ω. (b) Resistivity ρ = (51 − 12) / 500 = 0.0780 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: States R₀ = 12.0 Ω.
Identifies ρ with the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A).
Subtracts R₀ = 12 Ω from 51 Ω before dividing by 500 m⁻¹.
Obtains ρ = 0.0780 Ω m.

items.stem: Starting with forward velocity 14.0 m s⁻¹ at t = 0.0 s, an electromagnetic catapult shuttle follows the 12.0 s acceleration–time profile displayed on the axes.
items.workedSolution: (a) Maximum speed occurs when acceleration crosses zero from positive to negative at t = 6.00 s. (b) Positive area = 24.0 m s⁻¹, giving v_max = 14 + 24.0 = 38.0 m s⁻¹. (c) Negative area magnitude = 15.0 m s⁻¹, so v_final = 38.0 − 15.0 = 23.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: States t = 6.00 s.
Evaluates positive area up to 6 s (24.0 m s⁻¹) and adds u₀ = 14 m s⁻¹.
Obtains v_max = 38.0 m s⁻¹.
Subtracts negative area (15.0 m s⁻¹) from v_max.
Obtains final velocity = 23.0 m s⁻¹.

parts.prompt: State the time at which the forward speed is greatest.
workingSteps: Acceleration changes from positive to negative at t = 6.00 s.

parts.prompt: Calculate this maximum speed.
Calculate the velocity at t = 12.0 s.
workingSteps: Magnitude of negative a–t area (6 s to 12 s) = ½(2)(3) + (4)(3) = 15.0 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Terminal voltage V across a portable photovoltaic module under constant irradiance is logged as load current I varies from zero up to 5.0 A, producing the downward straight line below.
items.workedSolution: (a) Open-circuit intercept gives ε = 25.0 V. (b) Gradient = (10 − 25) / 5 = -3.00 V A⁻¹. (c) Mean terminal p.d. = ½(25 + 10) = 17.5 V.

markScheme.criterion: Reads ε = 25.0 V at I = 0.
Evaluates (10 − 25) / 5 including negative sign.
Obtains -3.00 V A⁻¹.
Uses ½(25 + 10) or area divided by 5 A.
Obtains 17.5 V.

items.stem: Because the force sensor has an unzeroed tare reading F₀, a student graphs total force F against r⁻² up to 40.0 m⁻² for isolated brass domes mounted above an electronic microbalance.
items.workedSolution: (a) At r⁻² = 0, systematic tare offset F₀ = 0.200 N. (b) Gradient = (1.6 − 0.2) / 40 = 0.0350 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Reads intercept F₀ = 0.200 N.
Evaluates ΔF = 1.6 − 0.2 using intercept from (a).
Divides ΔF by 40 m⁻² and states correct unit N m².
Obtains 0.0350 N m².

items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical intercept R₀ = 7.00 Ω. (b) Resistivity ρ = (41 − 7) / 250 = 0.136 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: States R₀ = 7.00 Ω.
